theme_description: Conscious recognition of one's thoughts, emotions, and behaviours, driven by a clear sense of purpose and values. It involves a confident understanding of one's strengths and weaknesses, fostering the ability to align actions with goals and a commitment to ongoing self-learning and personal growth.
sub_theme_description: Ability to critically examine and evaluate their own thoughts, behaviours, emotions, strengths, and weaknesses for introspection and self-reflection.

proficiency_levels.label: Recognises own thoughts, emotions, strengths, and weaknesses to align behaviour with professional expectations
proficiency_levels.description:
Identifies personal emotions and thoughts in routine official situations to understand their influence on interactions and maintain professionalism in service delivery. Recognises how reflecting on one’s thoughts, emotions, and behaviour supports self-improvement and builds a respectful team environment and responsive service culture.
Recognises individual strengths and limitations using self-observation or informal feedback, with the intention of performing duties more effectively and meeting service standards.
Seeks and reflects on feedback regarding personal strengths, limitations, and workplace behaviour to make immediate adjustments in line with departmental norms and improve individual task performance.
Recognises emotional reactions to everyday workplace challenges (e.g., task delays, disagreements) to regulate responses and maintain professional conduct. Reflects on induction learnings (e.g., code of conduct, service rules, service values) to align personal behaviour with departmental norms and uphold citizen service expectations through reliable and consistent delivery. I recognise my emotions by reflecting on day-to-day work situations to improve my interactions and carry out responsibilities more effectively.
I act on feedback from supervisors or colleagues by adjusting my behaviour to align with departmental norms and maintain professional conduct.
I track my emotional responses across tasks to build self-awareness.

proficiency_levels.label: Analyses behaviour and adjusts conduct to enhance work performance, interpersonal coordination, and accountability
proficiency_levels.description:
Reflects on recurring emotional patterns (e.g., frustration, defensiveness) during official interactions, such as interdepartmental coordination meetings, to recognise their impact on collaboration and efficiency. Adjusts personal conduct in response to recurring emotional triggers during tasks such as citizen grievance hearings or staff discussions to maintain composure, prevent conflict, and support a timely resolution.
Applies insights from structured feedback mechanisms (e.g., performance reviews, supervisory discussions) to make sustained adjustments in behaviour, strengthen collaboration with colleagues, and improve reliability of task and service delivery.
Applies self-reflection and emotional regulation strategies (e.g., taking pause, reframing perspective) to regulate emotions and maintain professionalism in high-pressure or sensitive tasks, including public-facing responsibilities.
Modifies behavioural responses in line with departmental values and priorities to prevent delays, reduce disruptions, and ensure accountability in service delivery.
Applies self-monitoring tools (e.g., reflection journals, behavioural checklists, etc) to recognise patterns in conduct and identify emotional triggers for consistent workplace effectiveness. Incorporates reflection into work routines (e.g., task debriefs, end-of-day logs) to track behavioural progress, reinforce learning, and strengthen long-term personal growth. I analyse my behaviour by using feedback and self-assessment to strengthen my performance and contribute to smoother coordination within the team.
I manage my emotional responses by applying regulation strategies to stay composed and professional in high-pressure situations.
I adapt my actions by reflecting on past experiences to meet departmental expectations better and support consistent service delivery.

proficiency_levels.label: Exhibits self-awareness and enables structured reflective practices that improve team effectiveness and service outcomes.
proficiency_levels.description:
Leads by example through the consistent use of structured reflection tools (e.g., journaling, post-task reviews) to evaluate personal conduct, decision making, and emotional responses in complex or high-stakes situations, promoting a culture of accountability and professionalism.
Mentors team members to identify emotional and behavioural patterns and apply self-regulation techniques (e.g., pausing before responding, identifying triggers), to reduce conflict, strengthen collaboration, and improve service delivery.
Integrates reflective practices into planning, review, and team learning processes (e.g., staff meetings, feedback sessions, progress reviews, or performance discussions) to encourage professional growth, adaptive performance, and enhance self-awareness.
Institutionalise systems for regular feedback and self-assessment (e.g., 360° feedback, peer reviews, team reflection practices) to promote behavioural improvement, reinforce accountability, and build a culture of openness and continuous learning across the organisation.
Encourages use of reflective tools (e.g., Johari Window, peer reviews, surveys) to uncover blind spots, reinforce empathy, and prevent misuse of authority or bias in administrative decisions. Ensures alignment of individual and team behaviour with departmental mandates, service values, and citizen-centric goals to improve responsiveness, professionalism, and long-term impact. I demonstrate integrity, emotional awareness, and sound judgment by practising structured reflection in complex situations.
I mentor my team to recognise and manage emotional patterns, fostering respectful collaboration and enhancing service delivery.
I institutionalise reflection by embedding tools such as 360° feedback, peer reviews, and reflection checklists in team routines to drive continuous improvement and citizen-centric outcomes.

theme_description: Conscious recognition of one's thoughts, emotions, and behaviours, driven by a clear sense of purpose and values. It involves a confident understanding of one's strengths and weaknesses, fostering the ability to align actions with goals and a commitment to ongoing self-learning and personal growth.
sub_theme_description: Ability to believe in one’s own abilities, judgment, and skills and have positive and realistic self-perception and assurance to tackle challenges. Take calculated risks and persist in the face of setbacks.

proficiency_levels.label: Builds confidence through independent task completion
proficiency_levels.description:
Uses feedback and self-reflection to understand strengths and areas for improvement, and then applies this awareness to complete tasks more effectively, for e.g., improving draft quality after reviewer inputs, contributing more actively in meetings, or refining a checklist before submission. Completes standard tasks by applying templates, peer suggestions, or past experiences, showing growing confidence in routine work. For e.g., preparing file notes or selecting agenda formats using past examples.
Makes routine decisions such as suggesting file routes or revising drafts without waiting for detailed guidance, demonstrating emerging judgment, and willingness to take small steps - for e.g., proposes adjustments in a checklist or drafts notes independently.
Responds constructively to corrections by revising and improving work, and shows persistence in meeting expectations - for e.g., reformatting a returned draft, refining timelines after last-minute changes, or revising a concept note multiple times until accepted.
Stays calm during everyday setbacks such as revisions, delays, or last-minute changes, and stays focused on task completion - for e.g., adjusting a returned draft, updating timelines, or shifting priorities without frustration.
Volunteers for familiar tasks beyond immediate responsibilities, showing belief in their own abilities and willingness to take initiative, for e.g., offering to draft a basic note during internal reviews or compile data for a team report.
Trusts personal judgment in new but simple situations and takes small, calculated steps without always seeking approval. For e.g., chooses to share a draft directly for review instead of waiting for peer validation. Seeks support or alternate approaches when facing initial setbacks, persevering until tasks are completed successfully - for example, adapting a template to meet new requirements or consulting a peer for input on a revised draft. I complete routine tasks with growing independence and take initiative when familiar with the work.
I listen to feedback and make corrections calmly, so my work improves and supports timely decisions.
I speak up when I’m confident, contribute to team discussions, and stay steady when challenges come up.

proficiency_levels.label: Shows confidence through ownership and ideas
proficiency_levels.description:
Completes multi-step assignments independently and adapts methods as needed, showing confidence in one’s ability to deliver reliably - for e.g., drafting inter-ministerial responses, finalising datasets, or preparing presentations for different audiences. Applies sound judgment by selecting and adapting methods, tools, or formats based on what the task or audience requires - for e.g., using a simplified concept note for a district team or adjusting visual layouts for stakeholder briefings.
Contributes insights confidently in team settings by using analytical and communication skills to improve group outputs - for e.g., refining reporting formats, suggesting stronger slide structures, or flagging missing details in a joint presentation.
Evaluates personal strengths and limitations through reflection and feedback, and chooses assignments that build on current skill level - for e.g., leads documentation while observing planning tasks to grow steadily.
Approaches unfamiliar or ambiguous assignments with composure, breaks them into manageable steps, and seeks guidance only when necessary - for e.g., compiling inputs from multiple divisions for a policy brief or synthesising feedback from various departments.
Shares learnings from personal experiences, including past errors, to help team members build confidence and avoid common mistakes - for e.g., explaining how to fix recurring reporting errors or navigate challenging review processes. Expresses well-reasoned views with respect and openness, challenges standard practices with reasoned suggestions, and helps the team improve quality or avoid risks - for e.g., recommending better routing processes, proposing streamlined templates, or suggesting agenda changes for efficiency. I take ownership of new and complex tasks and complete them with confidence.
I share ideas or concerns in team settings and offer solutions when I observe something can be improved.
I learn from past work and feedback to handle challenges better and support others when needed.

proficiency_levels.label: Leads with confidence, judgment, and integrity
proficiency_levels.description:
Leads complex initiatives with assurance by applying prior experience and skills to deliver on strategic objectives, even when navigating ambiguity and institutional complexity - for e.g., overseeing the design and rollout of a flagship programme involving multiple ministries, coordinating cross-sector partnerships, or piloting a multi-state digital platform. Builds confidence in teams by mentoring peers and junior staff using personal lessons from complex or challenging work contexts - for e.g., demonstrating techniques to manage stakeholder pushback, navigate budget constraints, or present high-risk proposals convincingly.
Drives bold, innovative reforms with conviction, justifying proposals through data, pilot learnings, and risk-mitigation strategies even in procedural-heavy environments - for e.g., initiating a digital grievance redressal pilot using AI within legacy systems.
Maintains composure and ensures progress during institutional uncertainty, adapting plans while upholding core delivery goals - for e.g., restructuring implementation plans after funding delays, shifting strategies during leadership transitions, or redistributing resources mid-project.
Fosters a psychologically safe work environment by encouraging open reflection and providing constructive feedback, enabling collective learning from high-pressure or uncertain situations - for e.g., conducting post-meeting debriefs, facilitating team reflection sessions, or sharing lessons learned after setbacks. Adapts leadership approach by recognising personal strengths and limitations, taking responsibility for areas where one adds the most value, and collaborating with others where specialised expertise is needed. For e.g., leads external engagement with district officials while coordinating technical inputs from domain experts. I lead projects with clarity and confidence, even when things are uncertain or complex.
I stay steady during challenges, adapt to plans as needed, and help others feel safe and confident to do their best.
I help my team grow by sharing my experiences and using feedback and data to improve how we work.

theme_description: Conscious recognition of one's thoughts, emotions, and behaviours, driven by a clear sense of purpose and values. It involves a confident understanding of one's strengths and weaknesses, fostering the ability to align actions with goals and a commitment to ongoing self-learning and personal growth.
sub_theme_description: Ability to align their actions, decisions, and goals with a clear sense of purpose or a higher meaning for working towards the goal of greater good of citizens.

proficiency_levels.label: Demonstrates how routine tasks contribute to organisational goals and societal impact
proficiency_levels.description:
Demonstrates how routine tasks (e.g., accurate data entry, timely file movement, systematic record-keeping) contribute to organisational goals and, indirectly, to citizen outcomes. Understands how one’s specific tasks support departmental goals — for example, recognising that processing a benefit application promptly ensures timely assistance, or that updating citizen records accurately enables smoother service delivery.
Follows prescribed processes and timelines with the awareness that reliable and consistent performance contributes to the shared purpose of building trust in public service delivery.
Seeks clarity from supervisors or colleagues to understand how routine tasks create an impact at the citizen level and adjusts actions accordingly.
Reflects regularly on whether their daily work is aligned to organisational goals and makes necessary adjustments to improve contribution to citizen outcomes.
Identifies personal strengths that support purposeful work (e.g., attention to detail, patience in service delivery) and works on weaknesses that may hinder it, such as delays or lack of focus.
Maintains commitment and professionalism in less visible or repetitive tasks by reminding oneself of indirect citizen impact (e.g., accurate data maintenance enabling better targeting of schemes; careful file handling reducing delays).
Records key actions, decisions, and learnings to ensure continuity in their work and to help improve service delivery within their team. Volunteers for tasks that are closely aligned to organisational priorities, even if they require additional effort or learning, to contribute to the larger organisational purpose. I follow processes with the understanding that consistent and accurate work directly builds citizen trust.
I reflect on my daily actions and seek guidance to ensure they contribute to organisational priorities and citizen outcomes.
I identify my strengths and work on weaknesses to align my work better to improve public service delivery.

proficiency_levels.label: Aligns priorities with long-term goals to advance organisational and citizen outcomes
proficiency_levels.description:
Prioritises work based on its potential impact on organisational goals and citizen outcomes (e.g., processing grievances that delay service delivery before routine updates; ensuring field-level data accuracy before reporting progress).
Anticipates challenges in meeting service objectives and modifies actions or timelines to stay aligned with expected citizen outcomes.
Continuously learns new methods or adopts tools that help improve work efficiency and ensure better delivery of citizen-focused outcomes (e.g., using digital dashboards to track progress, integrating GIS tools to improve targeting).
Encourages colleagues to reflect on how their roles contribute to citizen outcomes, promoting shared responsibility for service impact.
Shares specific feedback and examples with supervisors to suggest improvements that directly enhance service delivery for citizens.
Stays motivated during challenging situations by consciously reminding oneself of the long-term citizen benefit of their work, rather than focusing only on immediate pressures.
Balances short-term operational goals with long-term organisational priorities, ensuring immediate tasks do not compromise citizen-focused reforms. Shares documented examples of how purposeful decisions improved service delivery to encourage peers to align their actions similarly. I prioritise work based on its direct impact on citizen service quality and organisational goals to ensure meaningful outcomes.
I adjust my actions and decisions when expected results are not achieved, keeping them aligned with citizen service objectives.
I share feedback to help my team improve processes and stay focused on citizen outcomes.

proficiency_levels.label: Aligns departmental policies with long-term societal outcomes, using technology to improve citizen service delivery
proficiency_levels.description:
Advocates for aligning departmental policies, projects, and resources with measurable citizen outcomes, using evidence from field experiences or service performance data. Guides teams to set clear, measurable goals that are directly linked to organisational priorities and citizen service standards, tracking their progress regularly.
Mentors colleagues to build self-awareness by linking their personal strengths and contributions to the larger organisational mission and public good.
Leads by example by making decisions that prioritise long-term citizen benefits over short-term convenience or personal recognition.
Encourages teams to propose and adopt changes in work practices that align more closely with organisational values and citizen welfare (e.g., revising team priorities based on grievance patterns).
Represents the department in inter-departmental, state, or national forums to share purpose-driven practices and influence policy or process reforms for better citizen outcomes.
Communicates the purpose and expected impact of departmental initiatives clearly to stakeholders to build alignment and ensure team motivation. Recognises and appreciates team members who demonstrate purpose-driven behaviour, reinforcing a culture where individual actions consistently contribute to organisational and citizen priorities. I guide my team to set and achieve goals that align with organisational priorities and lead to measurable improvements in citizen outcomes.
I mentor others to stay motivated by connecting their strengths and daily work to the larger purpose of public good.
I help turn difficult situations into learning and improvement for teams and systems.

theme_description: Conscious recognition of one's thoughts, emotions, and behaviours, driven by a clear sense of purpose and values. It involves a confident understanding of one's strengths and weaknesses, fostering the ability to align actions with goals and a commitment to ongoing self-learning and personal growth.
sub_theme_description: Exhibits a commitment to addressing the Department’s, Ministry’s, or Organisation’s needs now and, in the future, through focusing on learning by identifying one’s own learning needs, setting a learning plan and choosing the appropriate learning resources. Focuses on learning how new and innovative ideas and emerging technologies can be adopted to contribute towards the successful completion of tasks.

proficiency_levels.label: Actively develops own capability to perform current responsibilities effectively
proficiency_levels.description:
Understands the purpose of the M/D/O and how their role contributes to service delivery (for e.g., timely file disposal, clear grievance replies, accurate reporting, etc).
Conducts regular self-assessments of strengths and improvement areas against current role requirements (for e.g., noting & drafting quality, e-Office file movement accuracy, grievance reply clarity, etc).
Identifies some priority areas for improvement that affect quality, timeliness, or compliance in day-to-day work.
Sets short-term learning goals (for e.g., over 2–3 months) linked to work improvement rather than course completion alone.
Uses available learning resources such as iGOT Karmayogi courses, departmental SOPs, circulars, manuals, and peer guidance to address identified gaps.
Seeks constructive feedback from supervisors or experienced colleagues and applies suggestions in subsequent tasks.
Applies new learning in current assignments (for e.g., improves structure of notes, reduces drafting errors, uses checklist before file submission, etc).
Maintains a documented learning log with course completions, reflection notes, and measurable improvements (for e.g., faster disposal, reduced clarifications, etc).
Explores and adopts relevant digital tools or new work methods (for e.g., improved dashboard use, basic AI-assisted drafting, etc) to enhance efficiency in assigned task. I align my improvement efforts with my role and departmental service standards.
I seek feedback and apply changes that improve the quality and timeliness of my work.
I demonstrate measurable improvement in my performance through continuous learning. I align my improvement efforts with my role and departmental service standards.
I seek feedback and apply changes that improve the quality and timeliness of my work.
I demonstrate measurable improvement in my performance through continuous learning.

proficiency_levels.label: Strengthens own expertise while enabling structured team learning to improve delivery standards
proficiency_levels.description:
Reviews team performance indicators (for e.g., CPGRAMS pendency, RTI timelines, audit remarks, dashboard data, etc) to identify capability gaps affecting public service delivery.
Continuously upgrades own knowledge in response to policy changes, new scheme guidelines, or digital system upgrades (for e.g., revised e-Office processes, new MIS dashboards, etc).
Maps team skill requirements against Annual Action Plans and upcoming reforms to anticipate future capability needs.
Facilitates monthly learning huddles and structured After-Action Reviews for key assignments (for e.g., scheme reviews, inspections, dashboard reporting, citizen communications, etc), documents lessons learned, and assigns responsible officers to implement agreed improvements.
Establishes peer review or buddy-check systems to improve drafting quality, compliance accuracy, and data reliability.
Designs a blended team learning plan (for e.g., peer demos, case walkthroughs, supervised practice, etc) that fits work cycles and ensures on-the-job application, so learning does not stay limited to course completion.
Coaches colleagues using structured methods (for e.g., GROW, SMART goals, etc) and tracks practice tasks and feedback in shared trackers to strengthen capability transfer and reduce dependence on one person for critical knowledge.
Tests and evaluates new tools, templates, or digital features (for e.g., upgraded MIS dashboards, automation features, AI-assisted summarisation for internal notes, etc) in low-risk environments, documents outcomes, and scales improvements within the team where beneficial.
Tracks whether learning-driven changes reduce repeat issues, improve turnaround time, or enhance service quality, and reports improvements to supervisors. I continuously upgrade my expertise and adapt to reforms and new systems.
I institutionalise structured team learning through regular reviews and ownership of improvements.
I demonstrate measurable improvements in service delivery linked to learning interventions. I continuously upgrade my expertise and adapt to reforms and new systems.
I institutionalise structured team learning through regular reviews and ownership of improvements.
I demonstrate measurable improvements in service delivery linked to learning interventions.

proficiency_levels.label: Leads personal and institutional learning to build future-ready and high-performing governance systems
proficiency_levels.description:
Continuously updates own knowledge of national priorities, reform agendas, emerging governance practices, and technological advancements relevant to the departmental mandate.
Anticipates future capability requirements based on policy shifts, digital transformation initiatives, demographic changes, and long-term service delivery goals
Evaluates emerging technologies and innovative administrative practices (for e.g., AI-enabled drafting, analytics tools, automation features, etc) to assess relevance and potential public value.
Institutionalises a structured governance model for capacity building and learning (for e.g., defined roles, review cadence, quality standards, etc) and integrates learning records with official systems such as iGOT and HRMS/e-HRMS.
Establishes an M/D/O-wide learning needs assessment approach that uses performance metrics, audit findings, and citizen feedback to prioritise learning where it improves trust, timeliness, and service quality for citizens.
Secures resources and partnerships (for e.g., with CTIs, ATIs, academia, etc) and formalises content curation standards to ensure the learning supply remains relevant, credible, and aligned with real-world needs.
Embeds reflective practice and feedback-seeking into team routines (for e.g., periodic retrospectives, learning reviews in program meetings, coaching expectations for managers, etc) to strengthen learning culture beyond one-off trainings.
Establishes communities of practice across teams, through running knowledge reviews, publishing playbooks and reusable templates, etc to improve transferability and reduce fragmentation across locations.
Publishes periodic capability and service-impact reviews demonstrating how learning investments improve turnaround time, compliance quality, transparency, and citizen trust I proactively upgrade my knowledge and anticipate future capability and technology needs.
I establish structured governance frameworks for responsible and scalable adoption of innovations.
I demonstrate, through measurable evidence, how institutional learning strengthens public service delivery and trust.

theme_description: Recognises one's emotional triggers and controls emotional reactions for retaining professionalism while working under pressure and heightened stress. Shows perseverance, self-control, and professional toughness when facing challenges and recovering from setbacks by adapting attitude and behaviour to meet a particular circumstance or in response to shifting working conditions and dynamics. Shows adaptability in fulfilling a given responsibility, navigating through uncertain situations with limited knowledge or resources.
sub_theme_description: Identifies one’s emotional triggers, regulates emotional responses through self-control, and maintains the dignity of the office and the position.

proficiency_levels.label: Manages personal emotions, and applies basic strategies to stay composed and deliver results despite workplace stressors
proficiency_levels.description:
Recognises personal emotional stress signals triggered by routine public service challenges, such as addressing public grievances or RTI case surges, and initiates basic calming techniques to sustain composure.
Demonstrates self-control during minor stressors (for e.g., managing RTI applications, during feedback, interdepartmental coordination, delays in meetings) and avoids reactive communication.
Applies basic stress reduction practices such as time management, prioritisation, or short breaks to manage daily pressures.
Seeks guidance from seniors or colleagues when overwhelmed, especially during reporting deadlines or last-minute demands.
Utilises basic digital tools (e.g., calendar reminders, task lists, email flags, etc.) to organise workload and manage information, understanding how these aid in personal stress reduction.
Aware of one’s own feelings, strengths, and weaknesses, and their connection to one’s own actions and performance. I maintain punctuality and deliver quality outcomes during high workload periods by managing my time effectively and seeking support when necessary.
I manage my emotions with self-awareness and maintain respectful communication to prevent misunderstandings.
I seek timely guidance from supervisors on managing stress to ensure service standards are upheld.

proficiency_levels.label: Mentors team members in applying stress management techniques, fosters supportive peer environments, and proactively redistributes workloads to balance pressure and maintain service continuity
proficiency_levels.description:
Provides guidance and peer mentoring on stress management during peak administrative periods like election deployments or audit preparations, facilitating workload adjustments and reinforcing team resilience Applies proven stress regulation strategies (e.g., breathing exercises, reframing, digital task delegation, etc.) during fluctuating workloads or stakeholder pressures.
Anticipates team and personal stress triggers during high-pressure periods like elections, inspections, or tight budget cycles, and plans accordingly.
Evaluates the impact of emotional dynamics on team productivity and morale, adjusting leadership or coordination approaches to maintain service quality.
Uses project dashboards, workload monitoring tools (e.g., eOffice MIS, etc.), and regular check-ins to track team stress levels and rebalance work where needed.
Actively manages self-effectiveness by thoroughly understanding one's own responses. I ensure smooth and continuous operations by anticipating stress and proactively redistributing workloads.
I mentor colleagues by offering constructive feedback and emotional support to sustain team effectiveness after stressful events.
I foster a resilient team environment by recognizing early burnout signs, facilitating timely interventions or workload adjustments, and preventing delays in citizen-facing services.

proficiency_levels.label: Builds and sustains systemic stress resilience within the organisation
proficiency_levels.description:
Strengthens organisational stress resilience by integrating wellness and emotional regulation into strategic planning and team operations. Guides adoption of departmental wellness initiatives aligned with DoPT and workplace health guidelines (for e.g., well-being check-ins, SOPs for high-stress events, etc) to proactively mitigate chronic stressors.
Ensures resilience frameworks meet compliance and audit standards (for e.g., audit backlash by CAG/CVC, major scheme rollout, etc.) to reduce institutional risk during oversight.
Develops contingency plans and scheduling during major government scheme rollouts (PMAY, Digital India) to safeguard staff well-being and service quality.
Fosters a psychologically safe work environment promoting ethical leadership, transparency, and collective perseverance.
Advocates for the use of AI and analytics tools to monitor workload imbalance and emotional risk factors in team performance data.
I embed departmental practices with government wellness policies to sustain citizen-centric service quality during crises and prolonged high-pressure events.
I ensure compliance with audit and oversight standards related to staff well-being, reducing institutional risks and enhancing organizational credibility.
I champion transparent communication and ethical leadership during major programs, reinforcing public trust and sustaining staff morale through a culture of resilience

theme_description: Recognises one's emotional triggers and controls emotional reactions for retaining professionalism while working under pressure and heightened stress. Shows perseverance, self-control, and professional toughness when facing challenges and recovering from setbacks by adapting attitude and behaviour to meet a particular circumstance or in response to shifting working conditions and dynamics. Shows adaptability in fulfilling a given responsibility, navigating through uncertain situations with limited knowledge or resources.
sub_theme_description: Exhibits competence, confidence, coping skills, and self-control through awareness and mindfulness of the shared purpose of good governance and maintaining positive relations. Demonstrating professional perseverance by modifying the approach while working under increased pressure.

proficiency_levels.label: Practices foundational emotional regulation, seeks support when needed, follows rules under stress, and adjusts actions
proficiency_levels.description:
Acknowledges personal, emotional, and professional limits in high-pressure situations (e.g., when criticised for delayed responses) and seeks support from colleagues, ensuring task completion in alignment with M/D/O guidelines. Remains constructive in response to setbacks such as changes in project plans, funding delays, etc, by prioritising tasks to maintain progress, ensuring service delivery continuity under constraints.
Adjusts emotions in difficult and uncertain conditions (e.g., technical failures during presentations or last-minute plan changes), demonstrating flexibility by adapting to sudden changes in timelines or resource availability, ensuring outputs are still met under pressure.
Remains patient while seeking information, including situations where standard sources are unavailable, delivering timely support to teams despite challenges.
Recognises frustrations constructively in conflict-prone environments, including team conflicts, preserving positive relations, and contributing to a stable workplace culture within the M/D/O.
Listens actively to others during disagreements or criticism before responding to maintain respectful and professional interactions under pressure.
Accepts and acts upon feedback (e.g., revisions of draft replies) by identifying improvement areas and adjusting processes to support personal and task-level improvement.
Follows rules and procedures (e.g., compliance with data sharing requests) of the M/D/O during periods of ambiguity, ensuring legal and procedural adherence even under stress. I recognise my emotional triggers and manage my reactions during stressful situations by staying calm and mindful.
I stay patient, seek guidance, and adapt my approaches to continue meeting responsibilities and delivering results under pressure.
I listen to others, understand differing views, and implement feedback to improve my work, support positive team dynamics, and uphold the M/D/O’s commitment to good governance.

proficiency_levels.label: Manages personal and team challenges with composure, adapts plans, maintains morale, and encourages others to align with purpose during uncertainty
proficiency_levels.description:
Applies basic stress management techniques such as short breaks or breathing exercises, modelling practical coping strategies, and communicates difficult messages honestly and professionally to maintain trust, strengthen teamwork, and demonstrate commitment to shared goals. Guides the team through stressful times, such as sudden leadership change, by holding regular check-ins, giving clear direction, and encouraging constructive, positive discussions, emotional recovery, and collective perseverance.
Exhibits the ability to recover from setbacks and stressful conditions like limited budgets and strong public feedback, by revisiting goals, staying positive, and suggesting improvements to maintain motivation, keep projects moving, and meet M/D/O goals.
Explains team contributions to senior officials and other key stakeholders concerning overall goals, such as efficient budget use to reinforce shared purpose, strengthen alignment, and build collective resilience to overcome challenges in the M/D/O. Addresses criticism from the media or citizens by using facts and clear rules to maintain accountability and build trust in the M/D/O’s governance. I maintain calm, professional communication and deliver honest messages during challenging situations to build trust, support relationships, and reinforce good governance in the M/D/O.
I guide and support my team through stressful situations by adapting plans, mentoring, and promoting open discussions to sustain morale, encourage learning, and strengthen collective resilience.
I anticipate and respond to challenging situations by suggesting practical solutions and explaining the team's contributions clearly to keep projects on track and achieve shared goals.

proficiency_levels.label: Leads with integrity to uphold and maintain strategic focus despite challenging circumstances
proficiency_levels.description:
Reviews past high-stress incidents with the team to find root causes, makes changes to prevent them from happening again, and sets up clear ways for the team to share concerns, building trust and psychological safety.
Evaluates strategic shifts during adverse periods such as budget cuts or programme realignment, and communicates them honestly to strengthen staff alignment, trust, and resilience under uncertainty.
Provides guidance and reassurance during transitions within the M/D/O, including restructuring or relocation, to instill team confidence and maintain service continuity.
Formulates and leads responses to crises (such as fund withdrawal mid-programme, public scrutiny, and technology failure) and provides clear direction to teams despite external volatility.
Resists pressure to take rushed decisions on politically sensitive matters by ensuring due diligence and consultation before acting to uphold sound governance, while leading unpopular or difficult decisions to balance M/D/O priorities and values.
Advocates for the M/D/O’s policy and program decisions in public forums by presenting evidence and risk analysis with confidence, calmness, and commitment, thereby strengthening institutional credibility.
Synthesises organisational needs and develops resilience strategies ( such as creating stress management SOPs and holding regular well-being check-ins), to build adaptive practices into the culture and strengthen collective competence and commitment to the M/D/O’s shared purpose. Champions an institutional culture grounded in integrity and psychological safety, exemplified by the implementation of open-door leadership, evaluating and reinforcing long-term organisational health and professional perseverance even amidst high-pressure external circumstances. I lead with calmness and confidence, encouraging the team to share openly, fostering a psychologically safe environment that helps the team adapt and overcome challenges together.
I evaluate sensitive and important decisions, including programme closures or crisis responses, and lead evidence-based, transparent communication to uphold organisational integrity and values.
I create and embed sustainable resilience practices and a culture to improve the well-being of my team and uphold commitment to good governance.

theme_description: Recognises one's emotional triggers and controls emotional reactions for retaining professionalism while working under pressure and heightened stress. Shows perseverance, self-control, and professional toughness when facing challenges and recovering from setbacks by adapting attitude and behaviour to meet a particular circumstance or in response to shifting working conditions and dynamics. Shows adaptability in fulfilling a given responsibility, navigating through uncertain situations with limited knowledge or resources.
sub_theme_description: Ability to effectively operate in situations characterised by uncertainty, complexity, and a lack of clear information or direction by adapting quickly to changing circumstances, be they new policy directives, unexpected challenges, or shifts in political priorities.

proficiency_levels.label: Recognises and adapts to ambiguity to deliver assigned tasks without disruption
proficiency_levels.description:
Continues progress despite incomplete clarity by adapting past formats or templates (for e.g., previous year’s report, earlier MoF guidelines, sample note) until updated versions are released.
Surfaces unclear responsibilities or timelines (for e.g., missing deadlines in Excel tracker, undefined section roles in eOffice, etc) and confirms with supervisors before proceeding.
Observes how colleagues adapt to shifting priorities and mirrors their coping strategies (for e.g., escalating delays, splitting tasks, etc).
Coordinates transparently using shared tools (for e.g., Google Sheets, WhatsApp groups, shared procurement tracker, etc) to keep team aligned during delays.
Suggests practical next steps when plans change suddenly, such as proposing rescheduling of trainings or adjusting visit plans when approvals are delayed to maintain citizen service delivery.
Tests small-scale options in uncertain contexts (for e.g., SMS reminders, offline registers, pilot checklists, etc) before formal systems are finalised. Explains how unclear guidance affects workflow (for e.g., repeated circulars, policy overlap, missing delegation note) and suggests ways to clarify. I clarify uncertain instructions early and use available tools or formats to keep work moving.
I stay composed and break problems into small, clear steps when priorities shift.
I document decisions on shared tools and promote team clarity in uncertain situations.

proficiency_levels.label: Enables team alignment and progress amid evolving priorities
proficiency_levels.description:
Reprioritises work based on urgency, citizen impact, or new policy changes (for e.g., reallocating field teams, updating audit focus, revising outreach schedule, etc).
Breaks ambiguous tasks into smaller steps and verifies with peers/supervisors (for e.g., combining overlapping audit reports, aligning MGNREGA and PMAY reporting, etc).
Improves public service delivery by adapting tools or templates from prior experiences, like updating vendor clauses after delays caused by past SLA confusion.
Collates progress from informal or real-time sources (for e.g., WhatsApp updates, district calls, shared MIS, local registers, etc) when formal data is delayed.
Tests responses in low-risk settings under unclear directives - for instance, piloting a revised grievance form in select wards before launching citywide and shares learnings to inform scale-up.
Leads discussions to address policy confusion or shifting timelines, helping the team align interim steps - for example, convening a meeting to clarify spending norms and documenting agreed next actions. Communicates evolving plans and uncertainties early (for e.g., team briefs, email summaries, temporary workflows, etc) to maintain morale and pace. I adjust priorities and coordinate with my team when plans change, to avoid delays and respond to citizens more effectively.
I use pilots and past learnings to refine how my team responds to uncertainty.
I organise scattered information and use tools to spot gaps and guide timely team decisions.

proficiency_levels.label: Leads through uncertainty to achieve long-term goals
proficiency_levels.description:
Balances competing political, administrative, and citizen priorities during ambiguity (for e.g., election codes, budget reallocation, urgent directive, etc) to sustain delivery without diluting policy intent.
Designs decision-support tools (for e.g., triage matrix, escalation flowchart, disaster-response SOP, etc) to guide action when information is limited.
Leads inclusive reform strategies (for e.g., hybrid rollout plan, phased pilot, flexible implementation note, etc) to meet mission goals while ensuring field readiness.
Identifies structural gaps in past crisis responses and recommends system-wide fixes - for example, reviews urban transport delays and proposes cross-department SOP alignment to reduce future ambiguity.
Runs scenario planning with cross-functional teams (for e.g., simulation templates, Excel risk maps, citizen feedback dashboards, etc) to anticipate emerging issues.
Builds team capacity to handle ambiguity by mentoring through tools, reflection sessions, and structured debriefs for example, leads post-crisis reviews to help junior staff shape adaptive strategies.
Institutionalises digital resilience tools (for e.g., live dashboards, IVR trackers, etc) embedding them into routine systems to enable real-time response in future uncertain situations. I balance political, administrative, and citizen priorities to maintain public service delivery under uncertainty.
I create systems, tools, and risk mitigation plans that guide teams during change.
I embed feedback and digital resilience tools so the organisation adapts faster next time.

theme_description: Displays a sense of carefulness and practicality in employing both creative and reflective problem-solving methods. Conducts thorough root-cause analyses and collaborates with experts and stakeholders to generate a range of hypotheses based on historical precedents, data, and reports, with a goal to anticipate potential issues and suggest practical and alternative solutions that are based on insights gained from a comprehensive analysis of all relevant available information.
sub_theme_description: Demonstrates ability to extract key information from data, reports, precedence through thorough examination, scrutiny, and analysis using logic to address issues and problems.

proficiency_levels.label: Gathers, organises, and interprets information to break down issues and plan tasks systematically
proficiency_levels.description:
Maintains attention to detail to obtain, and effectively sift through comprehensive information including reports, briefs, policy papers, data, etc.
Understands policies and standards applicable to the M/D/O and adheres to them in decision making for proposals, schemes, and guidelines.
Collects, analyses and breaks down complex issues into smaller parts for easier analysis from a variety of sources (such as statistical serials, census reports, budget papers, economic surveys, etc).
Checks the source of data, ensures relevance and validity, and formats data accordingly.
Understands the links between situations and given information to draw meaningful information, and address issues and problems. Plans own work thoroughly and meticulously by using planning tools such as work plans, checklists, etc and supports the introduction of better ways of working (for e.g., using softwares such as Trello or Miro to manage work plans).
 I pay close attention to detail while extracting and reviewing information, ensuring accuracy and relevance.
I collect and analyse complex issues from various sources, connecting information to draw meaningful insights and address problems.
I plan and organise my own work, using planning tools and introducing efficient methods to improve workflows.

proficiency_levels.label: Identifies root causes, analyses patterns, and collaborates to develop practical solutions
proficiency_levels.description:
Identifies critical patterns in information and data, to recognise root causes of actions that are not readily apparent for delivery of high standard citizen-centric outcomes (for e.g., identifying cause and effect relationships, etc).
Interprets information to identify discrepancies and inconsistencies to optimize workflows, ensure standards and guidelines are adhered to, tasks are completed, documents are reviewed, and re-work is avoided/minimized.
Transforms self, holds others accountable and monitors quality of work for delivery of high standard outcomes, adherence to policies and procedures, and provision of support/guidance where necessary by paying more attention to detail.
Prepares detailed records of discussions and agreed actions to ensure that information is accurate and prompt follow-up occurs where applicable to develop potential solutions, and identify risks.
Reviews problems and digs deeper by asking questions, examining literature or consulting experts (such as policymakers, academics, civil society members, etc) when not satisfied with the level of detail.
Assesses multiple cause-and-effect relationships in a problem, with the ability to see several potential causes of an event.
Supports in designing solutions that attempt to address the complexities at different levels in a practical manner to assess impact in the short, medium, and long term. Monitors compliance to procedures and regulatory requirements and takes action in case of any deviation with appropriate procedures (such as taking corrective and preventative actions, root cause analysis, Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FEMA), etc.
 I identify and interpret patterns and gaps in information, using root cause analysis to improve processes and public service delivery.
I assess information and design practical solutions collaboratively to address potential challenges and risks.
I comply with policies and apply corrective measures when necessary.

proficiency_levels.label: Synthesises complex data to design strategies, resolve risks, and guide long-term decision making
proficiency_levels.description:
Resolves broader issues about risk and compliance, quality of work, and service delivery to avoid unnecessary risks.
Designs solutions that attempt to address the complexities at different levels in a practical manner to assess impact in the short, medium, and long term.
Oversees systemic spot checks and balances (for e.g., by doing impact assessments, using a matrix analysis, force field analysis, affinity diagrams, etc).
Assesses the level of pressure or influence to apply with respect to each analysis conducted, with relation to the broader context and meeting specific M/D/O goals.
Leads strategy and approach based on a whole systems’ perspective after synthesizing relevant information. Builds consensus among diverse parties/stakeholders by assessing common interests, and taking a long-term view of public good.
 I resolve issues around risk, compliance, and service delivery using sound judgement.
I design practical solutions by considering complexities and assessing short-term and long-term impacts.
I create strategies using a systems-thinking approach, ensuring thorough assessments and balancing stakeholders interests.

theme_description: Displays a sense of carefulness and practicality in employing both creative and reflective problem-solving methods. Conducts thorough root-cause analyses and collaborates with experts and stakeholders to generate a range of hypotheses based on historical precedents, data, and reports, with a goal to anticipate potential issues and suggest practical and alternative solutions that are based on insights gained from a comprehensive analysis of all relevant available information.
sub_theme_description: Displays the quality of thoroughly, meticulously, and accurately examining all aspects of a problem or task, such as document creation to data analysis, budget management, and project implementation by employing a keen eye for detail for their screening and scrutiny using functional expertise and domain credibility.

proficiency_levels.label: Reviews documents carefully, follows protocols, and checks accuracy to ensure error-free work
proficiency_levels.description:
Understands the policies and standards of the M/D/O and adheres to them by referencing official manuals (e.g., Central Secretariat Manual of Office Procedures, DoPT circulars, etc) to ensure that file notings, sanction proposals, and administrative approvals are in line with standard protocols and submission formats.
Pays attention to detail to obtain comprehensive information by carefully reviewing documents, forms, and data entries (e.g., reconciling entries in eHRMS for staff postings), ensuring data completeness and accuracy before forwarding to supervisors for decision-making.
Understands the quality and accuracy of own and others’ work by reviewing completed case files, documents, registers, routine communications, etc in the section by using tools such as checklists, standard operating procedures, and predefined templates while flagging inconsistencies during routine reviews (e.g., by cross-checking progress trackers or pending case registers) to ensure that outputs meet required standards before final submission or circulation.
Displays willingness to consult supervisors and peers to validate the details by checking procedural interpretation while processing RTI responses, drafting replies to audit observations, or clarifying applicable CCS Rules, ensuring accuracy, and avoiding missteps in sensitive communications.
Recognises the significance of confidential information by following data handling protocols such as locking physical files, securing login credentials for portals like eOffice or CSCMS, and using secure communication channels when handling confidential matters like vigilance clearances, pension cases, or cadre transfers.
Identifies basic discrepancies in department budgets or project reports (e.g., mismatches in GeM purchase orders or training budget utilisation reports) and highlights the issue for correction to prevent misreporting or inaccurate submissions.
Follows defined processes for maintaining records and files by labelling physical folders accurately, entering data in movement registers or eOffice systems, and weeding out obsolete files under supervision, contributing to orderly and accessible document management.
Provides information in a timely manner and in a usable format (e.g., forwarding complete case files, reports, or summaries to seniors and other sections), enabling others to act without delay or need for clarification. Learns from mistakes and applies lessons learned by reflecting on feedback received from supervisors, understanding the consequences of errors, and taking corrective action to prevent future oversights. I examine documents, forms, or data carefully to reduce errors and ensure accuracy in my work.
I seek guidance from supervisors and peers to confirm facts or interpretations before making decisions, particularly when tasks have legal or procedural implications.
I handle sensitive information with care by using secure platforms, respecting confidentiality, and ensuring that privacy protocols are followed.

proficiency_levels.label: Ensures accuracy by reviewing work, guiding teams, and resolving recurring errors
proficiency_levels.description:
Holds self and others accountable for producing high-quality, compliant outputs by cross-verifying documents, financial records, and official drafts for factual accuracy, legal soundness, and adherence to departmental norms (e.g., CCS Rules, DoPT circulars), using structured verification tools such as checklists to reduce procedural lapses and fiscal risks.
Conducts root-cause analysis of recurring errors and implements corrective actions to prevent reoccurrence and maintain accuracy in operations.
Demonstrates procedural rigour by systematically tracking task progress, coordinating across teams to avoid duplication or delay, and establishing structured mechanisms (such as file registers, task sheets, etc) to enable visibility into workflows and promote accountability in routine operations in the M/D/O.
Implements internal monitoring systems by reviewing dashboards or registers to identify bottlenecks, flag delays, and verify timely submission of key records (e.g., APARs, RTI reports, training documents), initiating corrective action to ensure administrative discipline.
Defines quality benchmark parameters by defining expected output standards, referencing applicable guidelines, and guiding team efforts to ensure that outputs consistently meet institutional standards.
Reviews and edits outgoing communication such as inter-ministerial letters, sanction memos, draft orders, etc, for completeness, alignment with legal and procedural standards, and internal consistency before escalating for higher-level approvals.
Applies analytical thinking in managing complex cases by evaluating procedural implications (e.g., audit objections, legal notices), documenting decisions with clear rationale, maintaining audit trails, and distilling government circulars and rules into actionable guidance for consistent application in section-level workflows.
Guides staff by mentoring on standard protocols (e.g., leave processing, RTI workflows), identifying recurring errors, and organising knowledge systems, such as digital repositories, circular databases, e-office manuals, or compendia (such as Compendium of DoPT Guidelines or RTI Case Law Compendium) to ensure their capacity building and building long-term institutional memory. I drive quality assurance by applying domain-specific norms, reviewing outputs for accuracy and completeness, while incorporating cross-functional feedback to strengthen documents and processes.
I enhance team effectiveness by validating reports, clarifying gaps, and improving internal tools to strengthen task execution.
I analyse recurring problems by using field data and expert input to guide effective solutions.

proficiency_levels.label: Ensures accuracy by embedding quality systems, mentoring teams, and addressing errors proactively
proficiency_levels.description:
Plans and implements systemic checks and real-time validations by analysing procedural gaps, automating approvals, and using performance data and audit trails (e.g., Aadhaar-linked PDS) to reduce errors, ensure protocol compliance, and enhance efficiency, transparency, and accountability across the M/D/O.
Evaluates the utility and scalability of innovative tools (e.g., blockchain for GST tracking, automated PRAGATI systems) by analysing feasibility, risks, and user feedback.
Leads systemic upgrades data validation and quality control by benchmarking peer institutions to strengthen institutional workflows.
Ensures precision while identifying errors or gaps in critical workflows, ensuring accuracy and reinforcing M/D/O accountability.
Champions the M/D/O’s quality management processes by aligning team practices with institutional quality standards, communicating expectations clearly, and integrating quality management protocols in routine operations.
Mentors staff in advanced verification techniques through feedback-based reviews, recognises diligence in outputs, reinforces adherence to quality benchmarks, and fosters a culture of shared responsibility for procedural accuracy (such as error-free documentation) in routine operations. Steers attention to accuracy in high-stakes legal, financial, and inter-departmental functions by validating critical inputs, identifying errors in outputs, and prioritising tasks that directly influence the strategic goals of the M/D/O. I contribute to structured reviews and spot checks across teams, ensuring standards are upheld and deviations are addressed without delay.
I embed systems for quality control and use cross-departmental feedback to refine M/D/O wide service delivery.
I anticipate risks and quality issues by closely monitoring processes and regulations and propose solutions grounded in scrutiny, real-world insights, and regulatory norms.

theme_description: Displays a sense of carefulness and practicality in employing both creative and reflective problem-solving methods. Conducts thorough root-cause analyses and collaborates with experts and stakeholders to generate a range of hypotheses based on historical precedents, data, and reports, with a goal to anticipate potential issues and suggest practical and alternative solutions that are based on insights gained from a comprehensive analysis of all relevant available information.
sub_theme_description: Recognize one's area of responsibility as a critical component of the larger system of the Government machinery and understand its interrelatedness and interoperability with other areas. This involves perceiving and comprehending complex problems and systems, such as processes and policies, as a whole and in parts simultaneously. It also involves devising strategies that would impact the dynamics of the whole by synthesizing complex problems, creating feedback loops, and comprehending causality.

proficiency_levels.label: Recognises how individual roles, processes, and decisions fit within the broader government system
proficiency_levels.description:
Identifies own role and responsibilities within the larger public administration system by reviewing mandates, SOPs, and reporting structures to understand how individual actions contribute to, or constrain overall outcomes. Recognises key system components (for e.g., policies, processes, actors, and service delivery stages) by mapping basic service delivery processes to understand how work moves across M/D/Os.
Observes interdependencies and connections between functions (for e.g., administrative approvals, file movement, data submissions, and inter-departmental coordination, etc) to recognise how delays or errors in one part of the system affect downstream outcomes.
Explains simple cause-effect linkages (for e.g., delay in file approval leading to delay in fund release) using observable examples.
Reviews available data, reports, and past decisions to identify recurring issues and patterns, enabling understanding of the system’s structures and processes to shape outcomes.
Identifies and articulates recurring systemic constraints (for e.g., overlapping mandates, limited staffing, rigid approval hierarchies, etc) during discussions. Uses prescribed tools, under guidance, to document and visualise system components, linkages, and constraints through simple diagrams or notes, supporting shared understanding within the team. I explain how my work fits into and affects the larger public administrative system.
I identify basic system dependencies that influence service delivery outcomes.
I document system observations to support clearer and more structured problem analysis.

proficiency_levels.label: Analyses system’s behaviours to identify root causes and designs solutions
proficiency_levels.description:
Analyses how policies, processes, stakeholders, incentives, and resources interact across departments by using system-mapping tools (for e.g., stakeholder maps, process flows, causal loop diagrams, etc) to identify structural drivers of service delivery. Differentiates between symptoms and systemic root causes by examining data trends, implementation histories, and stakeholder experiences to balance short-term solutions and long-term impact.
Identifies where rules or incentives unintentionally drive poor practices (for e.g., targets that prioritise speed over quality), and explains how these dynamics cause recurring problems such as superficial compliance, rework, or grievances.
Examines time gaps between decisions and results (for e.g, under Jal Jeevan Mission, recognising that while funds may be issued quickly, household tap connections and water quality improvements take months due to procurement and seasonal constraints) to anticipate why outcomes may appear delayed or uneven across districts.
Assesses the ripple effects of policies beyond their immediate goals, e.g., by increasing inspection frequency may initially improve compliance (first effect), but also increase paperwork and staff workload (second effect), which over time can reduce field presence or slow grievance resolution (third effect), to minimise unintended consequences and implementation risks for the department.
Integrates insights from frontline staff, subject-matter experts, and partners to validate system understanding and test alternative hypotheses about the root causes of performance gaps and implementation challenges within the department.
Designs system-aware interventions (for e.g., process redesign, incentive realignment, coordination mechanisms, etc.) that address root causes rather than isolated outputs. Analyses system performance and implementation data to identify gaps in intervention quality or service consistency, and adjusts actions based on evidence to keep solutions effective and fit for purpose. I analyse system interactions to identify root causes and leverage points.
I design solutions that account for interdependencies and minimise unintended consequences.
I quality check and adapt interventions based on feedback and observed system responses to support sustained improvement.

proficiency_levels.label: Anticipates systemic risks and shapes reforms that strengthen long-term institutional resilience
proficiency_levels.description:
Synthesises insights across policies, institutions, and socio-economic contexts by integrating data, system maps, and implementation evidence to understand government systems as a whole rather than in silos.
Anticipates long-term and system-wide consequences of policy or programmatic decisions by analysing feedback loops, delays, behavioural responses, etc to support proactive and informed decision making.
Identifies and acts on critical levers within the system where targeted policy, process, or incentive changes can shift overall behaviour and performance at scale (for e.g., redefining approval authorities, resetting performance metrics used in senior reviews, altering funding and accountability mechanisms, etc) to deliver outsized impact with existing resources.
Designs strategic system-level interventions (for e.g., amending rules of business or delegation orders, linking appraisals to programme outcomes rather than activity counts, etc) that influence underlying dynamics rather than surface-level outcomes.
Uses scenario planning, policy simulations, or system modelling techniques to evaluate long-term risks and resilience under varying conditions.
Translates complex system analysis into clear strategic options, scenarios, and recommendations to inform policy and institutional reform. Builds individual and team capacity to apply systems thinking, while establishing feedback and learning mechanisms to enable continuous monitoring and course correction. I translate system-level insights into strategic policy and institutional reform recommendations.
I design and lead interventions that improve system-wide performance and resilience.
I build systems thinking capability within teams to sustain long-term improvements.

theme_description: Exhibits the ability to speak, read, and interpret official communications such as English/Hindi/State-specific in respect to their context, message, and intent. Displays positive non-verbal cues, actively practices attentive listening, endeavours to understand the viewpoints of others, and responds respectfully and humbly. Presents information with conviction, fluency, rationality, and persuasion while using communication techniques tailored to the audience.
sub_theme_description: Demonstrates the capacity to pay close attention to what is being said and to interpret the spirit and intent of the speaker from other cues such as body language and facial expressions.

proficiency_levels.label: Demonstrates active listening to recognise cues and ensure respectful and attentive communication
proficiency_levels.description:
Follows a structured approach to listening (such as probing, clarifying questions, etc.) by maintaining eye contact, nodding, and using open body language, ensuring trust and openness. Describes key points in the speaker’s message in their own words (paraphrasing) to ensure clarity and shared understanding of the message.
Practices attentive listening by recognising and acknowledging others’ emotions through verbal and non-verbal cues (e.g., tone, facial expressions) to understand the speaker’s emotions and intent, ensuring a respectful response,
Asks clarifying questions politely when content is unclear (e.g., about the subject, topic, key points, or intended output), while avoiding leading or biased questions to reduce misinterpretation and improve accuracy in understanding.
Listens with openness to diverse viewpoints, withholding immediate judgment to understand the complete context before responding, thereby fostering inclusive, well-informed communication within the M/D/O.
Records key points from discussions, meetings, or instructions (e.g., file notes, minutes) to support accurate follow-up and information retention. Listens attentively to all participants, including seniors, peers, and citizens, to ensure balanced understanding and inclusive communication amongst the teams. I pay full attention and avoid interruptions, so colleagues and citizens feel heard and respected.
I observe verbal and non-verbal cues to understand colleagues’ intent and ensure respectful, clear communication within the M/D/O .
I ask clarifying questions and paraphrase key points to avoid misunderstandings and support accurate information sharing in the M/D/O.

proficiency_levels.label: Applies active listening techniques to promote clear, empathetic, and collaborative communication within the team
proficiency_levels.description:
Applies active listening techniques by using a mix of open and probing questions, while analysing non-verbal cues such as open posture and eye contact, to support collaborative problem solving in team discussions Implements reflective listening by mirroring the speaker’s emotions and verifying understanding (e.g., “It sounds like you’re feeling stuck”), promoting empathy, trust, and effective communication both upward and downward.
Explains complex messages simply to others by summarising key themes and discussion points in accessible language, avoiding jargon or assumptions about prior knowledge, and adapting communication to diverse linguistic and cultural contexts to ensure inclusivity and understanding.
Avoids making premature judgments by consciously avoiding assumptions or personal biases during the conversation to enable openness and fairness.
Monitors and adapts responses (e.g., slowing pace, offering reassurance) in real time to maintain a respectful and responsive environment by analysing verbal and non-verbal cues and applying a mix of questioning techniques.
Creates psychologically safe spaces through consistent demonstration of confidentiality and setting personal boundaries (e.g., not interrupting, respecting differing views) to encourage honest and open dialogue. Identifies and addresses potential communication barriers such as assumed tone in written messages by clarifying intent explicitly (e.g., 'Just to be clear, I mean this supportively…'), and analyses non-verbal cues (e.g., hesitation, withdrawal) to surface unspoken concerns or emotions, creating space for underlying issues to be acknowledged and reducing the risk of conflict. I apply reflective listening techniques and adapt my communication style to build empathy, trust, and encourage open dialogue within the M/D/O.
I recognise and address unspoken emotions or concerns by creating safe spaces and demonstrating confidentiality to support open and honest conversations within the M/D/O.
I listen objectively to diverse perspectives and summarise discussions clearly to confirm mutual understanding and ensure aligned decision-making within the M/D/O.

proficiency_levels.label: Promotes active listening to manage complex discussions and strengthen respectful communication within the M/D/O
proficiency_levels.description:
Synthesises complex information from multiple speakers into clear, actionable summaries to be shared with key stakeholders, ensuring shared understanding and informed decisions within the M/D/O. Models empathetic and attentive listening by balancing compassion, silence, and clear feedback, using techniques like paraphrasing and withholding judgment to understand others' perspectives, build trust, and set a standard for respectful communication.
Institutionalises team communication norms that prioritise active listening (e.g., structured feedback sessions, dedicated reflection time) to champion continuous active listening practices, embedding listening as a core organisational value within the M/D/O.
Advises on conflict resolution by using reflective listening and clarifying techniques to address misunderstandings, reduce interpersonal tension, and enable harmonious working relationships
Evaluates communication dynamics in teams, identifying patterns of misunderstanding (e.g., frequent interruptions) and mentors teams to use advanced techniques like reframing and inclusive dialogue strategies, building a collective culture of empathetic listening within the M/D/O.
Leverage active listening as a strategic tool in negotiations, mediations, and stakeholder forums to align diverse perspectives, build shared understanding, and facilitate consensus-driven outcomes. Anticipates potential barriers (e.g., stress, cultural differences, distractions) to active listening by developing tailored strategies (e.g., extra clarification steps, adapted body language), ensuring effective communication across diverse contexts. I model empathetic, non-judgmental listening in important settings to set a standard for respectful, effective communication in the M/D/O.
I mentor teams to use active listening techniques to reduce conflict and support collaborative problem-solving.
I embed practices that ensure active, inclusive listening into our M/D/O’s culture to foster informed decision-making.

theme_description: Exhibits the ability to speak, read, and interpret official communications such as English/Hindi/State-specific in respect to their context, message, and intent. Displays positive non-verbal cues, actively practices attentive listening, endeavours to understand the viewpoints of others, and responds respectfully and humbly. Presents information with conviction, fluency, rationality, and persuasion while using communication techniques tailored to the audience.
sub_theme_description: Exhibits elevated reading skills, possesses a firm linguistic command, and knowledge. Demonstrates the ability to absorb information, understand it, and integrate it with existing knowledge.

proficiency_levels.label: Demonstrate reading comprehension and linguistic command to interpret and apply information
proficiency_levels.description:
Understands official documents (Office Memoranda, circulars, Gazette notifications, scheme guidelines, CCS Rules extracts, SOPs) carefully to understand explicit instructions and timelines. Recognises inconsistencies between English, Hindi, and State-language versions of official communications and seeks clarification where meaning diverges.
Identifies and synthesises key information such as dates, authorities, conditions, eligibility criteria, and compliance requirements from written communications.
Follows written directions accurately in routine tasks such as file noting, draft preparation, compliance reporting, or data submission.
Recognises standard government terminology (for e.g., “competent authority,” “with immediate effect,” “subject to approval,” etc) and applies it correctly with guidance.
Uses basic comprehension strategies such as skimming for structure, scanning for deadlines, and identifying main points in notes and memos.
Understands simple tables, annexures, dashboards, and non-continuous texts linked to official communication.
Connects new written instructions to previously explained procedures to avoid repetitive clarification. Seeks clarification respectfully when written communication is unclear rather than making assumptions. I accurately read and follow official documents to complete tasks correctly and on time.
I identify key instructions, conditions, and deadlines from written communications.
I apply basic comprehension techniques to understand routine official texts.

proficiency_levels.label: Interprets and synthesises official communications into actionable insights for effective implementation
proficiency_levels.description:
Interprets the meaning and implications of government orders, cabinet decisions, and policy circulars with clarity, translating them into actionable instructions for effective implementation at departmental or field levels.
Handle increasing complexity, technicality, and multimodality of texts through skimming for structure, scanning for key details, and interpreting information across multiple formats such as reports, data tables, and digital interfaces.
Analyses information across multiple documents (for e.g., guidelines, amendments, clarifications, audit notes, etc) to identify alignments, inconsistencies, or policy shifts.
Interprets multimodal information (for e.g., data tables, financial statements, performance dashboards, digital interfaces) and evaluates its implications for policy objectives and programme implementation.
Leverages comprehension skills to prepare explanatory summaries, background notes, or clarifications that accurately reflect source documents and support informed review by superiors.
Extracts operational requirements, constraints, and dependencies from lengthy communications to inform implementation planning. Evaluates practical implications of written instructions for different stakeholders (for e.g., Head Office, State units, field offices) and clarifies who must act, by when, and under what conditions. I interpret official communications to translate them into clear and actionable instructions.
I synthesise information across documents to support accurate and coherent implementation.
I identify ambiguities and prevent misinterpretation through careful analysis.

proficiency_levels.label: Analyses complex communications to guide strategic decisions
proficiency_levels.description:
Distils dense, technical, or politically sensitive documents (for e.g., Cabinet notes, judicial orders, audit reports, parliamentary references, etc) to surface intent, risks, and trade-offs.
Interprets communications in light of constitutional provisions, statutory frameworks, delegated legislation, and judicial precedents to prevent procedural or legal exposure.
Synthesises information across time (past precedents), institutions (multiple M/D/Os), and formats (orders, notes, dashboards, audit reports) to construct an authoritative understanding of issues.
Detects ambiguous phrasing, conditional language, or inconsistent instructions in official texts and resolves interpretive gaps through careful analysis.
Establishes logical linkages between current communications and prior Cabinet approvals, CAG observations, parliamentary assurances, or policy commitments.
Frames structured analytical briefs that enable leadership to take timely, informed, and legally sound decisions.
Anticipates reputational, operational, or audit consequences arising from misinterpretation of official communications. Guides teams in advanced reading practices, including distinguishing policy intent from procedural instruction and interpreting layered or conditional clauses. I distil complex policy communications into structured analyses for decision making.
