I identify legal, procedural, and governance risks embedded in written texts.
I ensure interpretations are consistent, defensible, and aligned with institutional mandates.

theme_description: Exhibits the ability to speak, read, and interpret official communications such as English/Hindi/State-specific in respect to their context, message, and intent. Displays positive non-verbal cues, actively practices attentive listening, endeavours to understand the viewpoints of others, and responds respectfully and humbly. Presents information with conviction, fluency, rationality, and persuasion while using communication techniques tailored to the audience.
sub_theme_description: Demonstrates ability to articulate thoughts and express/present ideas clearly and effectively using oral, non-verbal communication skills, aiming to inform, instruct, or persuade the audience/ stakeholders, and augments credibility of the position and the office.

proficiency_levels.label: Understands and communicates ideas clearly and listens attentively to support accurate understanding and respectful interaction in the office
proficiency_levels.description:
Expresses ideas, instructions, or information verbally in a clear and structured manner, ensuring the message is easily understood by the immediate audience/stakeholders. Uses appropriate tone, pace, and volume while speaking to convey professionalism and avoid misinterpretation of presented ideas.
Demonstrates positive non-verbal cues such as eye contact, attentive posture, and controlled gestures to reinforce spoken communication.
Listens actively to others by allowing them to complete their statements and by focusing on the content and intent of the message.
Shows ability to describe basic official communications (oral instructions, briefings, or discussions) accurately and seeks clarification when meaning is unclear.
Responds to questions or instructions respectfully by acknowledging inputs from peers, seniors, or stakeholders, to ensure mutual understanding and maintain professional working relationships.
Adapts language choice (English/Hindi/State language) at a basic level to suit the communication context and audience, so that messages are clearly understood. Demonstrates openness to feedback on communication style and makes conscious efforts to improve clarity and delivery to strengthen communication effectiveness and reduce misinterpretation in routine interactions. I articulate my ideas clearly and respectfully in routine interactions, ensuring my message is understood and reflects the professionalism of the office.
I listen attentively and respond appropriately to instructions and inputs, demonstrating understanding of intent and maintaining constructive communication.
I use appropriate verbal and non-verbal cues to reinforce my message and support a clear, effective understanding among others.

proficiency_levels.label: Adapts communication style to inform, guide, and influence others while maintaining credibility and mutual respect.
proficiency_levels.description:
Adapts verbal communication style (such as using formal language in official meetings, simplifying explanations during team discussions, or adopting a measured tone in stakeholder interactions) based on audience, purpose, and setting to ensure clarity and relevance of the message. Presents information in a clear, logical, and confident manner during meetings, reviews, or discussions to inform, guide, or influence team members and stakeholders, while reinforcing the credibility of the position and the office.
Applies persuasive communication techniques ( such as framing messages around shared objectives, using relevant examples or evidence, and emphasising expected outcomes) by structuring arguments with rationale, examples, and emphasis on outcomes.
Demonstrates controlled and consistent non-verbal behavior (such as maintaining appropriate eye contact, a composed posture, and a steady tone) to reinforce confidence, authority, and approachability during interactions.
Interprets nuanced verbal and non-verbal cues (such as hesitation, tone shifts, or body language) during discussions to understand underlying concerns, differing viewpoints, or emerging resistance.
Responds constructively to differing opinions by acknowledging others’ perspectives, clarifying intent with calm explanation, and maintaining a respectful tone to prevent defensiveness or escalation.
Facilitates productive discussions by encouraging balanced participation, summarising key points or viewpoints, and steering conversations toward a shared understanding. Refines communication approach based on feedback and observed audience response to improve clarity, influence, and overall communication effectiveness. I adapt my verbal tone, language, and non-verbal cues to suit different audiences and contexts, ensuring my message is appropriately conveyed.
I present ideas logically and with conviction, using clear reasoning and respectful communication to inform or persuade others while acknowledging differing viewpoints.
I contribute to effective discussions by expressing my views clearly, listening attentively to others, and reinforcing shared understanding through appropriate verbal and non-verbal communication.

proficiency_levels.label: Uses fluent and persuasive communication (verbal and non-verbal) to represent the office effectively and strengthen institutional credibility
proficiency_levels.description:
Articulates complex or sensitive issues in a balanced and persuasive manner, ensuring that intent, rationale, and implications are clearly understood by the team/department.
Demonstrates strong command over verbal and non-verbal communication to reinforce authority, trust, and professionalism in critical as well as routine interactions.
Interprets subtle verbal and non-verbal signals during discussions or negotiations to anticipate concerns and respond strategically.
Maintains dignity and neutrality of the office by responding calmly and respectfully under pressure or disagreement.
Influences service delivery outcomes by framing messages around shared objectives, public interest, and institutional priorities.
Guides teams in improving their communication effectiveness by modelling appropriate behaviours and offering constructive feedback.
Represents the office or department in formal forums, meetings, or stakeholder interactions by communicating with clarity, conviction, and composure. Strengthens institutional credibility by ensuring communication reflects consistency, confidence, and alignment with organisational values. I represent my office in formal interactions by articulating positions clearly and confidently, using appropriate verbal and non-verbal communication to reinforce the credibility of the office.
I influence understanding and outcomes by presenting ideas with conviction and clear reasoning, and by using respectful, persuasive communication tailored to the audience.
I uphold the dignity and authority of the institution through composed verbal expression and controlled non-verbal conduct, particularly in sensitive situations.

theme_description: Exhibits the ability to speak, read, and interpret official communications such as English/Hindi/State-specific in respect to their context, message, and intent. Presents information with conviction, fluency, rationality, and persuasion while using communication techniques tailored to the audience.

Uses tables, charts, and infographics created using software such as Microsoft Office, Google Suite, and Canva, among others to present complex data while following the organisational communication guidelines. Applies basic storytelling techniques to create a natural flow in presentations, ensuring that ideas are connected and easy to follow.
 I summarise key facts and data from sources such as ministerial or program guidelines, reports, and circulars among others to answer key questions like What, Why, How, and When, ensuring clarity and supporting informed decision-making.

proficiency_levels.label: Designs and delivers audience focused presentations that facilitate dialogue and support informed decision making

Conducts root cause analysis or problem identification to define the objective of the presentation, ensuring the content is relevant to the audience’s needs and purpose.
Facilitates multi-stakeholder discussions, meetings and workshops, among others using techniques such as Think-Pair-Share, World Café Method, Fishbowl Discussions, and Affinity Mapping to foster dialogue, enhance cross-departmental collaboration, engage audiences, and solicit feedback.
Engages the audience using non-verbal cues and active listening skills, responding respectfully to queries and adapting based on audience feedback.
Ensures presentations are well-structured, answering key questions like What, Why, How, and When, with clear messaging suited to the audience’s needs and purpose.
Creates communication guidelines for the ministry to ensure consistency in government presentations, reports, and official communication.

Explores emerging technologies such as AI-powered analytics, translation tools, and cloud collaboration tools, among others to enhance the delivery of presentations, making them more impactful, accessible, and engaging for diverse audiences.
 I conduct root cause analysis to identify the objective of the presentation, ensuring content is relevant to the audience’s needs and purpose in decision-making.
I facilitate using interactive techniques such as Think-Pair-Share and World Café to foster dialogue, enhance cross-departmental collaboration, engage audiences, and solicit feedback.
Adapts delivery using active listening, non-verbal cues, and responsive engagement.

proficiency_levels.label: Communicates complex programme and policy messages with clarity and coherence, shaping understanding and alignment across stakeholders
proficiency_levels.description:
Presents policy directives at national and international forums, ensuring alignment with the ministry’s vision and long-term goals while advocating for national priorities like Viksit Bharat 2047, Digital India, and Atmanirbhar Bharat to foster collaboration, build consensus, and drive collective commitment toward these initiatives.
Encourages the use of feedback mechanisms by leveraging emerging technologies to enhance presentation delivery by capturing audience sentiment and providing facilitators with insights based on audiences’s non-verbal cues.
Encourages training sessions and workshops to build the capacity of junior officials in presentation skills.
Advocates the use of storytelling frameworks such as Situation-Complication-Resolution (SCR) and, Problem-Agitate-Solution (PAS), among others in cross-departmental collaboration, public-facing presentations, press briefings, and other such engagements to ensure messaging is aligned with audiences' needs and purpose. Ensures that the ministry’s communication guidelines are followed across engagements to maintain consistency, clarity, and alignment with its objectives.
 I present policy directives at national and international forums, aligning with the ministry’s vision and long-term goals while advocating for national priorities to foster collaboration, build consensus and drive collective commitment toward these initiatives.
I advocate using storytelling frameworks in cross-departmental collaboration, public presentations, and press briefings to ensure clear, audience-focused messaging.

theme_description: Demonstrates an intense motivation to set goals and be responsible for their achievement while striving for quality excellence. Possesses the capacity to identify problems and gaps during service delivery and to proactively analyse and assess different options to ensure the best result. Drives systemic changes to increase effectiveness and efficiency in line with future needs.
sub_theme_description: Displays an underlying desire to be thorough and accurate when determining clear, challenging, & SMART (specific, measurable, achievable, relevant & time-bound) objectives or targets to guide actions as per set procedures, rules & guidelines.

proficiency_levels.label: Understands the purpose of goal setting in public service and drafts basic SMART goals for own team under guidance
proficiency_levels.description:
Explains the purpose of goal setting in government work, including how clear goals support accountability, service delivery, and outcome orientation.
Describes the components of SMART (specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time bound) goals and distinguishes between activities, outputs, and outcomes using simple examples from own section/unit (for e.g., recognising that logging and examining grievances in CPGRAMS is an activity, disposal of grievances within Citizen Charter timelines is an output, and reduction in repeat grievances is an outcome).
Drafts SMART objectives for M/D/O’s services or schemes to create a clear work plan that can be monitored.
Identifies relevant historical data sources for goal setting (e.g., CPGRAMS pendency reports, Citizen Charter timelines, PFMS expenditure summaries, e-Office disposal data, etc.).
Records baseline data source, reference period, and data owner in the prescribed format to support their tracking and fair goal setting.
Lists possible indicators linked to each objective with supervisor guidance, ensuring alignment to scheme or service intent (for e.g., for a grievance redressal objective, identifying indicators such as number of grievances disposed within Citizen Charter timelines, monthly pendency in CPGRAMS, etc).
Documents Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) definitions (unit, frequency, data source) in a simple KPI register ensuring progress can be tracked consistently over time.
Identifies linkages between unit-level objectives and higher-level outputs/outcomes (for e.g., Results Framework Document, Outcome Budget) using a basic goal-to-indicator mapping table.
Seeks clarification from supervisor when objectives, targets, or indicators are unclear or conflicting, instead of proceeding with ambiguous goals. Publishes approved goals and due dates on the unit intranet/notice board in simple language and records staff acknowledgement to build their shared understanding. I understand what makes a goal SMART and how activities, outputs, and outcomes differ in my M/D/O’s work.
I draft basic SMART goals for my team using approved templates and baseline data, with supervisor guidance.
I maintain clear records of goals, baselines, indicators, and approvals, and communicate timelines so responsibilities are understood.

proficiency_levels.label: Cascades goals across teams or sections, integrates dependencies, and uses data-driven reviews to correct course and deliver measurable outcomes
proficiency_levels.description:
Translates departmental priorities into section-level Objectives and Key Results (OKRs) with quarterly targets, ensuring each objective has 2-4 key results with tagged owners to enable accountability at scale. Assesses the feasibility of targets by considering field constraints, resource availability, and past performance trends before finalising goals.
Builds and maintains a KPI data dictionary (e.g., definition, formula, numerator/denominator, exclusions, etc.) to standardise measurement across teams.
Validates data quality by conducting periodic spot checks of records drawn from systems such as PFMS, ServicePlus, CPGRAMS, or e-Office.
Aligns goals with the OOMF , RFD , SDG/National Indicator Framework, etc., recording mappings to support consolidated reporting and benchmarking.
Reviews monthly performance variance using MIS reports, dashboards, or simple charts to identify emerging risks and slippages.
Documents root causes of underperformance using structured methods (for e.g., 5-Whys, Fishbone, etc) and assigns corrective actions with clear timelines.
Defines and monitors leading indicators (for e.g., average turnaround time, first-time-right rate, grievance rate per 1,000 cases, etc) to enable proactive intervention.
Formalises inter-sectional or inter-departmental dependencies for shared goals through SLAs or agreed action notes, tracking adherence and escalates delays through prescribed channels.
Deploys a role-based dashboard (for e.g., Power BI, DIKSHA Analytics, etc) with weekly auto‑refresh. Conducts structured capacity-building sessions for team members on SMART goals, OKRs, and basic data use, using approved departmental materials or guidelines. I cascade goals into clear, owned targets and track progress through regular data-based reviews.
I identify root causes of variance and ensure corrective actions are followed through.
I coordinate across teams so shared goals progress without avoidable delays.

proficiency_levels.label: Standardises M/D/O goal setting practices linked to outcomes, accountability, and service improvement
proficiency_levels.description:
Establishes an M/D/O wide goal setting policy and playbook (for e.g., SMART, OKR, OOMF mapping, templates, governance, etc.) to ensure consistency across units.
Leads the articulation of M/D/O outcome priorities by aligning cross-scheme goals (for e.g., major Central Sector/CSS schemes) to the SDGs and the National Indicator Framework.
Guides senior officers and unit heads in aligning annual goals with departmental priorities, budget allocations, and expected service outcomes.
Supports the consolidation of departmental performance information into a common MIS or dashboard aligned with Outcome Budget and OOMF requirements.
Uses performance evidence to recommend re-prioritisation, pruning, or redesign of targets that are no longer relevant or impactful.
Embeds structured risk identification for key departmental goals and ensures mitigation actions are built into annual action plans.
Designs the incentive and consequence mechanisms (e.g., performance agreements, recognition, targeted support, etc.) tied to outcomes to reinforce desired behaviours.
Promotes shared ownership of outcomes across teams, reducing siloed goal setting and encouraging collective accountability.
Ensures that findings from internal reviews, audits, evaluations, or CAG observations are reflected in subsequent goal setting and target revision cycles. Encourages transparent communication of departmental priorities and results to strengthen credibility and trust. I standardise goal setting practices across the department and link them clearly to outcomes.
I use performance evidence to guide priorities, reviews, and course correction.

I deliver high-quality work on time and follow procedures

proficiency_levels.label: Coordinates team efforts, monitors performance, and implements processes to ensure timely and efficient public service delivery

Develops clear guidelines for task execution related to public jurisdiction and ensures compliance with regulations (e.g. - municipal laws, RTI compliances, legal compliances).

Monitors team progress as per the department goals by conducting review meetings (for e.g., progress meetings with on-ground staff), identifies deviations (for e.g., underutilised funds, gaps in data) and implements corrective actions (for e.g., assessing priorities and reassigning responsibilities) and establishing best practices to improve.

Establishing measurable goals and milestones for teams (such as payment disbursal timelines, incentive releases) ensuring alignment with program objectives and departmental goals. Monitoring and ensuring compliance with quality assurance standards, by engaging with concerned stakeholders (for e.g., peers in line departments, elected representatives, etc). I coordinate team efforts and delegate tasks effectively to achieve goals.
I monitor performance, provide constructive feedback, and address deviations
I promote a culture of accountability and continuous improvement within the team.

proficiency_levels.description:

proficiency_levels.label: Delivers reliable outputs by following SOPs and applying basic quality checks
proficiency_levels.description:
Follows approved SOPs, templates, manuals, and checklists (for e.g., CSMOP , GFR references, Citizen Charter timelines, etc) while drafting notes, letters, or reports, ensuring completeness and accuracy before submission.
Applies a structured 3-point self-check (for e.g., content accuracy, procedural compliance, approval chain, etc) before routing files in eOffice.
Ensures proper documentation and traceability by uploading supporting documents, approvals, and references in designated eOffice folders and maintaining audit-ready records as per record retention schedules.
Cross-verifies key figures and beneficiary details against official records (for e.g., scheme guidelines, sanction orders, PFMS entries, MIS dashboards, registers, etc) before forwarding files.
Flags discrepancies, missing documents, or timeline risks to supervisors early, referencing agreed quality standards, grievance timelines, RTI deadlines, or Citizen Charter commitments where applicable.
Performs basic quality validation of data entries in PFMS, MIS, or dashboards by checking totals, dates, beneficiary categories, etc against source documents.
Ensures clarity and readability in written communication by checking formatting, references, annexures, and citations before submission. Demonstrates personal accountability for error-free work rather than relying solely on supervisory correction. I submit accurate and complete work by self checking before approval.
I maintain proper documentation and traceable records in eOffice and related systems.
I proactively flag errors or delays to prevent quality lapses.

proficiency_levels.label: Strengthens the teams quality systems by identifying root causes of errors and embedding structured quality assurance practices
proficiency_levels.description:
Develops quality plans and templates for assignments by defining acceptance criteria, timelines, compliance requirements, and review responsibilities to reduce variability and rework.
Conducts structured QA reviews at draft and final stages using checklists aligned to SOPs, GFR provisions, RTI norms, or scheme guidelines.
Analyses recurring errors using structured problem-solving tools (for e.g., 5 Whys, Fishbone analysis, etc) and implements CAPA with defined owners and timelines.
Reinforces clarity on quality expectations at the start of assignments and monitors adherence during implementation.
Coordinates with Accounts, IT/MIS, or Establishment sections to introduce validation checks such as mandatory fields, dropdown controls, or automated alerts in digital systems.
Monitors team feedback from citizens or stakeholders and uses that to propose small process improvements (for e.g., reducing duplicate data entry in scheme application).
Conducts periodic peer-learning reviews where recent file errors are analysed and preventive measures agreed upon. Builds salience around departmental QA/QC guidelines by orienting team members to quality standards at task initiation and reinforcing compliance through regular review, reminders, and performance discussions. I improve team accuracy and compliance by applying structured QA reviews and checklists.
I identify root causes of recurring errors and implement preventive fixes.
I strengthen quality control using data, dashboards, and cross-functional collaboration.

proficiency_levels.label: Institutionalises systemic quality controls and transparency mechanisms to drive continuous improvement
proficiency_levels.description:
Designs and institutionalises an M/D/O wide Quality Management Framework aligned to Citizen Charters, Sevottam principles, audit standards, and national programme guidelines.
Establishes measurable quality benchmarks (for e.g., error rates, rework frequency, grievance closure time, audit observations) and monitors them through dashboards and periodic file audits.
Benchmarks performance against peer offices or departments using Sevottam, NeSDA , or similar frameworks to identify improvement areas.

Builds team capacity through handbooks, refreshers, or peer-learning sessions on documentation and quality assurance and control. Champions a culture of quality by recognising and teams/officials who consistently meet high quality standards. I embed systemic quality controls that reduce errors and improve service reliability.
I use evidence and citizen feedback to continuously raise departmental quality standards.

theme_description: Working in tandem with others as an integral unit, establishing partnerships and cooperative working relationships toward realizing Division / Department / Ministry goals. sub_theme_description: Actively establishes connections, nurtures relationships, and capitalizes on opportunities to identify intelligence and insights into existing or potential challenges. Inspires others to consult, keeping the greater good in mind, before arriving at any critical decisions.
Demonstrates willingness to trade-off immediate gain with long-term benefit. Collaborates with other stakeholders such as civil society organisations, social enterprises, government agencies, to help meet the M/D/Os goals and objectives.
 I forge high-impact partnerships and lead joint initiatives.
I enable reform at scale through sustained multi-sectoral collaboration.
I monitor stakeholder impact, using data-driven insights to refine partnerships.

theme_description: Working in tandem with others as an integral unit, establishing partnerships and cooperative working relationships toward realizing Division / Department / Ministry goals. Proactively sharing relevant and useful knowledge, experience, or expertise with peers/team to strengthen knowledge base. It also refers to leveraging diverse strengths and contribution of every officer/staff for timely and high-quality delivery.
sub_theme_description: Create an inclusive work environment that values and embraces diverse perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences by actively promoting diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) within the Ministry/Department/Organization and integrating it into various aspects of working.

proficiency_levels.label: Demonstrates foundational understanding of diversity and inclusion principles and applies them in daily interactions
proficiency_levels.description:
Demonstrates basic understanding of diversity, equity, and inclusion concepts, including visible and invisible diversity (for e.g., gender, caste, disability, language, region, age), and recognises why inclusion is essential for respectful collaboration and public service.
Demonstrates awareness of key statutory and policy frameworks related to workplace inclusion (for e.g., POSH Act, RPwD Act, reservation policies, Official Language Rules, etc) and understands their purpose in ensuring dignity, fairness, and equal opportunity.
Follows prescribed DEI ground rules and service conduct norms in routine interactions (for e.g., using respectful and gender-sensitive language in files/emails, allowing space for diverse viewpoints in meetings, following POSH and RPwD-related do’s and don’ts) , seeking guidance from supervisors when unsure about inclusive or appropriate conduct.
Completes mandatory orientations and trainings on DEI-related topics and consistently applies basic do’s and don’ts in day-to-day workplace behaviour, particularly during teamwork and discussions.
Ensures GIGW 3.0 basics in unit documents/slides saved to shared drives to verify accessibility for PwD colleagues before circulation.
Supports accessibility and inclusion in routine work by checking basic accessibility and bilingual requirements in shared communications or materials before circulation, as guided by unit norms.
Reports or escalates observed incidents of overt discrimination or harassment through prescribed channels, maintaining confidentiality and professionalism as per the POSH Act. Cooperates respectfully with colleagues from diverse linguistic, regional, or cultural backgrounds (for e.g., allowing time for translation or repetition, avoiding side conversations, sharing written summaries after meetings, etc) to ensure inclusive participation. I demonstrate basic understanding of DEI principles and related rules in my daily work.
I follow prescribed processes to support inclusion, accessibility, and safe reporting in the workplace.
I communicate and collaborate respectfully with colleagues from diverse backgrounds.

proficiency_levels.label: Facilitates inclusive collaboration by analysing patterns, adapting team practices, and enabling diverse participation
proficiency_levels.description:
Identifies and analyses patterns of exclusion, under-representation, or participation gaps as per DoPT categories (for e.g., SC, ST, OBC, EWC , gender, etc) within the team or section, based on observations, feedback, or available people/process data.
Applies DEI principles to adapt team workflows, meeting practices, and communication norms so that diverse voices are heard and considered during discussions and decision making.
Uses learnings from DEI trainings to guide peers informally and address inclusion-related issues during team interactions.
Facilitates inclusive discussions by actively encouraging quieter or marginalised voices, synthesising differing perspectives, and preventing dominance or bias in group interactions.
Uses structured feedback mechanisms (for e.g., anonymised surveys, retrospectives, open forums, etc) to surface inclusion-related concerns and supports the team in identifying practical corrective actions.
Analyses recruitment data (for e.g., shortlisting-to-selection ratios, stage-wise drop-offs by category) and applies standardised interview rubrics and panel diversity norms as per reservation rosters to review score patterns, document justifications, and identify potential bias in recruitment records maintained on e-Office.
Conducts barrier analysis with the team (for e.g., identifying participation gaps, communication barriers, or access issues), prioritises inclusion challenges based on impact and feasibility, and tracks agreed actions with clear ownership and timelines for periodic review.
Reviews communication templates (emails, circulars) against plain language guide, proposes edits with tracked changes, and justifies improvements for adoption.
Supports managers and peers by sharing inclusive practices, simple checklists, or examples, and informally guiding others on handling sensitive situations constructively. Applies inclusive thinking when coordinating with other sections, field units, or external stakeholders, adapting engagement styles to context and diversity. I analyse patterns and feedback to identify and address inclusion gaps in my team.
I facilitate collaboration by ensuring diverse perspectives are heard and balanced in decisions.
I support peers and juniors to apply inclusive practices in everyday teamwork.

proficiency_levels.label: Champions and institutionalises inclusive practices to strengthen M/D/O collaboration and outcomes
proficiency_levels.description:
Evaluates systemic and cultural barriers to inclusion across the M/D/O by analysing disaggregated HRMS and e-Office data, reviewing POSH and RPwD-related grievance patterns, and synthesising structured staff feedback and lived experiences (for e.g., pulse surveys, focus groups), to identify priority gaps affecting collaboration quality and organisational performance.
Leads the design and adoption of M/D/O-wide DEI approaches by aligning statutory requirements, organisational values, and strategic goals, ensuring inclusion is embedded in governance and leadership practices.
Influences senior leaders and peers by demonstrating how inclusion improves trust, collaboration quality, and delivery outcomes, rather than positioning DEI as compliance alone.
Embeds inclusion requirements into M/D/O systems and incentives by integrating DEI considerations into procurement and budgeting processes, accommodation mechanisms under RPwD Rules, and leadership performance frameworks (for e.g., KRAs, APAR, etc), to institutionalise accountability for inclusive outcomes.
Represents M/D/O in DARPG or Sevottam forums by presenting evidence-based case studies, critically evaluating external best practices, and leading adaptation pilots suited to theM/D/O context. Designs multilingual crisis communication protocols (for e.g., standard e-Office alerts or staff advisories in official languages), tests their effectiveness through periodic drills, and refines them based on learnings to ensure timely and inclusive M/D/O response. I identify and address systemic inclusion gaps using evidence to strengthen collaboration and M/D/O performance.
I integrate inclusion into governance, decision making, and leadership accountability mechanisms to sustain equitable outcomes.
I influence peers and leadership, and represent the M/D/O where required, to demonstrate how inclusion builds trust and improves delivery.

theme_description: Working in tandem with others as an integral unit, establishing partnerships and cooperative working relationships toward realizing Division / Department / Ministry goals. Proactively sharing relevant and useful knowledge, experience, or expertise with peers/team to strengthen knowledge base. It also refers to leveraging diverse strengths and contribution of every officer/staff for timely and high-quality delivery.
sub_theme_description: Exchanges explicit and implicit knowledge with stakeholders at the inter-, intra-, divisional, departmental, and ministerial levels in order to improve output that leverages multiple viewpoints.

proficiency_levels.label: Applies basic knowledge sharing practices by collecting, organising, and sharing credible information
proficiency_levels.description:
Demonstrates awareness of the purpose of knowledge sharing, recognising that it enhances collective understanding within the team, supports better decision-making, promotes innovation, and improves public service delivery.
Provides ideas, inputs, and observations (e.g. - extracting relevant data, reporting on-ground status, etc.,) gained through experiences with team members and seniors during section update meetings, file discussions, or progress reviews to support task execution and informed decision-making
Maintains relevant information from official (external and internal) sources such as archived files, government websites (e.g., PIB, RBI, Census), or internal databases (e.g., previous file notings, government portals, published reports) and shares it when asked, ensuring accurate data reporting and following proper formats..
Follows prescribed documentation practices by maintaining records, tagging documents, updating communication logs, and uploading scanned materials to eOffice or relevant digital repositories to support timely reporting and institutional memory.
Practices basic digital collaboration skills such as transferring files in e-Office, GeM, PFMS, etc., uploading relevant documents (such as submitting scanned documents for scheme processing, fund disbursal, grievance handling, etc.) for compliance, raising requests for timely approval and action, using relevant portals for uploading documents, or submission of documents to ensure compliance e.g. - submission of documents to secure grants or funds. Ensures knowledge storage and retrieval by following document management protocols such as indexing, tagging, and categorising digital or physical records using platforms like e-Office or physical file registers to ensure traceability and easy access. I understand the purpose of knowledge sharing and contribute to it by enhancing team understanding, supporting informed decision-making, promoting innovation, and improving implementation quality.
I collect and organise credible information from official sources like file notings, government portals, or reports and share it with relevant stakeholders.
I contribute relevant information, observations, and on-ground insights during meetings and file discussions to support informed decision-making and timely task execution.

proficiency_levels.label: Analyses knowledge needs and work patterns to improve coordination, efficiency, and implementation quality within teams
proficiency_levels.description:
Encourages the team to share experiences, knowledge and best practices in the form of material access (resources, notesheet, SOPs, etc), institutional support (scheme guidelines, amendments to relevant acts, notifications, issues), and intellectual support (conceptualising, drafting, etc) to increase effectiveness and efficiency in processes and procedures.
Offers constructive feedback to team members and supports a safe space for sharing lessons from implementation gaps and successes.
Coordinates the creation and upkeep of internal repositories (e.g., updated documents, notesheet and RTIs) that capture institutional memory and reduce repeat errors.
Applies different ways of knowledge sharing that is tacit (through mentoring and peer learning), explicit (through SOPs, reports, and documentation), and implicit (through reflective discussions and process improvements) to enhance team understanding, support implementation, and improve cross-functional collaboration.
Articulates knowledge gaps and needs identified during implementation or team interactions to guide the design of internal communication strategies and knowledge-sharing activities.
Identifies inefficiencies or redundancies in existing knowledge-sharing procedures (e.g., inconsistent documentation) and proposes innovative improvements, such as streamlined processes and assigning clear responsibilities.
Applies a collaborative mindset by convening team-level knowledge sessions (orientations or exposure visits) and problem-solving meetings (including review meetings or site visits) that leverage diverse perspectives to improve quality and turnaround time.
Facilitates structured peer learning through SOP walkthroughs, dashboard demonstrations, or hands-on guidance on tools such as eOffice, eHRMS, or file tracking mechanisms at M/D/O. Ensures cross-sectional sharing across branches by proactively linking similar incidents or precedents, or by seeking input from colleagues managing comparable functions. (For e.g., on financial matters, encourages sharing between the budget, funds and accounts sections of M/D/Os) I coordinate with colleagues to ensure maintenance of updated internal knowledge resources and use them to reduce errors, support team learning, and improve implementation.
I create a supportive environment for knowledge exchange by encouraging the team to share tools, experiences, and best practices.
I identify knowledge gaps, propose improvements to sharing practices, and lead peer learning sessions, exposure visits, or review discussions to strengthen collaboration and improve turnaround time.

proficiency_levels.label: Evaluates organisational knowledge gaps and strengthens knowledge-sharing practices to support continuous learning and improved performance
proficiency_levels.description:
Creates a conducive environment for knowledge sharing by fostering a culture of curiosity, learning, and collaboration.
Engages with internal and external stakeholders who demonstrate an interest in sharing strengths and experiences to support M/D/O objectives/goals through training workshops, meetings, consultations, open forums, etc.
Leads the development of formal knowledge management policies aligned with the M/D/O’s vision and mission, securing commitment from senior leadership to embed knowledge sharing in core organisational values and long-term strategies
Contributes to the design and effective use of knowledge management systems and digital repositories such as e-office, works management dashboards like SAMADHAN, SOPs, or guidelines on schemes or guidelines aligned to M/D/O’s vision, mission and objectives.
Fosters a culture of continuous learning by embedding knowledge sharing in team norms (e.g., review meetings, field visits, etc.), by organising regular orientation sessions, workshops, and creating learning opportunities for other team members
Advocates for and ensures dedicated budgetary allocation to design, implement, and sustain knowledge sharing initiatives such as digital repositories, cross-learning platforms, and inter-departmental knowledge exchanges.
Defines and tracks key performance indicators (KPIs) and monitoring frameworks to assess the impact of knowledge management practices, such as frequency of cross-team collaboration, use of knowledge resources, and updation of repositories.
Implements monitoring frameworks to evaluate the impact of knowledge management practices, such as the use of knowledge resources, timely reporting, and data sharing, to drive continuous improvements across established systems.
Builds partnerships with Civil Service Training Institutes (CSTIs), academic institutions, or industry experts to strengthen the M/D/O’s knowledge ecosystem, bring in cross-sectoral insights and update on recent developments.
Champions open knowledge ecosystems by contributing to inter-ministerial platforms (open forums, through articles, etc.) to promote transferability and collaborative problem-solving. Supports knowledge-sharing initiatives during critical projects (e.g., scheme/initiate launch, audits, cross-department reviews) to ensure institutional continuity and minimise dependency on any single official. I support the development and use of structured knowledge systems and knowledge sharing practices aligned with M/D/O priorities, contributing inputs for leadership decision making.
I strengthen knowledge sharing efforts by embedding them into team routines and using monitoring insights to improve learning and practice over time.
I build cross-sectoral partnerships and facilitate platforms like consultations, open forums, and training workshops to promote a collaborative and open knowledge sharing culture across teams and stakeholders.

theme_description: Demonstrates the ability to focus one's efforts on discovering and meeting the needs of stakeholders by establishing a rapport, putting oneself into the mindset of the stakeholder and facilitating the delivery of services that meet their underlying and unexpressed needs. Demonstrates the ability to provide excellent service delivery while developing and maintaining strong relationships with citizens and balancing the government's key strategic priorities.
sub_theme_description: Ability to understand and connect with the emotions, perspectives, and feelings of others and take actions to support them through challenging situations.

proficiency_levels.label: Recognises emotions and perspectives of others and responds to citizens with sensitivity and respect
proficiency_levels.description:
Understands emotional cues, perspectives, and differing perspectives of colleagues, citizens, and stakeholders to build trust, inclusion, and cooperative working relationships. Listens attentively during citizen interactions (for e.g., at a public facilitation counter, while recording a grievance on CPGRAMS, etc) without interrupting, and paraphrases concerns to confirm understanding.
Maintains calm and respectful tone while responding to repeated queries, RTI applicants, or dissatisfied citizens, ensuring communication remains constructive and solution-focused.
Applies patience and clarity while explaining eligibility norms, documentation requirements, or procedural steps (for e.g., under RTI Act timelines or welfare scheme documentation, etc).
Recognises emotionally sensitive situations (for e.g., bereavement benefits, disciplinary proceedings, audit objections involving staff, etc) and seeks guidance from supervisors before responding.
Demonstrates openness to understanding the emotions, concerns, and perspectives of citizens and colleagues, and responds in a manner that reflects sensitivity, respect, and support, particularly in challenging or high-stress situations. Treats all individuals fairly and without discrimination, including elderly persons, persons with disabilities, women, and marginalised groups, while providing service or recording grievances. I listen actively and acknowledge concerns before responding.
I remain calm and respectful while handling grievances and routine service requests.
I treat all citizens and colleagues fairly while adhering to Citizen Charter standards.

proficiency_levels.label: Applies empathy to strengthen collaboration, resolve concerns, and improve public service delivery outcomes
proficiency_levels.description:
Builds empathetic working relationships by recognising emotional and situational needs of colleagues and stakeholders and offering timely support (for e.g., helping a colleague manage urgent reporting work, checking in during high-pressure periods, etc).
Uses structured active listening techniques (for e.g., clarifying questions, summarising, validating emotions) during grievance reviews or team discussions to ensure mutual understanding.
Identifies early signs of stress, conflict, or dissatisfaction and takes appropriate action (for e.g., initiating conversations, clarifying roles, informing supervisors where required, etc).
Adapts communication style based on stakeholder context and emotional state (for e.g., using simpler language with citizens, slowing down discussions when someone is stressed, adjusting tone in grievance situations, etc).
Balances empathetic engagement with rules, processes, and service standards (for e.g., explaining process constraints while guiding citizens on available options, etc).
Considers team workload, morale, and operating pressures while planning or allocating work (for e.g., distributing urgent tasks across the team, adjusting timelines where feasible during peak workload periods, etc).
Applies empathy while implementing departmental processes or initiatives (for e.g., considering field staff availability, simplifying information requirements where possible, etc).
Responds to citizen concerns or grievances in a timely and respectful manner (e.g., clarifying process requirements, coordinating with field teams to resolve issues, updating citizens on request status, etc). Coordinates with field offices or implementation units to ensure emotionally sensitive cases (for e.g., delayed pensions, scholarship rejections, etc) are handled with urgency and clarity. I adapt my communication to address citizen emotional and service needs.
I resolve concerns constructively while adhering to departmental procedures and timelines.
I use grievance trends and feedback to improve service responsiveness and reduce repeat complaints.

proficiency_levels.label: Models empathy to inspire teams, navigate challenges, and strengthen public service delivery
proficiency_levels.description:
Implements a culture where teams imbibe empathy, fostering trust, psychological safety, and shared accountability across the M/D/O. Leads teams through emotional and operational challenges in high-pressure situations by providing clear guidance and reassurance (for e.g., during policy changes, major audits, or department-wide reviews, etc) to maintain confidence, motivation, and performance.
Balances empathy for individuals with fairness to institutional priorities, explaining decisions clearly and transparently.
Models empathetic communication during conflict, using staff dialogues, townhalls, or grievance reviews, to ensure every voice is heard and morale is maintained.
Establishes standard protocols that embed empathetic communication in grievance redressal systems (for e.g., revising CPGRAMS response templates, Citizen Charter language, or call-centre scripts, etc).
Reviews grievance dashboards, citizen satisfaction scores, and escalation trends to identify systemic gaps in responsiveness and redesign processes accordingly.
Leads post-incident reflection reviews after high-conflict or crisis situations (for e.g., public protests, audit scrutiny, disaster response, etc) to strengthen M/D/O learning and trust. Upholds a culture of compassion by inspiring colleagues to act with empathy towards citizens, improving service delivery and institutional credibility. I help build systems that promote respectful and empathetic public service delivery.
I balance empathy with fairness while making decisions.
I strengthen citizen trust by making services more inclusive and responsive.

theme_description: Demonstrates the ability to focus one's efforts on discovering and meeting the needs of stakeholders by establishing a rapport, putting oneself into the mindset of the stakeholder and facilitating the delivery of services that meet their underlying and unexpressed needs. Demonstrates the ability to provide excellent service delivery while developing and maintaining strong relationships with citizens and balancing the government's key strategic priorities.
sub_theme_description: Demonstrate the ability to respond respectfully and effectively and ensure the highest level of care and satisfaction of citizens.

proficiency_levels.label: Demonstrates respectful, timely, and empathetic responses
proficiency_levels.description:
Demonstrates basic awareness of one’s own role in citizen service delivery and follows defined service standards, escalation pathways, and response norms without deviation. Responds courteously and promptly to citizen/stakeholder requests, ensuring respect in tone and actions (for e.g., using approved response scripts, language templates, adhering to prescribed communication protocols, and keeping citizens informed of progress, etc).
Documents queries and responses accurately in systems like CPGRAMS and e-Office to maintain transparency, while updating status regularly, mitigating citizen follow up.
Demonstrates empathy, especially in cases where citizens struggle to articulate their needs (for e.g., by asking clarifying questions, restating concerns to confirm understanding, etc).
Escalates issues responsibly if beyond personal authority, ensuring no grievance is left unattended, while keeping citizens informed about expected timelines and next steps.
Refers to official guidelines, FAQs, Citizen Charters, and approved knowledge repositories to respond accurately, avoiding assumptions or unofficial advice.
Proactively seeks clarification or support from supervisors or peers when faced with unfamiliar queries or situations, rather than delaying or providing incorrect information.
Handles citizen information responsibly by adhering to data-sharing protocols and confidentiality norms during communication and documentation. Identifies simple recurring issues and flags them to supervisors (for e.g., repeated delays in a specific service, frequent documentation confusion, etc). I respond to citizens respectfully and empathetically on time.
I follow service standards, escalate when needed, and document all cases accurately to maintain transparency.
I use official guidelines, seek support when unsure, protect citizen data, and flag recurring issues for improvement.

proficiency_levels.label: Applies systemic improvements and coordination to address citizen needs seamlessly
proficiency_levels.description:
Analyses dashboards and MIS tools (e.g., CPGRAMS, MyGov portal, etc) to track citizen satisfaction and systemic responsiveness by identifying patterns of delays, repeat complaints, and discontinuation of services.
Balances competing departmental priorities by applying structured coordination, negotiating realistic timelines and communicating proactively with internal and external stakeholders.
Analyses citizen narratives to distinguish between procedural issues, service gaps, and emotional reassurance needs, and responds accordingly.
Demonstrates emotional regulation and composure when managing complex, sensitive, or escalated citizen interactions, maintaining professionalism under pressure.
Demonstrates sensitivity to vulnerable or marginalised groups and adapts engagement to reduce power asymmetries and discomfort.
Improves procedures where delays or repeated complaints indicate deeper service gaps by applying root cause / problem tree analysis tools (for e.g., 5 Whys, Fishbone diagrams, etc) to recommend fixes.
Mentors team members on treating every citizen interaction as an opportunity to build trust and models appropriate tone, empathy, and professionalism.
Coordinates across sections/departments (for e.g., Finance, IT, field offices) to resolve cross-cutting issues promptly (for eg., approvals, system-errors, verification, and policy conflicts) and provide efficient service to citizens.
Establishes feedback loops (for e.g., post-service calls, IVRS surveys, WhatsApp check-ins) to validate if citizen needs were truly met.
Ensures communication is adapted to diverse audiences (language, literacy, accessibility) using plain-language guidelines and translated materials. Monitors grievances and proactively intervenes when cases risk breaching service delivery timelines. I use dashboards and feedback to understand citizen needs, identify service gaps, and ensure timely, accurate responses.
I coordinate across teams, and resolve cross-cutting issues so citizens receive smooth and reliable services.
I communicate with empathy, adapt to diverse citizens, stay composed under pressure, and mentor others to uphold high service standards.

proficiency_levels.label: Contributes to citizen-centric responsiveness by reinforcing service oriented practices in day-to-day implementation
proficiency_levels.description:
Drives and ensures responsiveness frameworks (e.g., service-level standards, grievance-redressal protocols, citizen charter mechanisms) are embedded in Ministry/Departmental priorities.
Enforces clear service standards by strengthening Citizen Charters, defining measurable service delivery benchmarks, and ensuring these are publicly communicated, periodically updated, and rigorously monitored.
Sets norms for transparency through public dashboards and citizen feedback loops to strengthen accountability and continuous improvement in citizen service delivery.
Leads teams by demonstrating and reinforcing best practices in active listening, empathetic communication, emotional regulation, and professional tonality, ensuring that staff consistently interact with citizens respectfully and deliver services effectively.
Creates enabling ecosystems for responsiveness by strengthening institutional capabilities, improving grievance platforms, building staff competencies, and ensuring resources, SOPs, and digital systems are continuously upgraded for better delivery of services to the citizens.
Influences organisational mindsets by role-modelling responsiveness, inspiring teams to prioritise citizen needs, and promoting a culture where officials take ownership of outcomes, not just processes.
Balances long-term national priorities with immediate service responsiveness (for e.g., ensuring continuity of policy commitments while simultaneously mobilising rapid citizen support during crises or emergencies). Creates a culture where officials at all levels value and practice responsiveness, by modelling desired behaviours, institutionalising service standards, integrating responsiveness into training and appraisal systems. I embed and uphold robust service standards and responsiveness frameworks through clear benchmarks, dashboards, and citizen feedback mechanisms.
I build a culture of accountability and service excellence by mentoring teams and strengthening institutional capabilities.
I balance long-term priorities with immediate citizen needs, strengthening systems and driving timely, reliable service delivery across the institution.

theme_description: Demonstrates the ability to focus one's efforts on discovering and meeting the needs of stakeholders by establishing a rapport, putting oneself into the mindset of the stakeholder and facilitating the delivery of services that meet their underlying and unexpressed needs. Demonstrates the ability to provide excellent service delivery while developing and maintaining strong relationships with citizens and balancing the government's key strategic priorities.
sub_theme_description: Demonstrating professional perseverance by focusing one’s efforts on meeting the set goals of the government as well as needs of the citizen while maintaining quality of delivery.

proficiency_levels.label: Responds to citizen queries and requests promptly and respectfully
proficiency_levels.description:
Understands how one supports the department’s citizen service goals and recognises that each interaction shapes citizen trust in governance. Responds promptly and respectfully to citizen queries by following prescribed procedures (e.g., verifying documents, explaining forms, guiding through portals like DigiLocker or UMANG, etc).
Acknowledges service issues raised by citizens (e.g., delayed disbursements, pending applications) and escalates them through designated channels (e.g., CPGRAMS, grievance portals, escalation matrices, etc) for timely follow-up.
Maintains courteous and professional communication across in-person, telephonic, and digital platforms so that citizens feel heard and respected.
Records service interactions and resolution details accurately in registers or digital systems to ensure continuity and tracking..
Maintains composure and neutrality during high-pressure or emotionally charged situations, ensuring fairness and quality in service delivery.
Seeks guidance from supervisors to clarify doubts and maintain consistency with service standards. Seeks simple, immediate feedback (e.g., “Was this helpful?” at the end of an interaction) to check service adequacy and improve future delivery. I respond to citizen requests timely and respectfully by following procedures to ensure consistency and fairness.
I escalate unresolved service issues through appropriate channels to ensure timely redressal.
I maintain accurate records of citizen interactions to support follow-ups and build public trust.

proficiency_levels.label: Anticipates citizen needs, adapts delivery approaches, and contributes to improving service systems
proficiency_levels.description:
Identifies common service challenges (e.g., digital access barriers, unclear procedures, high paperwork load) by reviewing grievances, field data, and recurring complaints. Adapts communication and service delivery approaches to suit diverse citizen contexts - for example, providing verbal guidance to digitally excluded citizens, translating forms for local understanding, or simplifying complex instructions for low-literacy users.
Balances empathy and efficiency by listening actively to citizens’ concerns while adhering to service standards and timelines.
Collaborates with colleagues across departments to resolve interlinked citizen issues (e.g., multi-step approvals for health, education, or financial benefits).
Keeps citizens informed about the status of requests, expected timelines, and next steps in simple, accessible language.
Seeks structured feedback (e.g., suggestion boxes, WhatsApp helplines, targeted surveys) and uses it to make tangible service improvements rather than only collecting inputs.
Identifies bottlenecks (e.g., repetitive documentation, delayed approvals) and designs practical tools like FAQs, guides, or simplified checklists to reduce citizen effort. Initiates small-scale systemic improvements (e.g., organising community helpdesks, leveraging social media for updates, documenting process notes for internal use) to improve accessibility and reduce turnaround times. I anticipate and respond to citizen needs in a timely and context-sensitive manner to improve their service experience.
I collaborate across teams and proactively communicate with citizens to ensure efficient resolution of their requests.
I take measures such as creating process guides or collecting feedback to reduce delays and improve service quality.

proficiency_levels.label: Advocates for citizen-centric governance by driving systemic improvements and fostering a people-first culture
proficiency_levels.description:
Advocates for changes in service rules, eligibility criteria, or formats by presenting evidence from recurring citizen grievances and service performance data at decision-making forums. Manages and regularly updates citizen feedback channels (for e.g., public consultations, digital feedback tools, community forums, etc), summarising key issues and trends to inform service improvements.
Builds a culture of empathy and fairness by mentoring teams, recognising good service practices, and encouraging reflection on the citizen impact of daily work.
Revises or approves updates to service tools (e.g., SOPs, helpdesk scripts, citizen charters) to improve accessibility, reduce turnaround times, and maintain service quality benchmarks.
Guides teams in handling complex or sensitive scenarios (e.g., marginalised communities, emotionally distressed citizens) with care, neutrality, and responsiveness.
Represents the M/D/O in state, national, or inter-departmental forums to share successful citizen-centric practices, advocate for reforms, and influence peer learning.
Explains major policy changes and unavoidable delays openly and proactively, helping citizens understand the rationale and sustaining confidence in government services. Advances a people-first approach by aligning departmental initiatives with citizen service goals and promoting effective governance that delivers measurable improvements. I advocate for policy and process reforms to make services more accessible, transparent, and citizen-focused.
I mentor teams to build a culture of empathy, fairness, and accountability in service delivery.
I lead initiatives that align departmental systems with citizen service goals to achieve effective and trustworthy governance.

theme_description: Establishes plans, defines milestones, and allots resources for regularly producing high-quality, cost-effective results that are in accordance with the department's or ministry's overall objectives. Focuses on tasks that will increase effectiveness, efficiency, and production through planning, intentional effort, and control. Determines goals, assigns tasks, and establishes priorities based on skill levels and the availability of resources.
sub_theme_description: Demonstrate the ability to effectively and efficiently allocate, utilise, and optimise various resources to achieve strategic goals and objective.

proficiency_levels.label: Demonstrates foundational understanding of efficient resource use to support smooth and timely public service delivery
proficiency_levels.description:
Understands that financial, human, time, and infrastructure resources are limited and must be used efficiently to avoid waste, duplication, and public service delays.
Maps people, funds, and materials against an approved work plan (for e.g., section duty rosters, e-Office trackers, scheme implementation schedules, etc) while recognising resource constraints.
Records utilisation of resources (for e.g., funds in PFMS, staff deployment logs, asset usage registers) to ensure they are used for approved purposes.
Follows prescribed procedures before committing resources (for e.g., approval notes, procurement through GeM where applicable) to ensure disciplined usage.
Tracks basic time and capacity indicators (for e.g., file turnaround time, pending case count, staff-hour allocation) to prevent bottlenecks.
Identifies inefficiencies (for e.g., idle equipment, repeated rework, overlapping responsibilities) and informs supervisors.
Recognises how misallocation or delays in resource use affect service timelines and public service delivery outcomes. Demonstrates responsible stewardship by avoiding over-commitment, duplication, or unnecessary expenditure. I understand the importance of efficient and disciplined resource use.
I align resource use with approved priorities and timelines.
I identify and flag basic inefficiencies or risks early.

proficiency_levels.label: Plans, prioritises, and optimises resources to improve productivity, efficiency, and service impact
proficiency_levels.description:
Analyses financial, human, infrastructure, and time resource requirements across units or programmes and prioritises allocation based on impact, urgency, and M/D/O objectives.
Develops structured resource deployment plans (e.g., staff allocation charts, milestone schedules, infrastructure usage plans, workload balancing sheets, etc) aligned with service targets.
Balances competing demands by reallocating time, effort, and assets toward high-impact activities.
Monitors utilisation using performance dashboards, workflow analytics (for e.g., e-Office movement data, grievance disposal metrics, service turnaround reports, etc) and identifies inefficiencies.
Diagnoses root causes of resource waste (for e.g., workflow bottlenecks, duplication of approvals, uneven staff distribution, etc) and recommends corrective adjustments.
Evaluates trade-offs between cost, quality, speed, compliance, and equity when reallocating resources (for e.g., balancing faster procurement with due diligence safeguards).
Optimises workflows (for e.g., redistributing workload across sections, improving approval sequencing, reducing redundant documentation, etc) to enhance productivity.
Coordinates with finance, procurement, administration, and vendors to ensure timely availability of funds, materials, and services. Applies value-for-money thinking (for e.g., choosing sustainable procurement options, reducing recurring maintenance burden, pooling shared resources, etc). I plan and monitor resources to ensure efficient and timely delivery of work.
I identify and address inefficiencies while maintaining compliance.
I balance competing priorities to maximise impact within available resources.

proficiency_levels.label: Shapes and reforms resource allocation systems to maximise public value and long-term institutional sustainability
proficiency_levels.description:
Evaluates M/D/O-wide deployment of financial, human, technological, and infrastructure resources to identify systemic inefficiencies and performance gaps.
Redesigns allocation models and operating structures (for e.g., centralised vs decentralised deployment, shared services, digital automation of workflows, etc) to improve productivity and reduce waste.
Aligns capital, operational, and human resource planning with Outcome Budget frameworks, Annual Action Plans, and multi-year strategic priorities.
Anticipates future resource needs based on evolving strategic, operational, and environmental drivers (for e.g., programme expansion, demographic shifts, technology adoption, regulatory changes, or climate resilience requirements).
Leads high-impact decisions involving cross-functional resource trade-offs and long-term sustainability considerations.
Establishes performance metrics (for e.g., cost per service delivered, utilisation ratios, productivity indices, citizen satisfaction indicators, etc) to measure value creation.
Champions innovation and sustainable practices (for e.g., digitisation, preventive maintenance, green procurement, shared digital platforms) to strengthen resilience.
Links resource governance reforms to measurable improvements in efficiency, quality, and public service delivery outcomes. I shape resource governance systems that improve productivity and public value.
I institutionalise systems that ensure long-term efficiency and value for money.
I strengthen M/D/O capacity through sustainable and outcome-linked resource management.

theme_description: Establishes plans, defines milestones, and allots resources for regularly producing high-quality, cost-effective results that are in accordance with the department's or ministry's overall objectives. sub_theme_description: Analyse and implement government processes and procedures to ensure alignment to the department's strategic objectives and ensure value to both internal and external stakeholders.

proficiency_levels.label: Follows workflows and utilises digital tools to organise, document, and complete tasks efficiently
proficiency_levels.description:
Understands and follows established government processes and procedures, recognising how each contributes to achieving M/D/O’s goals. Identifies and names key components of government administrative processes (e.g., file noting, approvals, record-keeping), and articulates their role in service delivery and institutional functioning within the M/D/O.
Organises personal work systematically using basic tools (such as to-do lists, tracking formats) and engages with available digital platforms (e.g., eOffice, PFMS, HRMS, etc.) for assigned work, seeking guidance when encountering unfamiliar features or issues.
Demonstrates awareness of how administrative processes contribute to larger M/D/O objectives, and reflects on how small delays or inefficiencies can affect service delivery outcomes.
Documents steps taken during task execution (e.g., maintains logs, adds notings, drafts email trails) to support continuity and institutional memory.
Seeks input and feedback from peers or supervisors when applying new processes, reflecting on suggestions to improve execution.
Adjusts to changing work demands or interruptions with basic support from colleagues, demonstrating adaptability and willingness to reprioritise tasks.
Participates in team discussions or reviews with curiosity, offering firsthand observations to understand process gaps or recurring delays.
Demonstrates openness to learning by reviewing field reports, audit findings, and user feedback to reflect and make iterative improvements grounded in operational realities. Shows attention to detail and clarity by refining and standardising tools like trackers, SOPs, or checklists, making them more accessible, user-friendly, and supportive of compliance and task-level handovers. I follow workflows, stay organised, and use digital tools to complete tasks on time.
I organise my work, monitor my progress, and flag any delays or inefficiencies.

proficiency_levels.label: Analyses process issues across teams, and refines tools and workflows to reduce delays and improve execution
proficiency_levels.description:
Implements process enhancements initiatives by engaging field teams, beneficiaries, and supervisors to identify process gaps and adapts existing workflows to improve relevance and responsiveness while maintaining compliance and transparency.
Manages plans and timelines proactively to manage shifting priorities or process delays, ensuring continued delivery in line with stakeholder expectations and M/D/O’s goals.
Coordinates proactively across the Ministry or Department to align timelines, manage task dependencies, and ensure resources are deployed efficiently, fostering accountability and mutual support among teams.
Engages collaboratively with IT teams, vendors, or helpdesks when platform issues arise (e.g., PFMS delays, DBT errors), proposing practical workarounds or improvements and ensuring service continuity without escalation delays.
Applies analytical thinking using methods like root cause analysis or fishbone diagrams to examine bottlenecks or redundancies, and implements redesign of process segments to reduce turnaround time while documenting all changes in line with government protocols.
Encourages a participatory team environment by creating space for colleagues to share implementation insights, co-own decisions, and hold each other accountable for timely, coordinated execution.
Analyses field reports, audit findings, and citizens’ feedback to identify gaps and implements iterative improvements that enhance operational effectiveness and relevance.
Develops process implementation plans by defining workflows, setting milestones, and allocating resources, ensuring alignment with M/D/O priorities and expected outcomes.
Modifies tools such as trackers, SOPs, and checklists by analysing operational needs of the M/D/O to improve clarity, usability, and alignment with compliance requirements and team workflows.
Identifies key stakeholders across departments and engages them to co-create implementation strategies and refine operational processes that maximise the value and relevance of outcomes.
Anticipates and mitigates process risks by incorporating redundancies, fallback workflows, and cross-departmental review systems.
Maintains partnerships within the Ministry or Department and with external stakeholders to co-develop or adapt digital tools and workflows that improve administrative efficiency while aligning with policy and platform requirements. I improve workflows by identifying recurring issues and suggesting practical changes.
I coordinate across teams to maintain efficiency and resolve process delays.
I analyse feedback and apply structured problem-solving to improve how tasks are executed.

proficiency_levels.label: Strengthens M/D/O process redesigns, institutionalises new systems, and mentors teams to embed continuous process improvement
proficiency_levels.description:
Strengthens process improvement initiatives by documenting existing procedures, defining roles and decision points, setting measurable performance indicators (e.g., turnaround time, error rates), and aligning team work plans, review mechanisms with M/D/O’s goals.
Provides strategic foresight for process and system improvement by integrating field data, stakeholder feedback, and compliance norms to resolve systemic inefficiencies and advance department-wide reforms aligned with organisational and national priorities.
Champions the design and institutionalisation of citizen-centric processes, ensuring administrative efficiency (e.g., DBT-enabled schemes, automated approvals) using process performance data and field insights to ensure redesigns optimise compliance, efficiency, and the overall citizen experience.
Establishes and monitors process performance metrics such as turnaround time, error rates, and user satisfaction, setting up dashboards and regular performance routines (e.g., reviews, coordination meetings) to align team efforts and resources with M/D/O goals.
Aligns redesigned workflows with broader departmental and national priorities (e.g., Viksit Bharat 2047, SDGs, Digital India), ensuring operational feasibility across diverse field contexts.
Supports the adoption of innovative processes by securing leadership endorsement and broad stakeholder buy-in in line with policy mandates and digital governance objectives.
Encourages a systems-thinking approach to resource reallocation, crisis management, and maintenance of service delivery standards in the Ministry or Department.
Drives cultural and structural transformation by institutionalising new workflows through SOPs, handbooks, and policy advisories, and by developing and standardising high-quality process documentation (e.g., revised SOPs, knowledge repositories, training guides) to ensure accessibility and support organisational learning.
Mentors teams by translating advanced process methodologies (e.g., Lean, Six Sigma) into accessible, actionable practices for daily use, and drives digital transformation by identifying systemic issues, coordinating upgrades, and fostering sustained adoption and impact through ongoing team support. Demonstrates strategic foresight by reviewing implementation outcomes, conducting “lessons learned” exercises, and applying insights to future improvements, while building a culture of continuous feedback and adaptive improvement through structured reflection spaces to capture lessons, test solutions, and update team norms. I use data, feedback, and metrics to track process outcomes and guide improvements.
I mentor teams, institutionalise best practices, and build systems for ongoing process excellence.

theme_description: Establishes plans, defines milestones, and allots resources for regularly producing high-quality, cost-effective results that are in accordance with the department's or ministry's overall objectives. sub_theme_description: Demonstrate the ability to deliver high-quality services through improvement of existing processes, systems, and practices within the sections, divisions, or departments.

proficiency_levels.label: Follows procedures to identify and report basic workflow inefficiencies
proficiency_levels.description:
Demonstrates ability to follow prescribed rules and instructions (for e.g., DoPT guidelines, CCS Rules, office manuals, etc) by referring to established procedures before acting, ensuring that work is compliant and free from avoidable errors. Shows understanding of existing office systems and workflows by observing how files, notes, and approvals move, thereby developing a foundational awareness of how the section operates.
Uses digital platforms (for e.g., e-Office, SPARROW , CPGRAMS , GeM , etc), ensuring tasks are processed in the correct systems and remain trackable and transparent.
Maintains accuracy in file noting and drafting under supervision by presenting facts correctly, following templates, and checking for errors, contributing to clearer documentation and less rework.
Identifies small or obvious inefficiencies (for e.g., duplicate paperwork, unnecessary movement of files, delays in obtaining signatures, etc) and brings them to the notice of the supervisor, contributing to smoother daily operations.
Follows required formats, templates, and quality norms when preparing drafts or inputs, helping maintain consistency across the section’s outputs.

Shows readiness to support guided improvements (for e.g., adopting a new step in the workflow, simplifying a repetitive task, etc), helping improve quality while learning from supervisors. I complete tasks accurately and within prescribed timelines using established rules and systems.
I use approved digital platforms to ensure transparency and traceability.
