proficiency_levels.label: Redesigns and monitors departmental processes to improve efficiency and accountability
proficiency_levels.description:
Improves end-to-end workflows (for e.g., RTI routing process, procurement approval cycle, grievance redressal chain, etc) and removes redundant approval layers to reduce TAT.
Analyses MIS dashboards and pendency reports (e.g., CPGRAMS pendency dashboard, e-Office disposal reports, PFMS fund release tracking) to identify bottlenecks.
Ensures alignment with government initiatives (for e.g., Digital India compliance, Sevottam service standards, Citizen Charter commitments, etc) while redesigning workflows.
Conducts structured root-cause analysis (for e.g., cause-effect mapping for repeated audit objections, process mapping for delayed sanction approvals, etc) to diagnose inefficiencies.
Uses stakeholder feedback (for e.g., citizen grievance categories in CPGRAMS, RTI query trends, audit observations, etc) to refine internal processes.
Introduces pilot improvements (for e.g., digitising manual registers, simplifying internal checklists, introducing weekly pendency tracker sheets, etc) before full implementation.
Designs monitoring tools (for e.g., Excel-based pendency dashboards, colour-coded compliance trackers, weekly review templates, etc) to enhance accountability.
Measures impact by comparing pre- and post-intervention indicators (for e.g., file disposal time reduced from 15 to 9 days, grievance closure rate improved by 20%, etc) Improves accessibility by simplifying document requirements (for e.g., reducing unnecessary affidavit submissions, standardising checklist-based applications). I streamline workflows to reduce delays, duplication, and resource wastage.
I use data and feedback to improve service reliability and accountability.
I monitor measurable performance indicators to sustain efficiency improvements.

proficiency_levels.label: Drives and embeds system-wide process reforms to sustain efficiency and citizen-centric performance standards
proficiency_levels.description:
Anticipates systemic inefficiencies (for e.g., recurring inter-departmental approval delays, repeated audit paras, etc) and proposes structural reforms aligned with national priorities (for e.g., Ease of Living, Digital Governance initiatives, etc).

theme_description: Champions ‘out of the box’ thinking, and supports experimentation of new ideas, utilizing technological advancements with the aim of transforming operations to enhance governance efficiency. proficiency_levels.label: Drives innovation by embedding flexibility in strategies and builds a culture of adaptability in government
proficiency_levels.description:

Synthesises insights from multiple sectors, disciplines, and behavioural patterns to challenge assumptions and introduce creative approaches, such as incorporating behavioural nudges into citizen engagement strategies.

proficiency_levels.label: Adopts new digital practices, uses departmental tools, and suggests small improvements to routine work

proficiency_levels.label: Brings global foresight into strategic decision making and planning

Encourages teams to adopt a global outlook through mentoring, capacity building, and embedding global best practices into departmental systems. Establishes long-term global learning partnerships and knowledge exchanges (for e.g., MoUs with OECD, UNDP collaborations, etc) to advance departmental goals.  I communicate persuasively by structuring arguments with relevant facts, policies, and relatable examples, ensuring that messages are inclusive and tailored to diverse stakeholders.

 I lead high-stakes negotiations with government, industry, and global partners, using adaptive strategies and consensus-building techniques to secure agreements that drive national policy and governance priorities.

theme_description: Fosters a positive work environment by actively engaging with the team, enabling their growth, and enhancing their proficiency. sub_theme_description: Provides timely feedback in a helpful, supportive, and constructive manner to others in a way that promotes their personal and professional growth while maintaining a positive and respectful working relationship.

proficiency_levels.label: Understands the value of constructive feedback and communicates it respectfully
proficiency_levels.description:
Recognises the importance of the role of feedback to support an individual's personal and professional growth. Demonstrates openness to receiving feedback by listening without defensiveness and acknowledging points for improvement.
Prepares feedback using a simple structure (for e.g., Situation-Behavior-Impact, Glow–Grow, etc) and supports it with objective evidence such as file outputs, noting quality, service timelines, or task trackers maintained on e-Office or section registers.
Checks readiness and seeks consent for the feedback conversation from the colleague (for e.g., “Is this a good time?”) and maintains a calm, courteous tone throughout the conversation.
Invites the colleague’s self-assessment and allows them to share their view of the situation first and listens attentively by paraphrasing key points, asking basic clarifying questions, and avoiding assumptions.
Provides feedback privately using respectful, neutral language that focuses on specific actions (for e.g., missed deadlines, incomplete documentation, etc) rather than personal traits, avoiding labels or blame.
Refers to simple and commonly understood standards (for e.g., task instructions, agreed-upon timelines, basic checklists, etc) when explaining feedback, so expectations are clear and grounded in a shared understanding.
Suggests specific manageable actions for improvement, such as clarifying steps, using a job aid, or trying a different approach in the next task, with an indicative timeframe discussed. Creates psychological safety by inviting feedback from team members and responding constructively to concerns or suggestions. I check readiness for feedback, listen openly, and communicate respectfully using neutral, non-judgemental language.
I focus feedback on specific work behaviours and agreed expectations.

Frames feedback around future focused improvements by suggesting alternative approaches or next steps for upcoming tasks, particularly when similar issues recur.
Creates developmental action plans based on received feedback that focuses on skills to be built and provides practice opportunities, tracking closure through regular check-ins.
Uses a clear escalation pathway for feedback and performance concerns (for e.g., progressing from coaching to a written improvement plan and, where required, consulting HR) while maintaining confidentiality and respectful handling throughout. Balances candour with empathy by addressing performance gaps clearly while reinforcing trust and ongoing working relationships. I provide timely, evidence-based feedback using consistent standards and considering context.
I use future-focused, developmental feedback to support improvement and strengthen peer capability.
I contribute to team learning by sharing feedback patterns and reinforcing openness and trust.

Applies aggregated feedback insights to drive systemic reforms such as improving role clarity, rebalancing workloads, strengthening coordination mechanisms, or refining service standards rather than targeting individual employees.
Establishes clear escalation governance that distinguishes developmental feedback from performance management or disciplinary action, ensuring due process, confidentiality, and protection against misuse.
Measures the impact of feedback governance using indicators (for e.g., team climate, error reduction, service timeliness and quality, citizen satisfaction proxies, etc) and iteratively refines policies and practices based on evidence. Intervenes when feedback is misused or perceived as punitive, reinforcing its purpose as a developmental and learning tool. I establish and govern M/D/O-wide feedback systems that ensure privacy, fairness, and psychological safety.
I use aggregated data and feedback insights to identify patterns, check for bias, and drive systemic improvements rather than individualised action.

Recognises emotional cues in self and colleagues and regulates responses to maintain professionalism during deadline-driven tasks (for e.g., parliamentary replies, audit responses, etc).
Maintains organised documentation and transparent note-drafting practices to set a predictable and careful example for peers.
Acknowledges colleagues’ contributions in meetings or official communications to reinforce positive behaviours.
Listens actively by summarising others’ inputs before responding, building foundational trust within the team.
Reports task completion transparently through MIS updates or file remarks, ensuring individual accountability. I demonstrate understanding of Karmayogi resolves and values through reliable and ethical conduct.
I fulfil assigned responsibilities diligently and meet established timelines.
I encourage colleagues through respectful listening and positive reinforcement.

proficiency_levels.label: Motivates and supports the team by demonstrating emotional intelligence and providing guidance
proficiency_levels.description:
Demonstrates emotional regulation during high-pressure cycles (for e.g., audit scrutiny, parliamentary questions, scheme reporting, etc) and stabilises team morale through clear communication. Embodies the spirit of service and empathy by actively listening to team concerns and offering practical support to resolve bottlenecks.
Uses structured one-on-one developmental conversations to provide evidence-based feedback linked to measurable performance indicators (for e.g., pendency reduction, grievance disposal timelines, etc).
Demonstrates a high degree of ownership and consistency in fulfilling team-wide commitments, setting a reliable benchmark for others to follow.
Recognises and reinforces behaviours that reflect Karmayogi values (integrity, diligence, responsiveness), linking appreciation to observable performance improvements.
Encourages collaborative working (Sahakaryata) by soliciting diverse viewpoints before decisions and strengthening shared ownership.
Addresses interpersonal tensions promptly using structured dialogue and agreed corrective actions to maintain a respectful and productive environment.
Explicitly connects routine tasks to citizen well-being (Svadharma) by linking everyday responsibilities to mission outcomes. Identifies opportunities to enhance the skills of peers through informal guidance and sharing of professional best practices. I provide structured feedback and recognition that improves team performance.
I foster a respectful and emotionally stable environment that sustains motivation and trust.
I align team efforts with measurable service delivery goals and accountability standards.

proficiency_levels.label: Institutionalises inspirational and citizen-centric leadership by modelling and embedding Karmayogi values
proficiency_levels.description:
Defines and embeds leadership norms reflecting duty (Kartavya), unity (Ekta), pride (Garva), and developmental commitment (Vikas) across the M/D/O.
Leads initiatives that embed ethical norms and good governance principles into permanent M/D/O policies and daily team culture.
Establishes performance-linked recognition frameworks that reinforce Svadharma (serving citizens with dedication) and measurable improvements (for e.g., Citizen Charter compliance, grievance resolution, etc).
Advocates stewardship of public interest (Svadharma) in all M/D/O decision making to sustain citizen's trust and improve Jana-Hita (societal good).
Champions psychological safety at scale by institutionalising feedback forums, anonymous climate inputs, and periodic leadership reflection sessions.
Demonstrates ethical courage in complex or politically sensitive situations, modelling principled decision making that reinforces M/D/O credibility.
Anchors strategic decisions in public value creation, reinforcing Svadharma and developmental vision (Vikas) in M/D/O goals. Influences cross-departmental stakeholders by exemplifying professionalism, emotional maturity, and unity in action (Ekta), enabling mission-wide adoption of Karmayogi values. I institutionalise leadership practices that strengthen integrity, accountability, and citizen trust across the M/D/O.
I build sustainable systems of recognition and mentoring rooted in Karmayogi values to elevate M/D/O performance.
I inspire principled, purpose-driven leadership aligned with national developmental and citizen-centric goals.

theme_description: Possess the ability to analyse facts, reports, policies, precedents, constraints, risks, and conflicting points of view in a comprehensive and logical manner to gain a holistic perspective and arrive at a timely decision. It involves weighing the pros and cons of various options to arrive at the best possible decision that would lead to the welfare of citizens and contribute towards the attainment of Aatma Nirbhar & Viksit Bharat.
sub_theme_description: Objectively analyse, evaluate, and interpret information and arguments in a logical and systematic manner in order to arrive at conclusions.

proficiency_levels.label: Gathers and organises reliable information from credible sources to support decisions
proficiency_levels.description:
Identifies and categorises relevant and credible information sources, collecting new data from internal and external sources (such as World Bank publications and Indian government reports) to inform decision-making at the ministries, departments, and organisations. Differentiates between primary and secondary sources, cross-validating collected data against multiple credible sources to ensure accuracy and reliability in the decision-making process.
Understands structured data collection techniques (such as surveys, questionnaires, and interviews) and systematically applies these methods to gather information using basic research principles.
Organises data logically through categorisation, labelling, and structuring, ensuring clarity and ease of retrieval for future analysis.
Documents findings in a systematic manner using standardised formats, facilitating future analysis and reporting while ensuring consistency and accessibility of information.
Understands various logical and critical thinking frameworks (such as SWOT analysis and decision trees) and applies these tools to enhance analytical thinking and decision-making processes.
I collect and categorise credible information from diverse internal and external sources.
I verify the accuracy of information by cross-referencing multiple credible sources.
I organise and document data in a structured and logical manner for easy retrieval and future analysis.

proficiency_levels.label: Applies structured tools to analyse options, prioritise solutions, and reach consensus-based decisions
proficiency_levels.description:
Evaluates complex data and information to identify significant trends, risks, and patterns that inform decision-making, demonstrating analytical thinking and attention to detail.
Utilises structured tools such as SWOT analysis, decision matrices, and risk assessments to systematically evaluate options, fostering a collaborative environment that encourages team input and diverse perspectives.
Utilises behavioural frameworks to prioritise solutions based on their potential impact and feasibility.
Demonstrates flexibility by adapting frameworks to meet the specific context and requirements of the decision-making process at the ministries, departments, and organisations.
Facilitates scenario analysis to explore multiple potential outcomes, assessing the risks and benefits associated with each decision, thereby promoting critical thinking and sound judgement among team members.
Guides the team towards consensus on decisions through logical reasoning and collaborative problem-solving, enhancing communication skills and ensuring that all voices are heard.
Performs basic risk analysis while organising and validating data to ensure the credibility and accuracy of the information collected, exemplifying diligence and a commitment to high-quality standards in the decision-making process.
I integrate insights from multiple complex data sources to inform tactical decision-making.
I apply structured tools such as SWOT analysis, decision matrices, and risk assessment matrices to prioritise options and guide strategic choices.
I reach consensus on decisions that reflect the collective input of cross-functional teams.

proficiency_levels.label: Anchors strategic decision making in national priorities
proficiency_levels.description:
Demonstrates strategic foresight by actively engaging in forecasting techniques and scenario planning to assess the long-term implications of decisions on organisational and national objectives.
Exhibits a commitment to integrating insights from diverse data sources, such as economic forecasts, social trends, and environmental factors to create comprehensive analyses that inform decision-making at the ministries, departments, and organisations.
Actively engages in transparent dialogue to evaluate the potential impact of strategic decisions on stakeholders, ensuring alignment with ethical standards and organisational values.
Ensures strategic alignment of decisions with national initiatives such as Aatma Nirbhar Bharat, instilling a sense of national commitment, and encouraging the team to prioritise sustainable development and citizen welfare.
Engages with key stakeholders to collaboratively articulate a shared vision that reflects national priorities, fostering open communication and building consensus.
Exhibits a commitment to continuous improvement by regularly monitoring and assessing the effectiveness of strategies in achieving desired outcomes, making necessary adjustments to stay aligned with evolving national goals.
Adopts cutting-edge technologies (such as machine learning algorithms, natural language processing, blockchain, etc.) to enhance logical reasoning and innovates the accuracy of decision-making processes. Employs advanced risk management techniques, such as predictive modelling, to enhance the robustness of decision making.
 I align strategic decisions with national priorities using technology to improve decision making across M/D/Os.
I employ advanced risk management techniques to identify and mitigate potential risks, enhancing the robustness of decision-making and ensuring alignment with evolving organisational and national goals.
I promote transparency and accountability by clearly communicating strategic decisions and facilitating collaborative input from diverse teams.

theme_description: Possess the ability to analyse facts, reports, policies, precedents, constraints, risks, and conflicting points of view in a comprehensive and logical manner to gain a holistic perspective and arrive at a timely decision. It involves weighing the pros and cons of various options to arrive at the best possible decision that would lead to the welfare of citizens and contribute towards the attainment of Aatma Nirbhar & Viksit Bharat.
sub_theme_description: Ability to make well-informed, rational, and balanced decisions based on a thorough analysis of available information, careful consideration of potential consequences, and alignment with ethical principles and M/D/O goals

proficiency_levels.label: Gathers facts and understands rules to make clear and responsible decisions
proficiency_levels.description:
Collects relevant information from reports, policies, and procedures to assess the situation (for e.g., by looking at past performance reviews, work allocation orders, and documented citizen feedback).
Demonstrates an understanding of M/D/O goals and values and applies them to everyday decision-making.
Comprehends and communicates the reasons for decisions taken based on sound judgements with the team clearly and transparently, and takes actions accordingly.
Identifies scope of own authority for judgement and decision making and escalates to the appropriate level if necessary.
Applies ethical principles and guidelines, ensuring that decisions align with M/D/O rules and the welfare of citizens.
Demonstrates accountability by documenting decision-making processes, keeping records of information sources, and seeking guidance when uncertain. Uses digital tools, such as data entry systems (such as dashboards, government portals, etc), personnel management systems (such as eHRMIS, Keka, etc), project management software (such as e-PMS, ClickUp, Trello, etc), among others to ensure accountability.
 I actively gather and review relevant information from official sources to stay informed and make better decisions.
I make informed decisions aligned with organisational goals and values, and communicate them transparently to stakeholders.
I leverage digital tools to ensure that my decisions and judgments prioritise the welfare of citizens.

proficiency_levels.label: Analyses risks and trade offs to make timely and balanced judgments in complex situations
proficiency_levels.description:
Analyses detailed reports and cross-departmental data to identify trends, opportunities and challenges from various sources (e.g., DPRs, dashboards, departmental reports) including internal and external environments to suggest timely solutions based on applicable rules and guidelines
Identifies risks by reviewing precedents and standard operating procedures (for e.g., by adjusting timelines and cost factors based on past project completion rates)
Anticipates the impacts and risks of decisions and actions, for various stakeholders (for e.g., by understanding internal and stakeholder requirements, considering cultural and ethical factors, considering hypotheticals, encouraging collaboration, etc).
Coordinates and engages with focus groups, team leads, and experts (such as academics, policymakers, civil society representatives, etc) to get additional information to make sound judgments and decisions.
Proposes feasible solutions and demonstrates decisiveness even when dealing with uncertainty, limited information, and under pressure, for example, when facing a sensitive situation, aligning with policy trends in a field, etc.
Monitors the impact of decisions and judgments on society by conducting analyses such as social cost-benefit analysis, counterfactual analysis, impact measurement and appraisal, etc.
Evaluates competing views and decisions to generate strategic ways forward that meet M/D/O goals and communicates these at a strategic level to ensure accountability. Promotes the use of data analytics tools (such as Excel, Power BI, etc), personnel management systems (such as HRMIS, Keka, etc), and project management software (such as e-PMS, Click Up, Trello, etc) to ensure transparency and accountability.
 I analyse trends, opportunities, challenges, and M/D/O practices to provide timely, well-informed recommendations that meet the needs of the concerned stakeholders.
I anticipate the impact and risks of decisions and actions to support stakeholders in making informed choices.
I monitor the social impacts of decisions, evaluate outcomes, and communicate them to stakeholders and leadership to ensure accountability.

proficiency_levels.label: Guides strategic decisions by navigating complexity with clarity, ethics, and foresight
proficiency_levels.description:
Assesses complex and ambiguous data to provide clarity of thinking and direction for the M/D/O, for efficient citizen-centric service delivery.
Assesses political and legal constraints, as well as national objectives, to develop strategies that positively impact the public good, especially for marginalised and disadvantaged groups (such as providing information and education through comprehensive programs, ensuring freedom of choice, avoiding government paternalism, amending law, regulation, and agency practices, reducing information asymmetries, etc.) ensuring that judgments are inclusive and consider these constraints while aligning with M/D/O goals and ethical guidelines
Promotes risk management strategies across M/D/O and provides unbiased, ethical advice to Ministers, ensuring alignment with M/D/O goals (for e.g., by identifying risks, improving preparedness capacity, ensuring increased financial resilience, or using tools such as the Fiscal Risk Matrix, a Contingent Liabilities Management Strategy, etc).
Leads high-level stakeholder consultations (for eg, between ministers, cabinet secretaries, the senior leadership of the M/D/O, etc with citizen groups, civil society, etc.), balancing ethical considerations and goals of the M/D/O.
Promotes M/D/O-wide adoption of emerging technologies like AI, IoT, big data, etc for evidence-based- decision-making. Demonstrates accountability by setting up monitoring frameworks (such as National Program and Project Management Policy Framework, Output Outcome Monitoring Framework, etc) and audit systems (for e.g., financial audits, social audits, etc).
 I develop comprehensive strategies by analysing complex and ambiguous data, which helps provide clarity and direction for my team and stakeholders.
I provide unbiased, ethical advice by assessing risks, using evidence and emerging technologies, and aligning decisions with M/D/O goals.
I conduct high-level consultations with key stakeholders to foster inclusive and sound decision-making, ensuring that all voices are heard and considered in the process.

theme_description: Establishes plans, defines milestones, and allots resources for regularly producing high-quality, cost-effective results that are in accordance with the department's or ministry's overall objectives. Focuses on tasks that will increase effectiveness, efficiency, and production through planning, intentional effort, and control. Determines goals, assigns tasks, and establishes priorities based on skill levels and the availability of resources.
sub_theme_description: Demonstrates the ability to effectively manage tasks and reorder priorities in order to make the most use of available resources.

proficiency_levels.label: Organises tasks and follows established priorities of the team or the M/D/O
proficiency_levels.description:
Understands how timely completion of tasks contributes to the team's effectiveness and effective citizen service delivery. Identifies and lists assigned tasks from supervisor briefings and other meetings, using simple tools such as to-do lists or eOffice, ensuring clarity on responsibilities and timelines.
Adheres to relevant SOPs, timelines, and resource requirements for assigned tasks, ensuring compliance with M/D/O norms and accurate execution of responsibilities.
Seeks clarification from supervisors when priorities conflict or instructions are unclear, demonstrating willingness to learn.
Organises personal work materials, digital files, and notes systematically in eOffice or shared drives for quick retrieval.
Reports progress regularly and flags anticipated delays to supervisors in a timely manner, ensuring transparency and accountability in daily work.
Recognises how own tasks are linked with others’ work (for e.g., file processing depending on prior approvals) and shows adaptability by adjusting task sequence to accommodate urgent work (for e.g., processing pension releases before routine file review).
Performs assigned tasks with attention to detail and timeliness, ensuring that critical citizen-facing services (for e.g., RTI replies, grievance closures, etc) are completed within deadlines. Uses simple digital tools (for e.g., calendar alerts, e-Office workflow, or WhatsApp reminders) to stay organised, manage task timelines, and ensure timely completion of work. I organise and complete my tasks on time by following instructions and processes.
I provide updates proactively and seek clarification on tasks to avoid delays.
I adapt to changing priorities while maintaining service continuity for citizens.

proficiency_levels.label: Manages multiple demands with fairness and efficiency
proficiency_levels.description:
Determines the necessary nature of activities and allocates the efficient level of resources needed to achieve both short- and long-term goals, ensuring alignment with M/D/O priorities. Organises team meetings to review priorities, discuss progress, and align on next steps, ensuring coordination and clarity across team members.
Maintains commitment while coordinating multiple tasks and competing priorities, using available resources efficiently.
Develops short-term contingency plans (for e.g., alternate delivery routes, staff rotations, etc) to manage potential disruptions (for e.g., strikes, floods, or IT downtime), mitigating risks, maintaining priorities, and ensuring continuity of service delivery.
Proactively coordinates with colleagues, M/D/Os, and external stakeholders (for e.g., district offices, line departments, vendors) to anticipate and resolve potential scheduling or resource conflicts, ensuring timely completion of tasks.
Negotiates with supervisors or M/D/Os to adjust timelines, budgets, or scope of work in response to changing external conditions, ensuring work remains realistic and deliverables are met.
Allocates available resources equitably, ensuring that critical citizen-facing functions (for e.g., DBT transfers, grievance closures) are prioritised during periods of constraint or high demand.
Monitors progress against defined milestones and takes timely corrective action when deviations occur by using available resources and tools (for e.g., team support, eOffice trackers) to ensure work is completed efficiently and on time. Maintains documentation of key risks and dependencies (for e.g., procurement delays, interdepartmental approvals, etc) and reports them early to enable timely resolution and informed decision making. I coordinate with my team to set clear priorities and ensure team efforts are aligned with M/D/O’s goals.
I adjust plans and resources proactively based on risks, progress, and service needs.
I build a transparent, accountable work environment where priorities are understood and met.

proficiency_levels.label: Leads strategic prioritisation and institutionalises effective planning practices
proficiency_levels.description:
Evaluates and aligns departmental priorities with broader national and state initiatives (for e.g., Viksit Bharat, PM Gati Shakti, etc), ensuring resources target high-impact, citizen-centric outcomes. Institutionalises organisation-wide planning frameworks and review mechanisms (for e.g., quarterly planning cycles, e-Samiksha dashboards, NITI’s Output-Outcome Monitoring Framework, eSamiksha, or PlanPlus, etc.) to strengthen agility, accountability, and transparency in departmental performance management.
Designs innovative approaches to planning and task sequencing (for e.g., clustering related activities to avoid duplication, or piloting a step before scaling across the project) to enable the organisation to achieve its long-term objectives with agility.
Mentors staff in applying foresight to anticipate challenges, balancing competing demands, and developing behaviours that enable teams to take ownership of goals, align priorities, and deliver results effectively and efficiently.
Institutionalise the use of data and citizen feedback for decision making by analysing performance dashboards, Sevottam/CPGRAMS grievance data, and citizen satisfaction surveys before setting priorities.
Negotiates with stakeholders to align priorities, allocate resources effectively, and build consensus (via joint task forces, etc.) on shared plans that support the M/D/O’s strategic objectives.
Champions a culture of accountability and agility by setting clear standards for quality, transparency, and sustainable work practices, thereby enhancing efficiency and strengthening institutional capacity.
Benchmarks departmental planning practices against national and international frameworks (for e.g., OECD Results-Based Management Framework, UNDP Foresight Playbook) to embed forward-looking, evidence-based approaches in planning and review processes. Standardises templates, documentation, and reporting formats across the M/D/O to promote consistency and streamlining of planning practices for greater efficiency and institutional learning. I align departmental planning systems with national goals and citizen priorities.
I institutionalise data-driven frameworks that ensure flexibility, inclusivity, and transparency in planning and prioritisation.
I strengthen institutional capacity by mentoring teams, embedding innovation, and institutionalising citizen-centric planning and prioritisation practices.

theme_description: Demonstrates expertise in managing various processes and procedures related to establishment and human resource management, including manpower planning for efficient and optimal staffing, as well as managing service and personnel matters such as holding DPCs, managing promotions, pay fixation, allowances, transfers, postings, deputations, resignations, retirement, pension papers, employee grievances, reservations for various cadres, grades, and groups of services, and preventing sexual harassment within the Department or Ministry. Recognizes the accountability to provide prompt, accurate, and concise responses to employee queries by referring comprehensively to various FRSR, related rules, acts, policies, executive orders, etc., to satisfy government employees and mitigate factors that could lead to grievances or administrative tribunal cases.
sub_theme: Handling Matters of Prevention of Sexual Harassment (PoSH) Policy
sub_theme_description: Demonstrates understanding and knowledge of the clauses, processes, and procedures outlined in The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013. Takes appropriate measures to address any violation of the policy for promoting a respectful and inclusive work environment. Ensure Internal Complaints Committee formulation.

proficiency_levels.label: Demonstrates awareness of PoSH provisions and maintains compliant, respectful workplace conduct
proficiency_levels.description:
Explains and understands the key provisions of the PoSH Act, 2013 (for e.g., including definition of “aggrieved woman”, “workplace”, “sexual harassment”, etc) and the role of the Internal Committee (IC), during team discussions or training sessions.
Understands behaviours that constitute sexual harassment by recalling legal definitions and examples from the PoSH Act and organisational policy, thereby building conceptual clarity and preventing unintentional misconduct.
Recognises inappropriate verbal, non-verbal, physical, or digital conduct (including emails, WhatsApp groups, official social media use) and refrains from forwarding or endorsing inappropriate content on official platforms.
Differentiates acceptable and unacceptable workplace behaviours by referring to organisational Code of Conduct, DoPT guidelines, and departmental PoSH Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
Describes the M/D/Os PoSH framework and reporting mechanisms by demonstrating awareness of complaint procedures, escalation channels, and the role of the Internal Committee, facilitating appropriate responses when concerns arise.
Recognises the impact of inappropriate behaviour on individuals and the workplace by acknowledging psychological, emotional, and professional consequences (for e.g., reduced morale, absenteeism, reputational risk to the Department, etc), reinforcing empathy and accountability during PoSH trainings or team briefings.
Demonstrates respectful, gender-sensitive, and professional conduct through appropriate language and workplace boundaries (for e.g., using formal communication in e-Office noting and emails, avoiding personal remarks, ensuring equitable participation in meetings, etc), contributing to an inclusive and dignified work environment.
Avoids participating in or normalising behaviours that may enable harassment by refraining from inappropriate commentary, humour, gestures, or complicity, reducing tolerance for misconduct. Complies with mandatory PoSH orientation and sensitisation programmes, including iGOT Karmayogi gender sensitisation modules and departmental training sessions, ensuring updated awareness. I identify and avoid behaviours that constitute sexual harassment under the PoSH Act and departmental policy.
I maintain respectful, gender-sensitive conduct and safeguard confidentiality in workplace interactions.
I follow prescribed PoSH reporting mechanisms and participate in sensitisation initiatives.

proficiency_levels.label: Applies PoSH procedures sensitively and ensures fair, confidential handling of concerns
proficiency_levels.description:
Applies PoSH principles and M/D/O procedures when handling concerns, referencing relevant policies and legal obligations to ensure consistency and procedural correctness.
Responds empathetically and without judgment to disclosures or complaints by listening attentively, calmly, and respectfully, fostering psychological safety and trust.
Maintains strict confidentiality by limiting information sharing to authorised Internal Committee members, protecting dignity and preventing retaliation or stigma.
Analyses the seriousness of cases to determine appropriate escalation in accordance with departmental workflow matrices and DoPT Office Memoranda.
Responds empathetically to disclosures by listening calmly, documenting concerns accurately using prescribed complaint recording formats, upholding fairness and neutrality.
Guides aggrieved individuals on formal complaint filing procedures, clarifying rights, protections against retaliation, and inquiry stages under the PoSH Rules, 2013.
Encourages responsible use of formal reporting mechanisms by guiding individuals toward designated complaint channels, strengthening institutional accountability.
Supports PoSH awareness and prevention initiatives within teams by participating in training, discussions, and communication efforts, reinforcing a respectful workplace culture.
Models ethical, inclusive, and professional conduct through consistent behaviour and communication, positively influencing team norms. Assumes responsibility for maintaining a safe workplace climate by constructively addressing inappropriate remarks or behaviours, discouraging normalisation of misconduct. I respond sensitively and guide individuals through prescribed PoSH reporting and inquiry procedures.
I ensure confidentiality, fairness, and adherence to statutory timelines while handling complaints.
I promote preventive awareness and discourage normalisation of misconduct within my team.

proficiency_levels.label: Strengthens M/D/O PoSH implementation, ensuring legal compliance and sustained culture change
proficiency_levels.description:
Evaluates M/D/O compliance by reviewing inquiry records, timelines, annual reports, and documentation standards, ensuring alignment with PoSH Act, DoPT guidelines, and Ministry instructions. Oversees fair and unbiased inquiry processes by applying principles of natural justice, ensuring opportunity to be heard, neutral assessment of evidence, and reasoned recommendations.
Validates confidentiality and documentation standards by monitoring access controls, record accuracy, and information handling practices, preventing breaches and M/D/O risk.
Supports the design and implementation of preventive and corrective PoSH strategies by analysing M/D/O risks, behavioural and cultural patterns, and systemic gaps, reducing incidents and vulnerabilities.
Builds the capacity of Internal Committee members and stakeholders by enabling training on legal compliance, inquiry techniques, and trauma-informed approaches, strengthening institutional competence.
Monitors trends, feedback, and data related to PoSH implementation by interpreting complaints, assessments, and audits, driving continuous improvement.
Advises leadership on policy refinement and systemic improvements by translating compliance insights into governance and organisational actions. Represents M/D/O integrity in audits, reviews, and external engagements by articulating compliance measures and ethical commitments. I implement PoSH processes and inquiry mechanisms in line with legal requirements and principles of natural justice.
I evaluate the effectiveness of organisational PoSH systems, awareness initiatives, and risk-prevention measures.
I champion accountability, gender equity, and a culture of safety and dignity across the M/D/O.

theme_description: Ensures citizens’ welfare and satisfaction by improving the standards of accountable and transparent governance, implementing result-oriented administration through innovative interventions based on design thinking, and enhancing citizen-centric decision-making. Implements Open Government policies and practices, which include collaborating and forming partnerships with informed citizens, leveraging social capital, and promoting participative public service delivery by ensuring freedom and ease of access to information. Establish an efficient framework that ensures the timely and transparent delivery of services by various government departments through awareness of various social, political, economic and technological developments that may impact citizens.
sub_theme_description: Demonstrates ability to decode intertwined administrative systems, understand dynamic and multifaceted situations, based on a solid foundation of study of need & demand of target population. Approaches problems with an empathic, “beginner’s mind”, openness, & optimism for creative and human-centered solutions. Follows a systematic and conscious approach to public service delivery that involves being open and impartial to the perspectives, grievances, and recommendations of service users and stakeholders, especially those from diverse social groups.

proficiency_levels.label: Understands citizen needs and service touchpoints using basic design thinking tools
proficiency_levels.description:
Understands basic needs, expectations, and grievances of service users/citizens by reviewing available data (e.g., CPGRAMS entries, service registers, Citizen Charters, surveys, or field interaction notes) and evidence to ground problem understanding in lived citizen realities rather than assumptions.
Engages with citizens using basic empathy and inquiry techniques (e.g., structured questioning, attentive listening, neutral note-taking) to accurately capture experiences, concerns, and suggestions without bias.
Identifies key stakeholders and citizen touchpoints across administrative processes by mapping basic services to pinpoint where the citizen experience is shaped or constrained.
Collects feedback, grievances, and suggestions through surveys, helpdesks, public consultations, or field interactions, ensuring citizen voices inform early problem understanding.
Observes service delivery processes and frontline interactions during field visits or reviews to recognise practical bottlenecks and citizen pain points in real-world settings.
Documents citizen needs, grievances, and service gaps in a structured manner to support transparency and informed discussion within the administrative system of the department. Follows prescribed design processes, tools, or templates for need assessment and problem definition (e.g., using standard empathy maps, service journey templates, or problem identification tools) under supervision, ensuring consistency and methodological rigour in citizen-centric initiatives. I gather and document citizen needs, expectations, and grievances to inform an initial understanding of service delivery challenges.
I identify key stakeholders and service touchpoints to highlight where the citizen experience is most affected.
I apply empathy and prescribed design tools to support structured, citizen-informed problem definition.

proficiency_levels.label: Analyses citizen needs and administrative systems to design and refine inclusive service solutions
proficiency_levels.description:
Analyses qualitative and quantitative data (e.g., CPGRAMS grievance trends, departmental MIS dashboards, service delivery reports, field survey findings, and RTI query patterns) to differentiate between expressed demand of citizens and underlying needs, enabling interventions to address root causes rather than symptoms. Analyses cross-departmental policy and process interactions using system-mapping and frontline inputs to surface systemic bottlenecks, misaligned incentives, and coordination gaps.
Reframes administrative or service challenges into citizen-centred problem statements using evidence and stakeholder inputs, to enable more relevant and impactful solutions.
Synthesises and integrates inputs from citizens, frontline staff, civil society, and partner agencies, balancing competing viewpoints, including documenting trade-offs and their rationale to arrive at inclusive and practical design choices.
Designs and compares alternative service delivery or policy solutions by developing and assessing options (e.g., simplified procedures, single-window delivery, digital vs assisted modes, etc) to assess feasibility, inclusiveness, and citizen impact.
Evaluates proposed solutions against administrative feasibility, equity considerations, and expected citizen outcomes to ensure responsible and implementable innovations.
Applies participatory mechanisms such as co-creation workshops, pilots, or feedback loops, to strengthen citizen ownership and responsiveness of services.
Refines designs using citizen and stakeholder feedback during pilots or early implementation, to improve service quality and user satisfaction. Analyses how administrative, policy, and resource constraints (approval hierarchies, restrictive eligibility rules, non-integrated systems, and staffing or budget limitations) affect service delivery, explaining why certain citizen issues persist despite the intent. I analyse data and stakeholder inputs to address the root causes of service delivery challenges.
I design,compare and assess alternative service or policy solutions to improve feasibility, inclusiveness, and citizen experience.
I pilot and refine solutions using citizen feedback to enhance service quality and responsiveness.

proficiency_levels.label: Leads system-wide adoption of design thinking to reform policies and scale citizen-centric service models
proficiency_levels.description:
Synthesises citizen insights, grievance patterns, and service performance data across social, economic, political, and technological dimensions to decode complex administrative systems.
Anticipates future citizen needs and service delivery challenges by tracking societal trends, policy shifts, and technological developments, and assessing their implications for access, equity, and service experience enabling proactive public service design.
Creates scalable and inclusive service delivery models (for e.g., single-window service systems, assisted or hybrid digital delivery models, decentralised outreach mechanisms, or redesigned grievance redressal processes) grounded in design thinking principles to ensure solutions are citizen-responsive and equitable.
Institutionalises design thinking processes/ practices by embedding citizen research, journey mapping, piloting, and feedback loops into departmental guidelines and decision making processes to mainstream participatory service delivery.
Influences and shapes policy formulation and governance reforms by translating citizen insights, grievance trends, and pilot evidence into policy briefs, design notes, and reform recommendations for senior leadership to inform decisions that reflect citizen realities.
Champions Open Government principles by promoting transparent access to service information, enabling sustained citizen collaboration in service design to enhance accountability and participative public service delivery.
Builds organisational and ecosystem capability by developing leaders, mentoring teams, and institutional partners in design thinking approaches (e.g., Stanford’s 5-stage model, IDEO’s Human-Centered Design, Double Diamond model, etc.) and setting quality standards for citizen-centric problem solving.
Leads partnerships with civil society, academia, technology partners, and community groups to leverage social capital and complementary expertise to co-create solutions that expand service reach, improve responsiveness, and generate public value at scale. Evaluates long-term outcomes of citizen-centric interventions using service performance, equity, and satisfaction indicators, and leads the scaling or replication of successful models across departments or sectors, to improve governance effectiveness and strengthen citizen trust. I translate citizen insights and system-level evidence into scalable service delivery models and policy reform recommendations.
I embed design thinking and participatory practices into organisational processes, guidelines, and decision-making frameworks.
I lead partnerships and build organisational capacity to sustain citizen-centric innovation and strengthen trust in public service delivery.

theme_description: Ensures citizens’ welfare and satisfaction by improving the standards of accountable and transparent governance, implementing result-oriented administration through innovative interventions based on design thinking, and enhancing citizen-centric decision-making. Implements Open Government policies and practices, which include collaborating and forming partnerships with informed citizens, leveraging social capital, and promoting participative public service delivery by ensuring freedom and ease of access to information. Establish an efficient framework that ensures the timely and transparent delivery of services by various government departments through awareness of various social, political, economic and technological developments that may impact citizens.
sub_theme_description: Demonstrates proficiency in mediating and engaging with various segments and groups of society to establish a common ground on issues and actions that benefit the entire community. Display “Good Governance” by aiming to enhance effectiveness, efficiency, and accountability through a consensus-based approach that emphasizes equity, inclusivity, and active participation, resulting in increased public satisfaction at lower costs.

proficiency_levels.label: Applies foundational citizen engagement processes to ensure responsive, inclusive, and timely service delivery
proficiency_levels.description:
Identifies different citizen groups (for eg., women, senior citizens, youth, beneficiaries, vulnerable communities) and recognises their everyday service delivery needs (for e.g., delays in accessing healthcare or pensions) and concerns.
Demonstrates basic understanding of good governance principles such as transparency, accountability, inclusivity, and participation, and explains how these principles apply to day-to-day service delivery.
Understands and uses citizen engagement tools, including digital platforms such as CPGRAMS, MyGov, RTI Online, Jan Sunwai, as well as outreach campaigns, to gather feedback and enable participative and responsive service delivery.
Records, classifies, and summarises citizen feedback related to service gaps (for e.g., complaints about service delays, lack of access to information, etc) to facilitate targeted follow-up and ensure responsive public service delivery.
Tracks service delivery indicators (for e.g., grievance disposal rate, turnaround time, repeat complaints, etc) using departmental dashboards or CPGRAMS analytics.
Uses basic communication methods (for e.g., notices, SMS alerts, social media posts, or public announcements) to inform citizens about schemes, services, or timelines.
Assists in organising or supporting participatory activities such as awareness drives, Gram Sabha meetings, or service camps to encourage citizen involvement in government initiatives. Demonstrates awareness of how social, economic, or technological changes (such as digital access or scheme modifications) may affect citizens’ ability to engage with government services. I systematically capture and document citizen needs using prescribed platforms and formats.
I support outreach activities that improve citizen awareness and service access.
I ensure grievances are registered, routed, and resolved within the prescribed timelines.

proficiency_levels.label: Implements structured citizen engagement processes to strengthen responsive and accountable service delivery
proficiency_levels.description:
Reviews social, economic, or technological developments (for e.g., digital access gaps or scheme changes) against GIGW/ WGAC guidelines to assess their immediate implications for citizen engagement and service access.
Analyses citizen feedback from multiple sources (for e.g., CPGRAMS data, RTI trends, social media analytics, field reports, etc) to identify recurring service delivery issues, access barriers, and trust gaps affecting different community groups.
Examines community-level issues by identifying root causes of service disruptions and proposes corrective actions to the concerned department.
Designs and facilitates structured forums (for e.g., consultations, workshops, listening sessions) with clear agendas and RACI, to enable transparent decision making.
Applies participatory tools and behavioural nudges (for e.g., reminders for vaccination drives, visual dashboards for budgeting, simplified information materials, etc) to increase awareness, participation, and accountability of citizens.
Applies relevant good governance standards (for e.g., Open Government principles, result-oriented frameworks, SDG-linked approaches, etc) to design inclusive and transparent engagement initiatives.
Prepares analytical summaries and learning notes on citizen engagement outcomes to inform supervisory review and service delivery improvements. Collaborates with community representatives, local bodies, NGOs, and frontline workers to co-develop practical solutions addressing identified service access or delivery challenges. I analyse citizen engagement data to identify systemic service gaps and recommend corrective measures.
I design and facilitate structured consultations that build consensus and improve equitable access to services.
I translate citizen feedback into documented improvements in service delivery and accountability mechanisms.

proficiency_levels.label: Institutionalises citizen engagement systems to drive responsive, inclusive, and equitable public service delivery
proficiency_levels.description:
Anticipates emerging social, economic, technological, and governance trends affecting citizens and integrates them into long-term strategies for citizen engagement that promote equity, trust, and participation. Leverages behavioural, socio-economic, and digital insights (for e.g., digital access surveys, income distribution reports, or migration patterns, etc) to design institutional frameworks that enable sustained citizen participation in service planning, welfare schemes, and governance initiatives.
Champions innovative initiatives that broaden citizen participation (for e.g., fintech-based micro-insurance for farmers or technology-enabled grievance redressal platforms integrating mobile apps with community facilitators) to enhance service responsiveness and public trust.
Establishes cross-sector partnerships with civil society, academia, and the private sector institutions to co-create solutions addressing complex, multi-dimensional governance challenges
Leads inter-departmental collaboration by establishing platforms for knowledge exchange and joint problem-solving on citizen-centric priorities (for e.g., healthcare access, financial inclusion, and education equity, etc).
Embeds and governs structured feedback loops that link citizen inputs to policy refinement, programme redesign, and organisational learning.
Guides and mentors teams to institutionalise participatory governance practices across all community groups by modelling and reinforcing values of equity, inclusion, accountability,
Aligns citizen engagement strategies with broader governance goals such as sustainable development, inclusive growth, and digital transformation, ensuring that service delivery remains outcome-driven and community-responsive.
Drives system-wide reduction in grievance recurrence and service delivery costs through process simplification, digitisation, and performance benchmarking. I institutionalise structured citizen engagement systems aligned with governance priorities and equity principles.
I lead cross-sector collaboration platforms that resolve complex, service delivery challenges.
I embed transparent feedback and performance metrics that improve citizen trust while reducing service delivery costs.

theme_description: Ensures citizens’ welfare and satisfaction by improving the standards of accountable and transparent governance, implementing result-oriented administration through innovative interventions based on design thinking, and enhancing citizen-centric decision-making. Implements Open Government policies and practices, which include collaborating and forming partnerships with informed citizens, leveraging social capital, and promoting participative public service delivery by ensuring freedom and ease of access to information. Establish an efficient framework that ensures the timely and transparent delivery of services by various government departments through awareness of various social, political, economic and technological developments that may impact citizens.
sub_theme_description: Maintains awareness of the national political leadership's vision for the country, as well as its strategic communications and collaborations with various national and global entities revolving around the economic, social or technological domains, in relation to the Department/Ministry/Organisation.

proficiency_levels.label: Recognises relevant PEST signals and uses them to anchor frontline service delivery
proficiency_levels.description:
Identifies key political priorities (for e.g., Viksit Bharat 2047), major economic trends (for e.g., inflation updates, Economic Survey insights), relevant social issues, and basic track of technological advancements (for eg. Generative AI). Demonstrates awareness of key policy documents, press releases, government orders and other publications of the M/D/O (for eg. Economic surveys, budget releases, etc) and any changes to the same.
Identifies the implications of changes to policies, circulars, and departmental priorities for frontline service beneficiaries.
Understands at a basic level how citizen needs, expectations, or access to services may change due to developments such as inflation, migration, digitisation of services, or social inclusion initiatives.
Recognises linkages between departmental schemes or programmes and broader national, sectoral, or mission-level priorities, and aligns day-to-day work accordingly. Applies awareness of PEST factors to ensure timely, accurate, and citizen-sensitive execution of frontline service delivery. I identify relevant political, economic, social, and technological developments and stay informed on advancements.
I recognise how changes in policies, budgets, or technology affect citizen access to services and scheme delivery.
I align my work with current national priorities and official directions to support citizen-centric outcomes.

proficiency_levels.label: Analyses PEST signals to adapt programmes, processes, and service delivery for improved citizen outcomes
proficiency_levels.description:
Analyses departmental data and dashboards to identify PEST-driven risks or opportunities (for e.g., a sudden drop in beneficiaries in a district, spike in commodity prices, social unrest, etc) to demand, access and equity in services and makes implementation adjustments where required. Interprets budget announcements, policy reforms, sectoral strategies, and technological shifts to anticipate operational, delivery, or implementation challenges.
Summarises key political, economic, or social developments into short internal briefs or talking points for supervisors.
Advises supervisors or teams on required adjustments in programme design, timelines, communication strategies, or implementation approaches basis PEST insights.
Aligns departmental initiatives with inter-ministerial priorities, state-level developments, or national missions affecting citizens.
Displays anticipation and political foresight by spotting possible political shocks, risk analysis of political, social and technological developments and developing suitable risk mitigation strategies.
Conducts stakeholder mapping to identify key actors in key PEST developments, and incorporates their inputs into implementation plans. Draws on lessons from other states, ministries, or countries facing similar PEST contexts and adapts relevant practices. For eg., is able to adapt Assam’s flood outreach model from Bihar’s early warning pilot. I analyse political, economic, social, and technological trends to assess their impact on departmental programmes and citizen services.
I recommend practical adjustments to policies, processes, or delivery approaches based on emerging external developments.
I support informed decision making by linking national priorities and sectoral trends with on-ground service delivery realities.

proficiency_levels.label: Embeds PEST analysis in policymaking to protect citizen services and drive adaptive, future-ready governance
proficiency_levels.description:
Guides department to embed PEST analysis into programme design, monitoring frameworks, reviews, and policy formulation processes.
Engages with inter-ministerial, state, or external stakeholders to enable coordinated responses to complex, cross-cutting political, economic, social, or technological challenges.
Anticipates long-term PEST trends and integrates strategic foresight into departmental planning to safeguard citizen outcomes amid uncertainty or change.
Strengthens institutional capacity by ensuring that external developments are translated into clear priorities, adaptive strategies, and citizen-centric outcomes.
Benchmarks departmental policies against national and global best practices, using platforms such as UNDP, G20, OECD Public Governance Reviews to guide departmental alignment.
Anticipates and influences long-term political, social, economic, and technological trends by conducting strategic foresight exercises (for e.g., scenario planning, trend mapping, rapid horizon scans, etc) across electoral cycles, demographic transitions, climate shocks, or disruptive technologies.
Promotes citizen-centricity by ensuring departmental strategies reflect national priorities and by communicating external developments in a clear, actionable manner.
Builds coalitions and exercises stakeholder influence—including national leadership, state/district partners, and civil society—to protect citizen interests in politically sensitive contexts, while institutionalising learning loops by using citizen feedback (e.g., Sevottam/NeSDA), and audits. Communicates PEST insights through actionable advisories for senior leadership, inter‑ministerial groups, or citizen‑facing campaigns. I integrate PEST considerations into long-term departmental strategies and strengthen institutional mechanisms for sustained adoption.
I champion interoperable digital platforms and resource‑optimised models that maximise citizen impact.
I communicate PEST insights effectively and build cross-sectoral coalitions to advance national and departmental goals while maintaining administrative impartiality.

theme_description: Demonstrates the capacity to detect gaps and improvement needs in existing policies in order to translate policy concepts into policy formulation for addressing existing and emerging needs of the citizens. Conducts thorough study and analysis of best practices at State, National, or Global levels, takes advantage of modern innovation and the most recent advancements in the social, economic, technological, and legal spheres while creating & implementing policies. Focuses on monitoring the application of policy and evaluating its impact and efficacy using a variety of instruments for responsible, open, and sustainable governance.
sub_theme_description: Demonstrates the ability to draft or amend government policies for delivering citizen-centric civil service basis feasibility analysis and risk assessment of various policy alternatives.

proficiency_levels.label: Supports drafting and amendment of policies in line with prescribed regulations
proficiency_levels.description:
Understands key concepts and principles of policy design/amendment (for e.g., agenda setting, policy tools, regulatory instruments, etc) and stakeholder engagement, to contribute to drafting processes.
Maintains updated records of draft notes, file movements, and approvals using tools such as e-Office or trackers to ensure tracking and compliance during policy drafting or amendment.
Recognises and refers to relevant clauses from current laws, policies, and scheme frameworks to support policy amendments, ensuring alignment with regulatory provisions (for e.g., IT Act , RTI rules, etc.)
Follows the prescribed steps and timelines in the policy amendment processes (for e.g., file submission, legal review, inter-ministerial consultation, etc) and supports timely preparation of required documents, flagging pending actions to supervisors.
Drafts standard official communication related to policy design/processes, such as reminders to states, clarifications on scheme guidelines, or responses to queries following M/D/O approved formats.
Updates draft sections (for e.g., cabinet note, scheme notifications, etc) based on supervisory feedback on legal provisions, and procedural protocols for improved clarity and compliance.
Identifies early-stage risks such as legal gaps, delays in stakeholder responses, or operational bottlenecks and flags them to relevant officials during policy drafting. Applies feasibility checks by reviewing past evaluations, citizen feedback, or scheme data to highlight relevant considerations for proposed amendments. I support drafting and amendment of policies using prescribed procedures.
I incorporate legal references, data inputs, and feasibility considerations into draft notes.
I ensure policy files are documented and processed in accordance with timelines and rules.

proficiency_levels.label: Designs and refines policy proposals using data, feasibility analysis, and stakeholder consultation
proficiency_levels.description:
Defines policy problems using data from scheme MIS, CPGRAMS, audit findings, and evaluation reports.
Implements policy design and amendment by translating strategic directions into actionable proposals in line with existing schemes, laws, and guidelines (for e.g., revising components of schemes like PM Svanidhi in line with the Street Vendor Acts and MoHUA guidelines).
Defines policy gaps by analysing data from various sources such as CPGRAMS , scheme MIS (for e.g., PM Poshan Tracker, UDISE +, or e-Shram), and audit findings to identify procedural bottlenecks and suggest mid-cycle adjustments to policy components to improve performance.
Assesses operational and institutional risks (for e.g., fund leakage, legal challenges, etc) based on field reports, audit findings and stakeholder feedback to inform revisions in policy design or scheme guidelines.
Applies feasibility analysis using tools (for e.g., cost-benefit analysis, implementation risk mapping, resource appraisal, etc) to justify the practicality and long-term sustainability of proposed policy amendments.
Assess current service delivery systems (for e.g., State DBT portals, e-voucher models, third-party partnerships, etc) to recommend policy-level improvements that strengthen last-mile connectivity and inclusion in remote or marginalised regions.
Incorporates field insights from state review missions, evaluation studies (for e.g., NITI Aayog outcome reports, CAG report, etc), or pilot results to propose revisions. Validates policy proposals through structured consultations with stakeholders, including line departments, state nodal officers, and subject matter experts, to verify assumptions and refine proposed designs or amendments for schemes under review. I develop data-backed policy proposals with clear alternatives and risk analysis.
I integrate feasibility, fiscal, and legal considerations into policy amendments.
I strengthen policy design through consultations and field validation.

proficiency_levels.label: Drives policy design by aligning national priorities into integrated, future-ready policy frameworks
proficiency_levels.description:
Embeds risk and feasibility assessment into policy design using multi-source data (for e.g., the NFHS, IndiaStack, Climate Resilience dashboards, etc) to anticipate future risks, demographic shifts, and emerging technologies to inform forward-looking policy design and long-term relevance. Leverages citizen feedback, grievance redress data, and field insights, applying approaches such as human-centred design or behavioural frameworks to co-develop inclusive policy design that addresses implementation gaps and enhance citizen experiences.
Designs integrated policy frameworks using appropriate fiscal, regulatory, and digital instruments to align national missions with institutional mandates and ensure feasibility and scalability.
Formulates evidence-based policy design choices by analysing the problem, defining the solution, and justifying the rationale for selected delivery mechanisms, to provide a clear rationale during Cabinet and inter-ministerial reviews.
Leads stakeholder convergence through formal consultation mechanisms and coordination with stakeholders, such as state governments and sectoral experts to shape and co-create policy narratives and ensure alignment with inter-ministerial priorities.
Adapts and institutionalises national and international policy innovations such as IndiaStack, JAM Trinity, etc, suited to the M/D/O’s legal, administrative and socio-economic ecosystem to future-proof design architectures. Institutionalises advanced policy practices by integration of real-time data systems relevant to M/D/O (for e.g., PM-KISAN dashboard or Aspirational Districts Programme monitoring) to support course correction, cost optimisation, and impact assessment. I lead the design of integrated and future-ready policy frameworks aligned with national priorities.
I embed risk analysis, innovation, and data-driven insights into policy architecture.
I strengthen policy coherence and sustainability through strategic alignment and review mechanisms.

theme_description: Demonstrates the capacity to detect gaps and improvement needs in existing policies in order to translate policy concepts into policy formulation for addressing existing and emerging needs of the citizens. Conducts thorough study and analysis of best practices at State, National, or Global levels, takes advantage of modern innovation and the most recent advancements in the social, economic, technological, and legal spheres while creating & implementing policies. Focuses on monitoring the application of policy and evaluating its impact and efficacy using a variety of instruments for responsible, open, and sustainable governance.
sub_theme_description: Establishes and implements appropriate procedures to facilitate the implementation of central policies within the context of good governance, such as government programmes, schemes, missions, initiatives, etc.

proficiency_levels.label: Reviews policies, compiles information, and prepares notes and trackers to support policy implementation
proficiency_levels.description:
Reviews relevant government policies, schemes, circulars, notifications, and programme manuals to gain a clear understanding of the guidelines and requirements for policy implementation. Collates relevant information on the policy landscape for context building that includes government priorities, socio-economic indicators, and legal documents (acts/amendments/bylaws) using credible internal and external sources (e.g., Census data, RBI reports, MoSPI surveys, scheme guidelines, etc).
Understands the key components, instruments, and tools required for policy implementation - such as financial allocations, standard operating procedures, and stakeholder consultations- and how they apply to departmental schemes or initiatives
Supports policy implementation activities by handling operational tasks such as preparing and maintaining files, tracking fund disbursal and approvals, compiling inputs from site, etc., ensuring all documentation aligns with procedural standards.
Seeks guidance from supervisors or senior officials to clarify doubts related to policy implementation protocols, reporting templates, or procedural rules, and applies this understanding to effectively support the implementation process.
Drafts structured briefing notes, responses, and reports that summarise implementation progress, highlight procedural bottlenecks, and provide recommendations for senior officials.
Document best practices, challenges, and implementation gaps encountered across the policy lifecycle to inform future improvements, amendments, or the formulation of new policies, as guided by supervisors. Reviews feedback and grievances from audit reports or field implementation notes to understand on-ground gaps in policy delivery, and supports documentation or internal communication to address these gaps. I refer to relevant government circulars, scheme manuals, and notifications to understand policy, scheme, mission objectives and identify the roles, steps, and timelines involved in implementation.
I collect and organise contextual information such as socio-economic data, legal references, and field reports to support planning, file processing, and documentation related to policy implementation.
I prepare notes, trackers, and draft responses that summarise progress and highlight procedural delays or gaps, while seeking guidance to ensure accuracy, compliance, and alignment with implementation protocols.

proficiency_levels.label: Aligns teams and tools to policy objectives, monitors progress, and resolves field level implementation issues
proficiency_levels.description:
Interprets implementation plans and policy objectives to ensure resource alignment, assign responsibilities, and adherence to procedural requirements for effective delivery of schemes, programmes, and initiatives.
Identifies the human, technical and institutional capacities and resources required for implementation, such as financial processes, procurement systems, or partner agencies, and supports alignment between desk and on-ground teams.
Conducts regular reviews of policy implementation trackers, dashboards, and progress reports by synthesising data trends, and flagging emerging gaps to suggest course correction and ensure timely execution.
Engages with internal and external stakeholders (e.g. officials, beneficiaries or partners) to identify on-ground implementation challenges and refines delivery approaches by incorporating field feedback, on-ground learnings, and sector-specific policy guidelines to maintain responsiveness and relevance.
Facilitates team reviews, peer learning spaces, or consultations to share learnings from policy execution, support collaborative problem-solving, and co-develop adaptive tools like reporting systems, real-time dashboards, or feedback mechanisms, enhancing responsiveness and implementation quality.,
Adapts implementation strategies in response to shifting priorities, on-ground evidence, or changes by authorities to realign on timelines, redefining stakeholder responsibilities, or updating reporting formats and procedures.
Identifies inefficiencies or redundancies in current policy implementation processes, such as poor interdepartmental coordination or unclear guidelines, and proposes targeted improvements to streamline workflows, enhance accountability, and optimal use of resources. Considers diverse viewpoints of stakeholders (on-field staff, and beneficiaries) when shaping implementation plans, to foster open communication, mutual trust and ensure that plans are sensitive to local contexts and, inclusive for advancement of the broader agenda of transparent, citizen-centric governance. I create policy implementation plans by interpreting policy objectives, aligning departmental workflows, defining responsibilities, and integrating tools like SOPs, dashboards, reporting templates, site reports, and feedback mechanisms to ensure timely, structured, and adaptive implementation.
I engage with stakeholders to identify on-ground challenges, analyse feedback, and refine delivery strategies, while ensuring implementation processes reflect local contexts, compliance requirements, and departmental priorities.
I review progress data, track implementation performance, and propose improvements such as clarifying responsibilities or streamlining workflows to enhance efficiency, address gaps, and adapt to evolving policy or operational needs.

proficiency_levels.label: Designs implementation frameworks and oversees M/D/O delivery systems
proficiency_levels.description:
Leads the strategic design and institutionalisation of policy implementation frameworks by aligning central/state policy mandates (such as Urban Sustainability Goals or Climate Action Plan ) with local administrative structures (ULBs , PRIs , etc.,) citizen needs, and M/D/O priorities, ensuring feasibility across varied field contexts and effective execution. Oversees policy implementation performance across the M/D/O by delegating responsibilities, and integrating review mechanisms to ensure transparency, accountability, and data-driven decision-making to deliver efficient, equitable, and citizen-centric public services.
Ensures compliance of monitoring mechanisms to track progress against the key performance indicators (e.g., turnaround time, beneficiary reach, process efficiency), and anchors continuous review cycles to drive adaptive improvements across the implementation cycle.
Establishes cross-sectoral (e.g., health, sanitation, agriculture, etc) and inter-ministerial policy networks by engaging with public officials, civil society, academia, and other institutes to advocate for effective policy execution and create enabling environments for convergence and coordination.
Designs strategic interventions by integrating lessons from past implementation cycles, such as scheme audits (CAG reports) or citizen grievances, and recommends course corrections aligned with institutional goals.
Formalise implementation toolkits such as operational manuals, training modules, audit protocols, and performance dashboards and standardise their use across departments to ensure procedural coherence, institutional memory, and ease of replication.
Drives policy-system innovation by leveraging emerging technologies such as AI, geospatial platforms (e.g. - Janmanrega Geo-tagging Platform) and digital public infrastructure (e.g. - PM Gati Shakti portal) and mentoring teams to pilot new approaches in high-priority implementation domains that ensures effective service delivery.
Anticipates systemic risks and builds resilience into the implementation framework, including fallback workflows, compliance protocols, and risk assessment to safeguard continuity in delivery of public services .
