Explores and adapts best practices from national and global contexts, and introduces new implementation models suited to the political, socio-economic, and cultural landscape of the M/D/O’s domain to encourage a culture of innovation. I lead the design and institutionalisation of policy implementation frameworks by aligning national mandates with local delivery systems, citizen needs, and departmental priorities, ensuring operational feasibility across diverse contexts.
I oversee policy implementation performance across the department by defining policy direction, setting up monitoring mechanisms with clear KPIs, integrating review routines, and anchoring data-driven improvements that enhance accountability and delivery outcomes.
I drive innovation in implementation systems by adapting national and global best practices, securing leadership buy-in, and building resilient, citizen-centric models that respond to emerging risks and needs.

theme_description: Demonstrates the capacity to detect gaps and improvement needs in existing policies in order to translate policy concepts into policy formulation for addressing existing and emerging needs of the citizens. Conducts thorough study and analysis of best practices at State, National, or Global levels, takes advantage of modern innovation and the most recent advancements in the social, economic, technological, and legal spheres while creating & implementing policies. Focuses on monitoring the application of policy and evaluating its impact and efficacy using a variety of instruments for responsible, open, and sustainable governance.
sub_theme_description: Creates and implements an effective and practical monitoring & evaluation framework for assessing the impact of policy implementation for maximising the impact and benefits for target stakeholders.

proficiency_levels.label: Applies monitoring frameworks and data tools to support structured policy assessment
proficiency_levels.description:
Understands different types of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, including conceptual, results, and logical frameworks, process, outcome, and impact evaluations, and results-based monitoring and the difference in them.
Identifies indicators using the SMART framework, differentiating between process, output, outcome, and impact indicators, and specifying them for the policy.
Displays awareness of different data collection methods, data quality parameters, and analytical techniques, such as interviews, case studies, statistical modelling, and cost-benefit analysis.
Collects and validates data from field and administrative systems, ensuring they fulfil set data quality standards.
Uses appropriate tools, such as dashboards, briefs, fact sheets, and templates, for documenting and reporting progress to internal and external teams.
Supports the implementation of approved monitoring and evaluation frameworks by accurately applying defined indicators, tools, and reporting formats. Recognises how monitoring findings are used to inform policy learning, implementation improvements, and evidence-based decision-making. I apply approved monitoring and evaluation frameworks accurately to support policy assessment.
I collect and validate data using approved systems and ensure compliance with reporting standards.
I document and report monitoring findings accurately to support structured policy reviews.

proficiency_levels.label: Monitors and assesses policies, analyses outcomes, and recommends actionable improvements
proficiency_levels.description:
Translates policy objectives into measurable outcomes, success metrics, and structured monitoring plans with defined timelines and responsibilities. Operationalises monitoring frameworks using government MIS platforms, dashboards, DBT portals, and sectoral systems (e.g., HMIS, UDISE+, PMIS ) to ensure timely data capture.
Maps stakeholder roles, data dependencies, and accountability mechanisms to strengthen monitoring design and implementation.
Integrates quantitative (for e.g., MIS data, PFMS expenditure data, DBT dashboards, etc), qualitative (for e.g., field interviews, beneficiary feedback, focus groups, etc), and comparative evidence (for e.g., State rankings, NITI Aayog indices, SDG indicators, OECD benchmarks, etc) to assess implementation performance and identify systemic gaps.
Integrates relevant social (equity and inclusion), economic (cost-effectiveness and fiscal efficiency), environmental (sustainability and resource impact), and legal (regulatory and audit compliance) dimensions into monitoring indicators to ensure a comprehensive and accountable assessment of policy performance.
Applies appropriate analytical tools and digital monitoring systems to improve the timeliness and reliability of policy assessment. Prepares structured evaluation briefs highlighting performance, risks, and recommended course corrections aligned with citizen outcomes. I translate policy goals into measurable indicators and structured monitoring systems.
I synthesise multi-source evidence to assess performance, equity, and efficiency of implementation.
I provide actionable, evidence-based recommendations to support accountable policy review and course correction.

proficiency_levels.label: Leads strategic monitoring and impact systems to drive evidence-based policy reform and systemic improvement
proficiency_levels.description:
Designs and institutionalises citizen-centric M&E frameworks, program assessments, and feedback loops to improve policy outcomes of effectiveness, efficiency, equity, and sustainability of public service delivery.
Establishes cross-departmental evaluation standards to ensure comparability, coherence, and data integrity across schemes.
Incorporates advanced analytical methods (for e.g., impact evaluation designs, quasi-experimental methods, predictive analytics, etc) to enhance rigour and reliability of policy monitoring and impact assessment.
Aligns evaluation frameworks with national development goals (for e.g., SDG indicators, Outcome Budget targets, Aspirational District metrics, etc) and applies internationally recognised evaluation standards (for e.g., OECD DAC criteria, results-based management, impact evaluation methods, etc) to ensure rigour, comparability, and credibility.
Identifies emerging fiscal, operational, and equity risks and assesses long-term sustainability to recommend policy redesign, scale-up, modification, or structured phase-out decisions based on evaluation evidence.
Institutionalises continuous learning cycles linking evaluation findings to annual policy reviews and reform initiatives.
Promotes transparency through dissemination of evaluation summaries, dashboards, and performance reports for leadership and public accountability. Guides junior officers in the application of suitable monitoring and evaluation frameworks, tools, and indicators, ensuring consistent data collection, rigorous analysis, and effective use of findings contextualised to the different policies. I institutionalise citizen-centric monitoring systems that improve policy effectiveness, efficiency, and equity.
I align evaluation evidence with strategic decision making and resource allocation to drive reform.
I strengthen transparency, accountability, and continuous learning across policy implementation.

theme_description: Demonstrates comprehension of the significance of Cabinet Notes in policymaking, where the Cabinet and its committees make vital decisions that are crucial for efficient governance. This includes the ability to prepare Cabinet Notes that address various national and international matters affecting different areas of governance and present them to the Cabinet for consideration and decision-making. Therefore, a deep understanding of the AoB Rules, 1961 & ToB Rules, 1961 is essential, along with exceptional skills in preparing comprehensive Cabinet Notes that provide pertinent details and the right perspective.
sub_theme_description: Ensures adherence to the procedures for preparing and submitting papers to be considered by the Cabinet, Cabinet Committees, and Committee of Secretaries (CoS) Notes, including the use of the prescribed format, inclusion of all necessary elements, and appropriate presentation of the Cabinet Note. Capable of grading the Notes and taking into account any special circumstances while being aware of common deficiencies.

proficiency_levels.label: Prepares drafts of Cabinet and CoS Notes using prescribed standard frameworks to ensure procedural compliance
proficiency_levels.description:
Understands the structure, purpose, and process for preparing Cabinet and Committee of Secretaries (CoS) Notes as outlined in sections such as consolidated instructions, forwarding procedures, checklists for avoiding common deficiencies, types of cases, content requirements, and implementation protocols in the guidelines on Preparation of CoS Notes and the Handbook on Cabinet Notes while recognising their significance in policymaking. Understands applicable provisions (e.g., distribution of subjects, allocation of departments, inter-departmental consultations, submission protocols) of the Allocation of Business Rules, 1961 and Transaction of Business Rules, 1961 to appreciate their significance in policymaking and ensure procedural compliance.
Supports the creation of Cabinet and CoS Notes by aligning content with national priorities such as Viksit Bharat@2047, Aatmanirbhar Bharat, Make in India, etc, through the use of updated national strategy documents and guidelines during the drafting process.
Compiles papers, relevant data, annexures, and inter-ministerial inputs for inclusion in the Cabinet or CoS Note to ensure that the Note is comprehensive.
Identifies areas where procedural non-compliance occurs during documentation and seeks clarification or guidance to address them.
Uses standard templates and checklists from the Handbook on Cabinet Notes to ensure inclusion of all required elements and logical sequencing, to support the effective preparation of Cabinet Notes.
Uses digital tools (eOffice, eFile system, Microsoft Office, Single File System (SFS), Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS), Records Management System (RMS), File Tracking System (FMS), etc) for documentation and file management in line with Central Secretariat Manual of Office Procedure (CSMOP) guidelines. Maintains accurate and updated records, including version control, to support traceability, accountability, and smooth workflow during note preparation. I understand the structure, purpose, and procedures for drafting Cabinet and CoS Notes to support accurate and well-structured note preparation.
I draft Cabinet and CoS Notes using prescribed formats, integrating background material, precedents, inter-ministerial inputs, and annexures to ensure procedural compliance and completeness.
I use official digital tools (e.g., eOffice, eFile, SFS, CPGRAMS, RMS, FMS, among others) to draft, format, manage versions, to ensure timely processing of Cabinet Notes in line with CSMOP and Cabinet Secretariat procedures.

proficiency_levels.label: Finalises Cabinet and CoS Notes by ensuring clarity, compliance, integration of inputs, and alignment with national priorities
proficiency_levels.description:
Reviews drafts for completeness, clarity, coherence, and alignment with official guidelines (e.g. Preparation of CoS Notes, Handbook on Cabinet Notes), while checking for common deficiencies to improve quality. Assesses possible implications (such as legal, financial, institutional, or operational issues) and includes measures like clarifying ambiguities, ensuring legal soundness, or adding missing data to reduce risks and strengthen policymaking in Cabinet Notes.
Identifies missing approvals and procedural gaps, as per the Allocation of Business (AoB) Rules, 1961 and the Transaction of Business Rules (ToB) Rules, 1961.
Ensures that Cabinet and CoS Notes reflect alignment with national priorities such as Viksit Bharat@2047, Aatmanirbhar Bharat, Make in India, etc by linking proposals to relevant policy frameworks and strategic objectives, to support coherent, forward-looking decisions across levels of government.
Integrates inputs and comments from all relevant line ministries, departments and organisations to ensure alignment, clarity, and completeness of the Cabinet or CoS Note.
Reviews past Cabinet and CoS decisions, applicable rules, and precedents to maintain policy continuity and avoid inconsistencies.
Coordinates timely routing, approvals, and formatting compliance of Cabinet and CoS Notes before final submission by using digital tools (e.g., eOffice, eFile, SFS, CPGRAMS, RMS, FMS, etc) in accordance with CSMOP guidelines. Guides officials on the use of prescribed formats, required elements, and presentation standards for preparing and submitting Cabinet, Cabinet Committee, and CoS Notes to ensure procedural compliance and build internal capacity. I review Cabinet and CoS Notes for completeness, clarity, and alignment with the Handbook on Cabinet Notes and CoS Note Preparation Guidelines, and ensure they reflect national priorities to support decisions across levels of government.
I integrate inputs from multiple M/D/Os, flag procedural gaps, ensure alignment with AoB and ToB Rules, and use digital tools to support timely routing and approvals.
I mentor officials on improving Cabinet and CoS Notes by refining structure, addressing common deficiencies, to ensure coherence in presenting recommendations.

Develops M/D/O capacity by mentoring teams and institutional partners in designing, tracking, and interpreting KPIs, fostering a results-driven and accountability-based culture. I lead full lifecycle monitoring of complex projects, anticipating risks and ensuring alignment with DPR scope and contractual obligations.
I use advanced analytics and performance insights to guide decision making and strengthen public service delivery outcomes.
I strengthen accountability by linking KPI performance to contract terms, financial controls, and outcome-based mechanisms.

theme_description: Demonstrates the ability to procure goods, services, or works using GeM (Government eMarketplace, National Public Procurement Portal) and other electronic portals, directly or through empanelled agencies, whether by way of purchase, lease, licence, or another method based on fundamental principles of transparency, fairness, competition, economy, efficiency, and accountability with respect to procurement. Ensures judicious use of public funds or any other source of funds (such as grants, loans, donations, or private investment), in accordance with GFR 2017, DFPR 1978 (DFPR Rule 21, 21(a), 21(b)), Manual of Procurement 2022 and their amendments, AOB, TOB, ToR.
sub_theme_description: Demonstrates practical knowledge in regulatory and procedural compliance, procurement planning and execution and vendor management and risk management, by following the Rules & Regulations, Policies & Principles, and procedures in accordance with the "Manual on Procurement of Goods 2017" "Manual for Procurement of Services, 2022", General Financial Rules (GFR) 2017 and its amendments, and the DFPR (Indents, Contracts and Purchases for public service) guidelines.

proficiency_levels.label: Understands foundational procurement processes and demonstrates working knowledge of e-procurement platforms in public purchasing
proficiency_levels.description:
Understands public procurement rules (e.g., GFR 2017, Manual for Procurement) and applies them to routine purchase cases, while using digital platforms like Government E-Marketplace (GeM) or Central Public Procurement Portal (CPPP) to initiate transactions and maintain documentation.
Recognises fundamental procurement principles such as fair pricing, transparency, competition, and non-discrimination, applying them consistently to routine procurement cases.
Understands requirements for secure record-keeping, approval workflows, vendor data confidentiality, and adherence to audit protocols in public procurement.
Maintains purchase records and generates basic reports from e-procurement portals to track timelines, expenditures, and vendor responses.
Recognises problems in basic procurement scenarios such as single bids, vague specifications, etc., and flags them to supervising authorities for escalation. Collaborates with procurement or finance officials for documentation, approvals, and vendor communication to complete end-to-end transactions. I understand and apply basic public procurement rules and digital tools to make compliant and efficient purchases.
I am aware of the principles and objectives of public procurement, such as fairness, transparency, and value for money.
I follow standard ethical guidelines and prescribed procedures in procurement to support fairness, security, and compliance.

proficiency_levels.label: Manages full procurement cycles using structured planning, evaluation, and compliance methods for efficient public service delivery
proficiency_levels.description:
Designs and executes complete procurement workflows such as bid preparation, vendor evaluations, and purchase finalisation, using digital portals (e.g. CPPP, GeM), aligned with regulatory and Departmental mandates.
Evaluates vendor performance using procurement data, supplier records, past performance reports, and compliance checklists to optimise decision-making, pricing, and service delivery outcomes.
Applies risk mitigation, audit-readiness, and compliance protocols to support cross-departmental coordination for efficient procurement aligned with M/D/O objectives.
Drafts clear and complete tender documents, including scope of work, KPIs, and evaluation matrices, aligning with legal and ethical standards.
Implements monitoring and reporting mechanisms to track vendor adherence to timelines, cost, and quality, ensuring alignment with contract requirements. Reviews and validates procurement documents and ensures procurement plans are consistent with program timelines and budget forecasts. I use procurement data, vendor records, and performance reports to assess vendor performance, optimise contracts, and deliver timely, value-based procurements.
I apply compliance, risk, and inclusion frameworks across procurement stages to uphold legal and citizen service outcomes.
I manage procurement processes to streamline planning and execution in alignment with organisational goals, enabling informed decisions that improve vendor performance, optimise pricing, and ensure timely delivery.

proficiency_levels.label: Leads strategic procurement reform using regulatory frameworks, planning tools, and monitoring systems to institutionalise ethical procurement ecosystems.
proficiency_levels.description:
Designs procurement strategies using price trend analysis, risk assessment matrices, inventory planning tools, and regulatory guidelines to strengthen M/D/O planning and decision-making.
Institutionalises ethical standards such as fairness, transparency, non-discrimination, and accountability in vendor engagement, procurement platforms, ensuring alignment with GFR 2017, DFPR 1978, and their amendments, AOB, TOB, ToR .
Leads procurement innovation (e.g., open framework agreements, startup sourcing) to drive transparency, responsiveness, and inclusion in public service delivery.
Drives capacity building across teams on topics such as regulatory compliance, ethical contracting, sustainability standards, risk mitigation, procurement planning, vendor management, and effective use of e-procurement platforms like GeM and CPPP to ensure transparent and accountable procurement practices.
Develops and uses reporting and analytics tools to compare procurement performance across departments, identify cost-saving opportunities, and improve overall efficiency.
Advises leadership on emerging procurement risks and opportunities, including evolving regulatory requirements and innovative contracting practices. Promotes inter-departmental collaboration and standardises contracting practices to improve accountability and citizen engagement in public procurement. I lead innovations in procurement by implementing advanced planning tools and strategies that strengthen compliance, increase transparency, and improve the delivery of goods and services.
I guide the adoption of ethical standards in procurement and ensure alignment with regulatory frameworks, embedding compliance and accountability into procurement systems and processes.
I institutionalise strategic procurement reforms to advance citizen centricity, competition, and public sector innovation.

theme_description: Demonstrates the ability to procure goods, services, or works using GeM (Government eMarketplace, National Public Procurement Portal) and other electronic portals, directly or through empanelled agencies, whether by way of purchase, lease, licence, or another method based on fundamental principles of transparency, fairness, competition, economy, efficiency, and accountability with respect to procurement. Ensures judicious use of public funds or any other source of funds (such as grants, loans, donations, or private investment), in accordance with GFR 2017, DFPR 1978 (DFPR Rule 21, 21(a), 21(b)), Manual of Procurement 2022 and their amendments, AOB, TOB, ToR.
sub_theme_description: Oversee and execute contractual agreements, characterised by practical expertise in various facets of the contracting process. Has the ability to conduct contract scoping, formulate well-defined Terms & Conditions, consider attached commercial nuances and legal aspects, and implement practices for risk mitigation in pursuit of the Public Good. Leverages domain knowledge to evaluate technical proficiency, skillfully negotiate contracts, and select the most suitable vendor, guided by principles such as transparency, fairness, competition, economy, efficiency, and accountability.

proficiency_levels.label: Executes basic contracting tasks using standard templates and procedures to support compliant and transparent contract development
proficiency_levels.description:
Identifies key stages of the contract lifecycle (for e.g., scoping, drafting, award, execution, amendment, and closure) and follows prescribed procedures for each stage under supervision. Understands the foundational aspects of the contracting lifecycle, including contract scoping, formulation of Terms & Conditions, commercial and legal considerations, and basic risk mitigation practices (for e.g. milestone-based payments, cost-plus contracts, etc.), to support effective public procurement guided by principles of transparency, fairness, efficiency, and accountability.
Prepares initial drafts of contract documents (for e.g. contract letters, change orders, notices, among others, etc) using approved templates, ensuring relevant terms and timelines are included.
Identifies routine deviations or errors in contract drafts (for e.g. missing clauses, ambiguous wording, etc) and flags them for corrective action to reduce delays and risks.
Supports contract management practices such as procurement through eProcurement platforms (for e.g., GeM-CPPP, PPP, Post-Award Contract Management Toolkit, etc), compiling vendor data, and assisting in evaluations to promote transparency, fairness, and value-for-money in pursuit of the Public Good.
Maintains records and updates status logs of contracts, deliverables, communications and clarifications to ensure transparency and availability for audit or reporting purposes. Refers to regulatory frameworks such as GFR 2017, DFPR 2024, the Manual for Procurement of Goods 2024, and departmental SOPs to ensure prescribed risk mitigation clauses (for e.g. milestone-based payments, performance security, LD clauses) are correctly included in contract drafts and flags deviations for correction to ensure legal soundness and procedural compliance. I draft and update contract documents using approved templates, ensuring required clauses, timelines, and payment terms are accurately captured.
I use procurement platforms to support vendor data compilation, assist in evaluations, and document key communications to ensure transparency, accuracy, and informed procurement decisions.
I follow GFR, DFPR, procurement manuals, and SOPs to ensure compliant and timely contract processing.

proficiency_levels.label: Manages contractual processes through collaborative drafting, risk mitigation, and performance monitoring to ensure accountability and compliance
proficiency_levels.description:
Reviews contracts and supporting documents such as RFPs , RFQs , award letters, and performance clauses, among others, to ensure alignment with GFR 2017, DFPR 2024, the Manual for Procurement of Goods 2024, departmental SOPs, and project-specific objectives, enabling outcome-based accountability and procedural compliance. Applies principles of transparency, competition, fairness, and accountability while documenting evaluation rationale, negotiation outcomes, and approvals at each stage of the contracting process.
Prepares negotiation briefs by analysing cost benchmarks, risk allocation, payment structures, and vendor proposals, and records negotiated deviations through approved minutes and amendments.
Conducts contract scoping by interpreting technical specifications, scope of work, and contextual requirements (for e.g., operating conditions, target beneficiaries, and expected service levels, etc) by applying domain knowledge to ensure relevance, feasibility, and value-for-money in pursuit of the Public Good.
Coordinates with procurement, legal, and technical divisions to integrate specifications, SLAs , and dispute resolution clauses, supporting risk mitigation through mechanisms such as milestone-based payments, cost-plus contracts, among others.
Analyses vendor performance against contractual deliverables using dashboards or MIS tools and initiates corrective actions such as notices, penalty triggers, or extension proposals to ensure service continuity.
Resolves disputes or misinterpretations in contract terms by referencing precedent cases and guidelines to prevent escalation.
Uses contract monitoring dashboards (e.g. GeM-CPPP, PPP Post-Award Contract Management Toolkit, among others) and e-Procurement analytics (for e.g., bid comparisons, delivery timelines, etc) to track contract progress and support informed decision-making in pursuit of the Public Good. Mentors contract and procurement teams across M/D/Os on good contracting practices and the use of procurement platforms. I review, finalise, and amend contracts to ensure legal compliance, clarity of obligations, and value-for-money outcomes.
I coordinate with legal, technical, and procurement teams to manage risks, negotiations, and execution issues during the contract lifecycle.
I monitor vendor performance and initiate timely corrective actions to ensure quality, timeliness, and accountability in service delivery.

proficiency_levels.label: Oversees contract scoping, negotiation oversight, and dispute resolution to ensure accountable execution and protection of public interest
proficiency_levels.description:
Leads contract scoping and stakeholder consultations for high-value, multi-party, or inter-agency agreements (for e.g. centrally sponsored schemes, shared service arrangements, PPPs), by consolidating technical, legal, and financial inputs and assessing downstream execution risks, service continuity, and citizen impact.
Guides and validates negotiation strategies for complex contracts by reviewing cost structures, risk allocation, payment mechanisms, and performance incentives, ensuring negotiated outcomes remain compliant with GFR provisions and principles of fairness and competition.
Evaluates and resolves escalated contractual disputes, claims, extensions, and amendments by interpreting contract clauses, procurement rules, audit observations, and precedents, and records reasoned decisions to safeguard public interest and minimise litigation risk.
Advocates for the institutionalisation of best practices in contract management, such as performance-linked contracts, risk-sharing mechanisms (for e.g. milestone-based payments, cost-plus contracts, etc.), and the use of emerging technologies (for e.g. blockchain, generative AI, etc.), to improve efficiency, transparency and traceability across M/D/Os. Reviews contract performance trends, audit findings, and dispute patterns to recommend targeted improvements in scoping, T&Cs, and risk mitigation approaches for future procurements, strengthening institutional learning and execution quality. I lead and approve complex contract scoping and negotiation outcomes for high-value or multi-party procurements, ensuring compliance, fairness, and value-for-money.
I evaluate and resolve escalated contractual disputes to safeguard public interest and uphold transparency and accountability.
I strengthen contract execution quality by standardising clauses, risk mitigation approaches, and post-award monitoring practices based on audit findings and performance trends.

theme_description: Demonstrates the ability to procure goods, services, or works using GeM (Government eMarketplace, National Public Procurement Portal) and other electronic portals, directly or through empanelled agencies, whether by way of purchase, lease, licence, or another method based on fundamental principles of transparency, fairness, competition, economy, efficiency, and accountability with respect to procurement. Ensures judicious use of public funds or any other source of funds (such as grants, loans, donations, or private investment), in accordance with GFR 2017, DFPR 1978 (DFPR Rule 21, 21(a), 21(b)), Manual of Procurement 2022 and their amendments, AOB, TOB, ToR.
sub_theme_description: Demonstrates the ability to identify, evaluate, and manage vendors and consultants using established government systems (such as the Government e-Marketplace, GFR 2017, DFPR 1978, and the Manuals for Procurement of Works and Consultancy 2022). Ensures that procurement decisions reflect transparency, competition, economy, efficiency, and accountability, and that agreements are properly executed before commencement of services.

proficiency_levels.label: Applies procurement rules and digital systems to support compliant and timely vendor selection
proficiency_levels.description:
Understands the fundamental principles of public procurement under GFR 2017 (transparency, competition, economy, efficiency, accountability) and explains their relevance in vendor selection.
Identifies the appropriate procurement method (for e.g., GeM, limited tender, open tender, or empanelment) under Rule 149 and records file references and approving authority as per DFPR/AoB.
Prepares and organises complete eOffice/physical files (for e.g., sanction, estimate, SoW/ToR, RfP, approval notes, etc) using prescribed templates to ensure checklist-based compliance.
Uses GeM/CPPP search and approved empanelment lists to prepare a longlist of vendors with basic eligibility screening (for e.g., PAN, GST, UDYAM/MSME, debarment checks, etc) so that only eligible bidders are invited.
Assists in publishing NIT/RfP on GeM/CPPP within prescribed timelines to ensure fair competition and transparency.
Maintains a tracker of bid milestones (queries, pre‑bid, bid‑opening, TEC, award) and circulates weekly updates to reduce processing delays.
Validates receipt of EMD/PBG and required declarations (conflict of interest, integrity pact where applicable) before bid opening.
Performs three-way verification (contract/PO vs. CRAC/GRN vs. invoice) and routes payments through PFMS within defined timelines. Files all communications, corrigenda and approvals with version control to enable traceability during internal/audit review. I follow GFR rules and digital systems to support compliant vendor selection.
I maintain complete documentation and timelines to ensure audit readiness.
I prevent delays and compliance risks by verifying securities and escalating deviations early.

proficiency_levels.label: Manages procurement cycles to ensure transparent, competitive, economical, and efficient vendor selection
proficiency_levels.description:
Designs tender documents and eligibility criteria that promote open competition and prevent restrictive specifications, ensuring fairness and wider vendor participation. Customises model bid documents (for e.g., RfPs, QCBSs, QC, etc) with standard clauses (for e.g., blacklisting, LD, arbitration, IP where applicable) and legal vetting to reduce post‑award disputes.
Conducts pre‑bid conference, issues clarifications within deadlines on CPPP/GeM, and maintains a speaking‑order log to ensure equal access to information.
Leads bid responsiveness checks and applies approved evaluation methodology (for e.g., QCBS, L1, etc) with documented scoring sheets and speaking orders.
Applies approved evaluation methodology (for e.g., QCBS, least‑cost, etc) and documents scoring sheets and minutes to ensure transparent, replicable decisions.
Issues LoA/contracts and ensures execution of securities, insurances, and compliance documentation before service start.
Monitors vendor SLAs through dashboards/MIS, records performance ratings, and issues notices for delays or deficiencies.
Manages change orders/extensions within GFR provisions and maintains a vendor risk register for financial and operational risks. Trains colleagues on checklists/templates and standardises trackers across projects to improve throughput and consistency. I conduct transparent and competitive procurement processes that withstand audit and scrutiny.
I ensure economy and value for money through structured evaluation and price benchmarking.
I enforce vendor accountability by monitoring performance and applying contractual safeguards.

proficiency_levels.label: Institutionalises procurement governance systems that embed transparency, competition, economy, efficiency, and accountability across the M/D/O
proficiency_levels.description:
Establishes standardised procurement SOPs and digital workflows aligned with GFR/DoE manuals to institutionalise transparent and rule-based vendor management.
Implements analytics-driven oversight (for e.g., GeM analytics, spend dashboards, PFMS cycle data, etc) to improve efficiency and reduce procurement delays across divisions.
Leads demand aggregation, rate contracts, and category strategies to achieve economies of scale and measurable cost savings.
Designs vendor performance scorecards and public disclosure dashboards (for e.g., awards, savings, vendor ratings, etc) to strengthen transparency and public trust.
Institutionalises competition safeguards by periodically reviewing vendor concentration risks and preventing dependency on single suppliers.
Establishes procurement risk frameworks (for e.g., heat maps, early-warning triggers, dependency analysis, etc) to proactively mitigate financial and operational risks.
Builds capacity (for e.g., periodic training, communities of practice, guidance notes, etc) and assigns role‑based authorisations to reduce single‑point failures. Reviews procurement outcomes annually (for e.g., cycle time, savings achieved, compliance deviations, etc) and initiates systemic reforms to continuously improve efficiency and economy. I institutionalise procurement systems that embed transparency and competition across the M/D/O.
I drive measurable cost savings and efficiency improvements through data-led procurement strategies.
I strengthen accountability and public trust by enforcing integrity safeguards and publishing performance outcomes.

theme_description: Demonstrates ability to maintain accurate records of goods and materials in the Ministry / Department / Organisation. Ensures proper custody of delivered items, conducts physical verification of assets, and identifies surplus and obsolete materials. Determines appropriate categories and modes of disposal for goods, such as auction or e-auction, in compliance with GFR, DFPR 1978, and Manual for Procurement of Goods 2017, to minimise losses due to various reasons.
sub_theme_description: Oversees and conducts accurate physical verification of materials, valuation of material, analysis of losses etc., and accordingly take required actions for disposal of assets, as per laid down processes/ guidelines in GFR 2017, Manual of Procurement of Goods, 2017, DFPR etc.

proficiency_levels.label: Applies procedures to maintain records, verify materials, and support compliant disposal
proficiency_levels.description:
Identifies and explains key provisions of GFR 2017, DFPR delegation limits, and the Manual of Procurement of Goods 2017 relating to stock maintenance, annual physical verification, loss reporting, valuation principles, write-off procedures, and approved modes of disposal (for e.g., auction, transfer, write-off). Maintains updated Stock Register, Asset Register, and Dead Stock Register in prescribed formats, ensuring entries match GRNs and issue vouchers.
Assists in annual and surprise physical verification exercises and reconciles physical stock with ledger balances, documenting discrepancies in verification sheets.
Ensures secure storage and tagging of assets (for e.g., asset coding/barcoding of IT equipment, etc) to prevent pilferage or misplacement.
Executes disposal of surplus or unserviceable materials through approved methods (for e.g., auction, transfer, write-off) in compliance with GFR and departmental procedures.
Reports loss, shortage, damage, or deterioration immediately as per GFR loss reporting procedures, preparing preliminary loss statements for supervisory review.
Prepares draft Survey Reports and Condemnation Proposals for unserviceable items (for e.g., outdated computers, damaged furniture, etc) under supervision.
Verifies supporting documentation such as inspection notes, delivery challans, warranty records, ensuring audit-ready documentation. I maintain accurate and audit-ready stock and asset records.
I support physical verification and promptly report discrepancies.
I process disposal documentation in compliance with GFR and DFPR.

proficiency_levels.label: Implements and monitors inventory and disposal processes to ensure operational readiness and financial compliance
proficiency_levels.description:
Implements structured procedures for receipt, inspection, storage, and issue of materials, ensuring compliance with GFR 2017 inventory provisions.
Conducts variance analysis between physical stock and ledger balances and initiates corrective action (for e.g., stock adjustment notes, loss assessment, etc).
Constitutes and coordinates Survey/Condemnation Boards, documents proceedings, and ensures proper valuation of obsolete or surplus materials.
Determines reserve price using approved valuation methods (for e.g., book value, depreciated value, market assessment, etc) before auction/e-auction.
Executes disposal through authorised platforms such as GeM or MSTC e-auction portals, ensuring transparency and competitive bidding.
Utilises inventory management systems (for e.g., integrating with PFMS for financial tracking or departmental e-Office modules) and oversees stock levels to ensure the continuous availability of materials for immediate use
Monitors compliance with DFPR delegation limits and ensures approvals are obtained from competent financial authority. Verifies the condition and safe disposal of degraded, contaminated, or obsolete materials, ensuring adherence to the Manual of Procurement of Goods 2017 to eliminate environmental risks and ensure proper asset lifecycle closure. I monitor inventory systems to prevent losses and ensure compliance.
I conduct transparent and time-bound disposal through authorised platforms.
I address discrepancies and audit observations with documented corrective action.

proficiency_levels.label: Strengthens M/D/O-wide systems for transparent, risk-controlled, and compliant material management and disposal
proficiency_levels.description:
Designs and standardises M/D/O-wide Asset Lifecycle Management SOPs aligned with GFR 2017 and DFPR provisions.
Establishes digital asset tracking systems integrated with PFMS/ERP platforms to enable real-time reconciliation of financial and physical records.
Reviews high-value or sensitive disposal cases (for e.g., vehicles, specialised equipment, etc) and approves disposal strategy (for e.g., auction, transfer, write-off) based on risk and valuation analysis.
Conducts root cause analysis of recurring loss events (for e.g., repeated stock shortages, delayed condemnation, etc) and implements internal control reforms.
Establishes risk-based verification schedules for high-value or theft-prone items (for e.g., IT hardware, fuel inventory, etc).
Provides guidance and strategic direction for the development and implementation of capacity building initiatives and training curricula to strengthen staff competence and institutionalise best practices in materials management and disposal procedures.
Ensures uniform application of disposal and valuation policies across regional offices through circulars, compliance reviews, and periodic reporting dashboards. Advises senior management on financial exposure risks arising from asset depreciation, idle inventory, or delayed disposal. I robust systems that ensure transparent and compliant asset management across the M/D/O.
I mitigate financial and audit risks by strengthening internal controls and oversight mechanisms.
I oversee complex and high-value disposal cases with strategic and regulatory judgement.

theme_description: Demonstrates ability to maintain accurate records of goods and materials in the Ministry / Department / Organisation. Ensures proper custody of delivered items, conducts physical verification of assets, and identifies surplus and obsolete materials. Determines appropriate categories and modes of disposal for goods, such as auction or e-auction, in compliance with GFR, DFPR 1978, and Manual for Procurement of Goods 2017, to minimise losses due to various reasons.
sub_theme_description: Manages receipt, storage, issue, verification, and disposal of goods and materials in government offices as per approved financial and procurement rules. Ensures traceability, accountability, and safety of items through accurate registers, timely reconciliation, and adherence to General Financial Rules (GFR 2017), Delegation of Financial Powers Rules (DFPR 1978), Manual for Procurement of Goods (2017), and related departmental instructions.

proficiency_levels.label: Maintains accurate and traceable storage records
proficiency_levels.description:
Records all receipts, issues, and balances in a Master Stock Register for both consumable and non-consumable items, as per the General Financial Rules (GFR) 2017 and the Central Secretariat Manual of Office Procedure (CSMOP) 2019. Verifies goods received against the sanction order, supplier bill, and inspection note; prepares a Goods Receipt Note (GRN) in the e-Office system as evidence of receipt and acceptance.
Assigns each item a unique Asset Identification Number linked to the officer or section responsible for it.
Tags non-consumable items with barcodes or Quick Response (QR) codes showing make, model, serial number, and warranty period.
Records the physical location of non-consumable items and user details to maintain traceability.
Issues materials only against authorised Indents (approved internal requests), updates Bin Cards and Stock Ledgers immediately after issue to maintain accurate balances.
Maintains Movement Registers and Gate Pass Registers for items sent outside office premises for repair or transfer; ensures acknowledgement upon return to prevent loss or misuse.
Organises storage areas (stores) by category: stationery, electrical, electronic, or hazardous items, and conducts weekly checks to ensure safety and prevent deterioration.
Assists in reconciling store records with entries in the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) and vendor payments; reports discrepancies within three working days as required under CSMOP 2019 (Paragraph 87).
Tracks all maintenance and repair activities under Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMC) and warranties; keeps service reports for vendor compliance. Participates in quarterly Physical Verification of Stores (PVS) and prepares Variance Notes (records that explain shortages, excesses, or mismatches between physical and recorded stock) along with reasons and corrective actions. I keep all receipts, issues, and balances accurate and verifiable as per government financial rules.
I ensure every asset is tagged, traceable, and accounted for at all times.
I promptly identify and report mismatches between financial records and physical stock for corrective action.

proficiency_levels.label: Operates multiple storage systems and enforces compliance
proficiency_levels.description:
Develops and implements Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for receiving, inspecting, issuing, transferring, and disposing of materials, including a maker-checker system (one person enters data, another verifies it) to prevent misuse. Conducts ABC Analysis (Always, Better, Control) and FSN Analysis (Fast, Slow, Non-moving) to classify items by importance and usage rate.
Fixes minimum and maximum stock levels and reorder points to avoid overstocking or stockouts.
Reconciles Stock Ledgers with e-Office and Public Financial Management System (PFMS) data every month.
Prepares written explanations for any mismatches and obtains approval for corrections.
Forms Boards of Survey or Condemnation as per the General Financial Rules (GFR) 2017, Rules 194–197, for inspection and disposal of unserviceable or obsolete items.
Maintains condition reports, photographs, and supporting documentation to justify disposal decisions.
Conducts auction or e-auction of surplus or condemned materials through authorised government platforms (e.g., MSTC), ensuring reserve price approval, GST compliance, and remittance through PFMS
Ensures safe disposal of electronic waste and hazardous items (for example, expired batteries, printer cartridges, or chemicals) by authorised recyclers, in line with the E-Waste Management Rules, 2016, and maintains disposal certificates.
Monitors vendor performance through Service Level Agreements (SLAs) mentioned in Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMC) or Annual Technical Support (ATS) contracts; enforces penalties for non-performance.
Manages inter-office material transfers through Transfer Challans and insurance coverage for goods in transit. Produces bilingual (English and Hindi, or regional language) Inventory Dashboards on stock accuracy, item ageing, and disposal pipeline, in accordance with the Guidelines for Indian Government Websites (GIGW), for managerial review. I manage multiple storage areas through clear procedures to ensure accountability and transparency.
I conduct all write-offs and disposals in a fair, rule-based, and well-documented manner.
I maintain consistent alignment among physical stock, financial data, and digital records to support informed decision-making.

proficiency_levels.label: Institutionalises inventory governance and assurance
proficiency_levels.description:
Implements and reinforces a Departmental Inventory Management Policy aligned with the General Financial Rules (GFR) 2017, Delegation of Financial Powers Rules (DFPR) 1978, and the Manual for Procurement of Goods 2017.
Mandates uniform rules for classification, tagging (barcode or Radio Frequency Identification (RFID)), and digital record keeping.
Aligns procurement planning with demand forecasting and stock level data to ensure timely delivery and avoid idle inventory.
Coordinates with the Finance Department to ensure proper capitalisation, depreciation, and write-off approvals based on verified stock before year-end account closure.
Enforces a transparent Disposal Framework, including rules for the constitution of Boards of Survey, reserve price approvals, electronic auction protocols, and public notifications to ensure public confidence.
Commissions independent Stock and Process Audits every year and ensures Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA) are taken.
Summarises findings in the Annual Administrative Report for executive and statutory review
Enforces risk control mechanisms such as access controls, surveillance systems, segregation of duties, and secured storage for high-value items to mitigate fraud and theft risks
Ensures compliance with environmental and safety regulations by obtaining annual certificates from authorised recyclers and including disposal data in sustainability or environmental compliance reports.
Integrates Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and Service Level Agreements (SLAs) for inventory accuracy, turnaround time, ageing, and disposal lead time results into officer and vendor performance appraisals and identify capacity issues Institutionalises staff capacity building by conducting regular training on the General Financial Rules (GFR), Public Financial Management System (PFMS), and e-Office procedures I institutionalise inventory policies and systems that promote organisation wide transparency, efficiency, and accountability.
I align procurement, finance, and disposal systems to ensure no discrepancies between physical stock, audit findings, and accounts.
I strengthen institutional capacity through regular audits, staff training, and data analysis to reduce risk and improve performance.

theme_description: Demonstrates the ability to develop monitoring and evaluation framework for tracking implementation of central government policies, schemes, and projects for the Department, Ministry or Organisation. Identifies right set of data, information, and relevant parameters to evaluate. Undertakes qualitative and quantitative assessments to determine the progress of a government policy, schemes and project towards pre-specified goals and objectives, and to highlight any alarming gap that may hamper the slated outcomes & outputs. Facilitates in making informed decisions and adjustments to improve policy effectiveness, ensuring policies lead to desired outcomes and benefits. Identify successes, challenges, and lessons learned to enhance future policymaking and implementation processes for the Government of India.
sub_theme_description: Conducts assessment based on the data to identify strengths and shortfalls in intended outcomes and formulates remedial actions to correct deficiencies in delivery of schemes and government programs.

proficiency_levels.label: Understands scheme indicators and performance data and flags strengths and shortfalls for review
proficiency_levels.description:
Identifies prescribed output and outcome indicators from scheme guidelines, OOMF documents, or DMEO templates, and understands what each indicator is intended to measure. Recognises DPDP and RTI requirements for scheme data and follows approved checklists and SOPs for masking PII , sharing aggregates, and maintaining basic access records.
Maps the scheme logic (inputs - activities - outputs - outcomes) using standard templates to understand where performance should be assessed.
Defines indicators (mix of output and immediate outcome) with SMART metadata (for e.g., definition, unit, frequency, disaggregation, etc) in a data dictionary for supervisor approval.
Extracts and organises data from authorised sources (for e.g., scheme MIS, PFMS, dashboards, survey summaries, etc) as per defined formats and timelines.
Flags strengths, shortfalls, and data quality issues in summary notes or dashboards for supervisory review.
Compares actual values against baselines and targets (for e.g., using predefined templates, variance thresholds, or system-generated flags) to identify areas of underperformance or overachievement.
Uses basic disaggregation (for e.g., district, beneficiary group, time period, etc) to highlight visible gaps, as per predefined parameters.
Documents assumptions, data limitations, and missing information to avoid misinterpretation of results. Files all artefacts (for e.g., logic model, dictionary, datasets, dashboard, action log, etc) in e‑Office with version control, to keep an auditable trail. I identify strengths and shortfalls in scheme outputs and outcomes using prescribed indicators and data sources.
I organise and present performance data clearly to support review and decision making.
I maintain accurate, auditable data records and flag data limitations transparently.

proficiency_levels.label: Conducts outcome and output assessments and recommends remedial actions to improve scheme delivery
proficiency_levels.description:
Designs an evaluation plan (for e.g., including questions, indicators, sampling, timeline, etc) for districts and states.
Collects primary data using stratified samples and standard tools (for e.g., FGDs, KIIs , structured surveys, etc), ensuring high response rates and inter‑rater reliability checks to improve validity.
Integrates administrative data (e.g., MIS, PFMS, etc) with primary data sources to create a consolidated dataset for assessment.
Applies standard analytical techniques (for e.g., trend or cohort analysis) on integrated datasets to assess changes in outputs and outcomes over time.
Documents data sources, assumptions, and analytical steps in a methods note to enable review and reproducibility of findings.
Assesses cost, efficiency, and coverage in relation to observed outcome shifts to support value-for-money analysis.
Builds disaggregated views (for e.g., gender, caste, geography, vulnerability groups, etc) and tests gaps, flags equity shortfalls with confidence intervals, to target inclusion.
Performs root cause analysis (for e.g., fishbone, 5‑Whys, etc) on underperforming indicators and proposes CAPA (for e.g., process, staffing, outreach, supply changes, etc) to enable action.
Presents assessment findings and recommended remedial actions to supervisors or steering committees for decision making.
Tracks implementation of agreed corrective actions and reports early signs of improvement or persistence of gaps. Publishes anonymised datasets and codebooks on approved platforms (for e.g., e‑Office link or data.gov.in, etc) with metadata, to support transparency and reuse. I conduct structured assessments to explain why scheme outcomes and outputs are performing as observed.
I recommend data-backed remedial actions to address delivery and design gaps.
I track whether corrective actions lead to measurable improvements in performance.

proficiency_levels.label: Institutionalises outcome and output assessments and ensures evidence drives policy, funding, and scheme redesign
proficiency_levels.description:
Institutionalises evaluation frameworks, standards, and schedules across programmes to ensure consistent assessment of outcomes and outputs.
Sets an annual evaluation calendar (for e.g., in terms of process, outcome, impact studies, etc) with independent/third‑party components, allocating budget and publishes ToRs with quality assurance criteria, to ensure rigor.
Establishes portfolio analytics (for e.g., outcomes achieved vs targets, cost‑effectiveness, equity gaps, risk flags, etc) and uses them in quarterly reviews to recommend scale, stop, and/or reset of schemes, to optimise impact.
Links evaluation evidence to budget allocations, performance reviews, and policy amendments.
Ensures accountability by publicly disclosing evaluation findings and tracking closure of agreed corrective actions on transparent dashboards (for e.g., service time saved, leakage reduced, coverage gaps closed, etc).
Enforces privacy, ethics, and accessibility (for e.g., DPIA, consent/notice, anonymisation, GIGW conformance, etc) across all studies and artefacts, audits compliance annually, to reduce risk.
Coordinates with states, PSUs, line ministries, etc to harmonise indicators and share best practices.
Builds institutional evaluation capacity by mandating management responses and learning notes for major assessments and running communities of practice or certification mechanisms to strengthen evaluator skills and shared learning in the M/D/O.
Leads M/D/O learning by commissioning meta-evaluations or learning syntheses and systematically updating indicator catalogues or playbooks based on consolidated lessons. Uses evaluation evidence to support policy and legal decisions by clearly documenting the rationale for actions taken. I institutionalise assessment systems such that evidence consistently informs policy and funding decisions.
I ensure remedial actions lead to sustained improvements through programme redesign and system changes.
I use evaluation evidence to strengthen accountability and long-term public value across schemes programmes.

theme_description: Formulates budget and expenditure plans aligned to the objectives and budget allocation of the Ministry / Department / Organisation, in accordance with the rules and guidelines of the Ministry of Finance, while also forecasting future expenditures. Manages and monitors the Division/Department's budget, accounts & expenditure, while promoting financial prudence within the Department to enhance overall efficiency. Develops proficiency in handling PFMS (Public Financial Management System).
sub_theme_description: Demonstrates the ability to forecast and prepare budget for Division / Department / Ministry / Organisation, for specified period, aligned to the guidelines and standards formulated by Ministry of Finance

proficiency_levels.label: Prepares simple budgets and tracks expenses using PFMS to follow financial rules
proficiency_levels.description:
Prepares basic budget estimates in alignment with allocated resources and organisational guidelines, adhering to financial policies set by the Ministry of Finance.
Monitors daily expenses and income to ensure alignment with the approved budget and identifies any variances from projections.
Understands basic budgeting and forecasting principles, accounting standards, and components of a budget.
Operates financial systems, including PFMS, ensuring compliance with financial rules and accuracy in accounting processes. Analyses past expenditures and simple financial reports to assist in future budget preparation. I produce budget estimates that reflect realistic forecasts by accounting for prior spending patterns, current obligations, and future needs.
I ensure compliance with financial regulations in daily operations, addressing variances and ensuring financial accuracy and adherence to projections.
I utilise the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) effectively to process budget-related transactions and generate reports, ensuring fiscal discipline and adherence to financial rules.

proficiency_levels.label: Develops multi-year forecasts, reallocates budgets based on changing priorities, and ensures efficient resource use
proficiency_levels.description:
Evaluates past financial data and spending patterns to develop multi-year budget forecasts, aligning with broader M/D/O goals and financial policies.
Collaborates with cross-functional teams to adjust the budget based on priorities, risks, and unforeseen circumstances.
Develops contingency plans for budget shortfalls and surpluses, ensuring compliance with Ministry of Finance directives.
Uses structured financial tools to assess requirements, allocate budgets, monitor progress, and resolve budgetary issues. Conducts periodic reviews and optimises resource allocation to manage budgetary constraints effectively. I produce multi-year budget forecasts that incorporate previous financial data and align with the overall goals of the ministry, department, or organisation (M/D/O).
I adjust budgets based on identified risks and changing priorities, ensuring smooth realignment in response to contingencies.
I ensure effective resource allocation and manage shortfalls or surpluses in line with ministry directives and departmental needs.

proficiency_levels.label: Leads strategic financial planning by aligning budgets with national goals and innovative practices for long term fiscal sustainability
proficiency_levels.description:
Leads long-term financial planning for the M/D/O, incorporating advanced forecasting models to anticipate future expenditure trends and align them with objectives. Engages with key stakeholders to prioritise resource allocation and maximise budgetary efficiency, ensuring alignment with national initiatives like Atma Nirbhar Bharat.
Oversees the financial health of the department, ensuring that budget formulation and implementation contribute to the organisational mission.
Innovates budgetary practices through advanced financial management technologies, such as blockchain and machine learning models, for precise financial projections and risk management. I produce long-term financial plans that ensure alignment with the strategic objectives of the M/D/O, using advanced financial management technologies such as forecasting models.
I ensure the alignment of budget allocations with national priorities (e.g., Atma Nirbhar Bharat), maximising the impact and efficiency of resource use.
I innovate budgetary practices using advanced financial management technologies like blockchain and machine learning, enhancing fiscal prudence and long-term sustainability.

theme_description: Formulates budget and expenditure plans aligned to the objectives and budget allocation of the Ministry / Department / Organisation, in accordance with the rules and guidelines of the Ministry of Finance, while also forecasting future expenditures. Manages and monitors the Division/Department's budget, accounts & expenditure, while promoting financial prudence within the Department to enhance overall efficiency. Develops proficiency in handling PFMS (Public Financial Management System).
sub_theme_description: Demonstrates the ability to adopt internal control mechanisms for efficient & effective financial operations as well as identify potential threats & opportunities for the Ministry / Department/ Organisation.

proficiency_levels.label: Manages financial operations accurately and follows rules to support informed expenditure-related decisions
proficiency_levels.description:
Understands and executes day-to-day financial operations using PFMS and MoF -mandated systems (e.g., treasury module, sanction module, bill processing) to ensure payments, receipts, and reconciliations are completed accurately and on time, reducing risks of delays or mismatches.
Follows rules, procedures, tools and financial frameworks (General Financial Rules, Delegation of Financial Powers, Public Expenditure and Financial Accountability frameworks) correctly while processing bills, sanctions, and procurements, ensuring transactions are compliant and reducing the likelihood of audit objections.
Uses checklists and templates (e.g., pre-audit checklists, expenditure vetting formats) to ensure adherence to audit and internal financial control requirements of the M/D/O including maker–checker validation, segregation of duties, and complete documentation.
Supports the preparation of budget estimates by compiling data from varied sources (e.g., units, schemes, and cost centres), ensuring that submissions are timely and aligned with MoF formats.
Assists in tracking actual expenditure against approved budgets, flags basic variances, and alerts supervisors where emerging risks (e.g., potential overspend or underspend) may affect programme delivery.
Collates and provides information on fund utilisation across all programs/schemes/agencies to support efficient decision-making and transparency. Maintains a complete audit trail (notings/approvals/PFMS reference numbers) and escalates exceptions through the defined DDO–PAO workflow. I prepare and maintain financial records and reports in PFMS or other prescribed formats to ensure timely submission and reconciliation.
I comply with budgetary and expenditure procedures as per the Ministry of Finance's rules, the General Financial Rules (GFR), and departmental guidelines.
I monitor expenditure against budgets and report variances or assumed risks for corrective action.

proficiency_levels.label: Monitors and optimises expenditure, ensuring timely, accountable use of public funds
proficiency_levels.description:
Prepares, monitors, and revises departmental budgets and expenditure plans, aligning priorities with fiscal allocations and MoF guidelines. Analyses expenditure trends across schemes/programmes to identify risks, inefficiencies, and opportunities for cost optimisation, and recommends corrective measures to improve fiscal discipline.
Develops and implements internal monitoring mechanisms, including benchmarking against national/global indices (e.g., PEFA, Public Expenditure Reviews), to flag emerging risks early, improve transparency, and support data-driven mid-course corrections in departmental spending.
Suggests process improvements to enhance efficiency, prevent cost overruns, and streamline operational systems in the PFMS or other financial management systems.
Coordinates with programme divisions, finance, and implementing units/agencies to resolve expenditure issues, including head-mismatch corrections and DDO/PAO/PrAO reconciliations.
Facilitates internal scrutiny and audits, embedding anti-corruption approaches and legislative oversight, and suggests reforms to improve resource allocation. I plan, monitor, and revise departmental budgets and expenditures to align with fiscal priorities and approved allocations..
I analyse expenditure trends, identify risks and inefficiencies, and recommend corrective actions to optimise costs and strengthen accountability.
I coordinate, implement process improvements, and embed monitoring mechanisms to ensure timely and transparent use of public funds.

proficiency_levels.label: Shapes expenditure strategy to ensure efficient and transparent financial management
proficiency_levels.description:
Shapes departmental expenditure strategy by aligning resource allocation with fiscal policy, outcome-based budgeting, and long-term organisational and national priorities. Drives high-impact expenditure reforms to improve efficiency and control compliance, including commitment control (liability tracking), UC/SOE discipline for grants, and reduction of “rush of expenditure” through stronger review cadences.
Anticipates risks and opportunities in expenditure patterns using trend analytics, exception reporting, audit para trends, and scheme-wise utilisation signals, and advises leadership on mitigation or strategic actions.
Formulates the financial risk philosophy of the M/D/O by analysing long-term trends in government, economy, and society and embeds this philosophy into planning, budgeting, and expenditure control processes.
Formulates policy options and strategic approaches for financial development and inclusion from a macroeconomic perspective, anticipating trade-offs and proactively addressing potential challenges.
Oversees critical financial systems and institutional processes, including PFMS-linked workflows, partnerships, and revenue administration, to ensure high standards of compliance, transparency, and comprehensiveness.
Champions' adoption of embedded technologies (real-time dashboards, AI-based forecasting, PFMS analytics) to strengthen expenditure oversight, accelerate financial reporting, and enable timely, data-driven decisions across programmes and schemes.
Mentors teams and stakeholders to cultivate financial responsibility, compliance culture, and transparent expenditure practices. I shape departmental expenditure strategies and fiscal policies aligned with long-term organisational and national priorities to enhance financial performance.
I drive reforms and embed technology to strengthen transparency, accountability, and efficiency in financial management.
I mentor teams, guide stakeholders, and make strategic financial decisions to ensure sustainable and compliant expenditure practices.

theme_description: Formulates budget and expenditure plans aligned to the objectives and budget allocation of the Ministry / Department / Organisation, in accordance with the rules and guidelines of the Ministry of Finance, while also forecasting future expenditures. Manages and monitors the Division/Department's budget, accounts & expenditure, while promoting financial prudence within the Department to enhance overall efficiency. Develops proficiency in handling PFMS (Public Financial Management System).
sub_theme_description: Prepares and presents accounts as per Government Accounting Rules, 1990; Accounting Rules for Treasuries; and Account Code Volume III, and classifies transactions in Government Accounts. Ensures that budget heads adhere to the classification rules and other guidelines of GFR 2017 and its relevant amendments.

proficiency_levels.label: Applies accounting rules to correctly classify, post and reconcile routine transactions
proficiency_levels.description:
Demonstrates awareness of the provisions of Government Accounting Rules, 1990, GFR 2017, Treasury Rules and Account Code Vol. III.
Understands the basic structure of budget heads and classification guidelines in GFR 2017 and LMMH, using checklists to map object heads to major, minor, and sub‑heads, so that misbookings are prevented at source.
Posts receipts, payments, advances and recoveries in PFMS within the next working day to maintain updated ledgers.
Verifies sanction number, financial concurrence, delegated authority and budget availability before booking expenditure.
Uploads sanction orders, invoices, vouchers and supporting documents in PFMS and records movement in e-Office to maintain complete audit trail.
Maintains sanction, advance, contingent expenditure and suspense registers and updates liquidation status monthly.
Prepares monthly head-wise expenditure statements, reconciles them with DDO and PAO figures, resolves mismatches within the set timelines, and records the reasons clearly and accurately. Records reasons for reconciliation differences and initiates correction entries promptly to avoid carry-forward mismatches. I classify and post transactions correctly under appropriate budget heads within prescribed timelines.
I maintain complete documentation and reconciled records ready for audit review.
I ensure routine accounting work complies with GAR, GFR and LMMH provisions.

proficiency_levels.label: Manages reconciliations, controls classification risks and supports budget discipline
proficiency_levels.description:
Prepares CoA and classification checklists and trains DDOs on correct booking, helping reduce re-classification errors recorded in the monthly defect register.
Follows maker–checker procedures, checks bills for GFR and delegation compliance, and issues defect memos while tracking their timely closure.
Monitors AC/DC bills, Grants-in-Aid and Utilisation Certificates through PFMS dashboards and escalates overdue cases.
Manages budget control by maintaining registers, processing re-appropriations within delegated powers, preparing rule-based proposals where approvals exceed powers, and updating PFMS after approval.
Coordinates with the A&E, PAO, and CCA on inter-account adjustments, DDR/PLA settlements, and advance clearances.
Implements internal controls by conducting risk-based post-audit checks, recording issues and corrective actions, and submitting monthly reports to the controlling officer. Applies correct budget‑head classifications to routine and non‑routine transactions based on GFR 2017 and LMMH, documenting rationale for bookings to make future reviews traceable. I ensure accurate classification and timely reconciliation across all schemes and heads.
I reduce misclassification, clear suspense balances and prevent excess expenditure.
I strengthen budget discipline through variance analysis and timely corrective action.

proficiency_levels.label: Leads annual account closure, institutionalises controls and advises on fiscal risk
proficiency_levels.description:
Leads year-end account closure and validates final bookings before submission of annual and appropriation accounts within statutory timelines.
Develops and updates departmental accounting SOPs linking GAR 1990, GFR 2017, LMMH and PFMS workflows.
Reviews and approves classification structures for new schemes or restructuring proposals and ensures PFMS configuration aligns with approved CoA.
Anticipates and conducts regular financial risk checks (misclassification, idle balances, fraud), monitors controls continuously, and issues corrective circulars while tracking compliance.
Introduces automated validation checks or system-based controls in PFMS to reduce manual errors and strengthen classification accuracy.
Leads preparation of replies to audit observations from C&AG and Internal Audit and monitors time-bound para settlement.
Oversees digital tracking of Grants-in-Aid and ensures reduction of overdue Utilisation Certificates through structured follow-up mechanisms.
Presents quarterly financial performance to leadership, showing utilisation, commitments, and liabilities, and recommends fund surrenders or additional allocations to maintain fiscal discipline. Develops guidance notes, checklists, and tools on complex budget‑head classification and reallocation, mentoring DDO/PAO staff to build institutional capacity and reduce repeat errors. I ensure timely and error-free annual accounts and audit closure.
I institutionalise strong controls to prevent misclassification and financial risks.
I guide leadership decisions through clear financial performance and risk insights.

theme_description: Formulates budget and expenditure plans aligned to the objectives and budget allocation of the Ministry / Department / Organisation, in accordance with the rules and guidelines of the Ministry of Finance, while also forecasting future expenditures. Manages and monitors the Division/Department's budget, accounts & expenditure, while promoting financial prudence within the Department to enhance overall efficiency. Develops proficiency in handling PFMS (Public Financial Management System).
sub_theme_description: Utilises the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) to ensure transparent and accountable financial management within the Ministry/Department/Organisation. This includes enrolling and managing implementing agencies and recipients, mapping schemes, and maintaining accurate beneficiary records. Generates, interprets, and analyses PFMS reports, including operational, performance, fund flow, and daily transaction summaries, to track utilisation and identify discrepancies. Performs accounting functions, reconciles PFMS records with physical accounts, and maintains a complete audit trail for compliance with Ministry of Finance rules. Monitors expenses, programs, and grants to ensure funds are released, utilised, and reported in line with approved allocations and financial guidelines. Strength in this competency supports accurate forecasting, informed decision-making, and enhanced efficiency in public financial management.

proficiency_levels.label: Accurately carries out basic PFMS operations
proficiency_levels.description:
Enters and updates implementing agency and beneficiary details in PFMS (for e.g., Aadhaar/bank validation, IFSC verification, duplicate record checks, etc) with complete documentation within prescribed timelines to ensure traceable onboarding. Records sanctions, fund releases, expenditures, and vouchers in PFMS using prescribed workflows (for e.g., sanction order entry, bill-wise/voucher-wise posting, bank scroll updates, etc) following the maker–checker process to ensure compliance with GFR 2017 and MoF guidelines.
Generates standard PFMS reports (for e.g., daily transactions, utilisation certificate, expenditure summary, etc) using predefined formats and filters.
Understands the fund lifecycle within PFMS (sanction, release, utilisation, UC submission, reconciliation) and performs assigned tasks accordingly.
Uploads supporting documents in prescribed formats, tags transactions with sanction orders and UC references, and maintains scheme-wise chronological records to ensure audit readiness.
Applies data protection and access control protocols (for e.g., official login credentials, log-out discipline, masking personal identifiers, etc) in accordance with UIDAI Section 7 and MoF data-handling advisories. Resolves basic operational issues using PFMS Helpdesk manuals, FAQs, and nodal guidance before escalation. I accurately enrol agencies and record transactions in PFMS with complete documentation and maker–checker compliance.
I generate and reconcile PFMS reports within prescribed timelines to prevent financial discrepancies.
I maintain traceable audit records so every transaction can be verified against source documents.

proficiency_levels.label: Manages PFMS operations for assigned schemes, ensuring compliance and validating reports
proficiency_levels.description:
Manages scheme mapping, agency approvals, and user access controls in PFMS, ensuring correct Scheme–Component–Subcomponent hierarchy and maker–checker alignment. Validates and reconciles fund releases, advances, settlements, and expenditures using PFMS reconciliation tools, bank statements, and sanction records to ensure alignment with BE, RE, and Cash Management Guidelines.
Conducts root-cause analysis of recurring discrepancies (for e.g., mapping errors, Aadhaar validation failures, delayed UCs, etc) and implements corrective controls to improve efficiency and reduce financial risk.
Analyses scheme-wise, division-wise, and exception reports in PFMS to identify discrepancies such as failed transactions (for e.g., Error Code 101), UCs status mismatches, unreconciled advances, and unreflected unspent balances, and initiates timely corrective action.
Coordinates with implementing agencies, DDOs , finance and accounts divisions, PAOs, auditors, and PFMS nodal units to resolve mismatches and update PFMS records.
Prepares consolidated reports (for e.g., scheme utilisation, fund flow, reconciliation statements, etc) for submission to senior officers and Finance Advisors.
Ensures DBT compliance (for e.g., Aadhaar consent/Section 7, bank validation, etc) and masks personal data in outputs to meet UIDAI guidance.
Uses historical utilisation patterns to project short-term expenditure trends and support RE, revalidation, or surrender decisions, strengthening efficient public financial management. Uses PFMS trend data to support QEP monitoring, recommend revalidation or surrender of savings, and flag potential year-end fund parking risks. I manage scheme-level PFMS operations ensuring accurate disbursement, reconciliation, and timely UC closure.
I detect and resolve fund-flow discrepancies through structured analysis and stakeholder coordination.
I provide consolidated PFMS analytics that support compliance, forecasting, and informed expenditure decisions.

proficiency_levels.label: Leads strategic PFMS governance and forecasting to optimise fund utilisation and ensure financial compliance
proficiency_levels.description:
Designs and institutionalises a M/D/O-wide PFMS governance framework with defined SLAs for reconciliation, UC submission, advance adjustment, and reporting to ensure funds are released and accounted for in accordance with GFR 2017 and MoF guidelines.
Develops cash-flow forecasting models using PFMS historical utilisation trends to guide BE, RE, monthly expenditure ceilings, and year-end expenditure management.
Benchmarks departmental fund utilisation performance against CGA advisories and peer ministries, introducing efficiency indicators (for e.g., UC closure cycle time, reconciliation lag, advance settlement period, etc).
