Conducts systematic compliance reviews of parliamentary records against Secretariat guidelines, documentation standards, and retention rules to ensure completeness, defensibility, and timely accessibility.
Identifies gaps, discrepancies, or missing documentation and proactively coordinates with parliamentary branches, Secretariat officials, and internal divisions to obtain authenticated records, ensuring procedural continuity.
Disseminates advance copies of parliamentary documents and approved replies to the Houses and relevant departmental stakeholders, strengthening preparedness, alignment of messaging, and quality of parliamentary engagement. Maintains updated registers, assurance trackers, and session-wise repositories to enable leadership access to historical references and monitor commitments across parliamentary cycles. I ensure parliamentary records and responses are accurate, verified, and procedurally compliant.
I maintain updated assurance trackers and session repositories for seamless retrieval.
I strengthen M/D/O preparedness during parliamentary sessions through structured documentation.

proficiency_levels.label: Strengthens systems for parliamentary record management to ensure institutional continuity and strategic readiness
proficiency_levels.description:
Designs and standardises SOPs, templates, and classification frameworks for parliamentary record management across sessions.
Establishes quality assurance mechanisms (for e.g., periodic audits, validation reviews, reconciliation checks, etc) to maintain accuracy and completeness.
Ensures continuity and timeliness of departmental support for parliamentary operations by maintaining consistent coordination, documentation, and follow-up across parliamentary sessions and house cycles.
Advises divisions on documentation standards and retrieval protocols for rapid response during sessions.
Strengthens coordination mechanisms with Parliamentary Secretariats and internal branches for seamless information flow.
Reviews sensitive parliamentary material handling protocols to mitigate legal and reputational risks.
Analyses recurring parliamentary themes and trends to inform proactive preparation of future briefs. Provides curated historical references and strategic parliamentary compendiums to senior leadership. I institutionalise robust systems that ensure continuity and reliability of parliamentary records.
I strengthen assurance tracking and archival frameworks across sessions.
I provide strategic parliamentary insights that enhance leadership preparedness and responsiveness.

theme_description: Demonstrates thorough knowledge of the RTI Act, 2005, and promptly & appropriately handles RTI responses. Drives proper maintenance of RTI records to ensure procedural compliance as per the established rules. Provides assistance to person(s) seeking information, displaying transparency, good governance, and accountability.
sub_theme_description: Understands the request/query/complaint/appeal and drafts responses by retrieving relevant information available in Section/Division and ensures timely disposal of the requests through PIO (Public Information Officer).

proficiency_levels.label: Applies standard RTI processes and legal requirements to ensure compliant, timely, and transparent handling of information requests
proficiency_levels.description:
Understands departmental protocols for receiving, recording, and acknowledging RTI applications by logging them in designated registers or electronic systems, issuing receipts where required, and maintaining an audit trail to ensure accountability, traceability, and readiness for audits or appeals. Understands and identifies potential exemptions or issues such as missing, untraceable, or partly exempt records by noting relevant RTI Act sections, informing the CPIO, and providing supporting notes to enable accurate categorisation and informed decision-making, ensuring transparency and safeguarding applicant rights.
Recognises the subject matter and priority (e.g., Very Important Person (VIP)/Member of Parliament (MP) labels, public grievances) of RTI requests and accurately categorises and routes them to the correct Section or Division, ensuring effective tracking and timely processing within statutory channels.
Understands institutional roles and responsibilities in RTI processing, including of CPIO, APIO, and FAA , to support precise categorisation, efficient routing, and coordination of RTI process.
Retrieves relevant information strictly from records "held by or under the control of" the public authority by carefully searching indexed files, registers, or digital repositories, ensuring that only accurate, complete, and pre-existing information is shared, in compliance with the RTI Act, 2005, requirement to avoid creating new data.
Identifies and verifies the validity of incoming RTI applications by checking for the prescribed documentation as mandated under Section 6(1) of the RTI Act, 2005, ensuring that only complete and compliant applications proceed while rejecting incomplete submissions with clear reasons to prevent delays in processing.
Records and tracks the status and movement of RTI files or requests by updating physical registers or electronic systems with dates and actions taken, enabling clear monitoring of statutory timelines such as the 30-day disposal requirement under Section 7(1), thereby reducing the risk of missed deadlines and deemed refusals.
Supports the CPIO in transferring RTI applications to the appropriate public authority within the five-day limit under Section 6(3) by preparing transfer letters, notifying applicants of the receiving authority’s details, and recording transfer dates to ensure procedural compliance and applicant awareness.
Drafts clear, legally compliant responses to applicants to RTI requests using departmental templates and guidelines, including confirmation of information provided, requests for additional fees as per RTI Rules, 2012, or justified rejections citing Sections 8, 9, or 24, to ensure consistent, transparent, and error-free communication with applicants. Maintains and updates knowledge of RTI provisions, exemptions, and departmental procedures by regularly reviewing DoPT circulars, attending training workshops, and sharing important updates with colleagues to improve legal compliance, service quality, and the organisation’s overall capacity to respond effectively to RTI requests. I verify and process incoming RTI applications to ensure they are complete, compliant, and ready for timely legal disposal.
I retrieve and share accurate, pre-existing records to support the PIO in drafting clear and legally compliant responses.
I track and document the movement of RTI requests to maintain accountability and meet statutory timelines for citizen information access.

proficiency_levels.label: Analyses, organises, and coordinates RTI processes to ensure efficient and legally sound information disclosure across the M/D/O
proficiency_levels.description:
Analyses the clarity, validity, and supporting documentation of RTI applications by confirming subject matter specificity, payment of prescribed fees, and Section 6 compliance, incorporating quality assurance checks to ensure early identification of issues and reduce errors, rejections, appeals, and delays. Organises and coordinates effective routing of applications and follow-up requests by liaising with other Sections, Divisions, and M/D/Os to gather all necessary information, ensuring complete responses to complex queries.
Implements systematic search protocols and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to collate, verify, and analyse records from physical and digital archives, confirming accuracy, completeness, and relevance to support the CPIO’s assessment of exemptions and partial disclosure opportunities, including “severance” as per Sections 8, 9, and 24.
Monitors the movement and status of RTI files in the section using registers or digital tools, spotting delays and fixing issues to meet statutory deadlines (30 days, 48 hours for life or liberty cases), ensuring compliance and avoiding deemed refusals.
Manages section-level work allocation, scheduling, and resource use (e.g., assigning staff to tasks, balancing workloads) by setting section-level deadlines aligned with statutory requirements, and prioritising urgent or VIP requests, ensuring the CPIO receives complete, validated information on time to avoid penalties and maintain service standards.
Drafts thorough, clear, and well-reasoned preliminary responses or notes for PIO review by explaining legal grounds for exemptions, calculating additional fees, and outlining appeal procedures, ensuring all replies meet statutory requirements for clarity, accuracy, and “speaking order” standards.
Collaborates with the CPIO to address retrieval challenges, identifying records containing exempt and non-exempt elements, recommending severance approaches, and preparing well-documented justifications for partial disclosure or rejection in compliance with the Act’s mandate for “speaking orders,” promoting transparency and defensibility of decisions in the M/D/O.
Reviews updates to the RTI Act, Central Information Commission (CIC) Orders, case laws, and departmental circulars to stay informed about changes affecting exemptions, transfers, and disclosure obligations.
Guides and trains peers and subordinates by interpreting updates on the RTI Act, 2005, and explains their implications to ensure consistent and legally sound handling of RTI processes within the team. Supervises the maintenance and enhancement of record management practices to facilitate accessible, compliant retrieval for RTI processing and proactive disclosures under Section 4(1)(b) in the M/D/O. I analyse and validate RTI applications and records to reduce errors, appeals, and delays while supporting legal compliance.
I coordinate and organise information retrieval across sections and M/D/Os to ensure complete, accurate, and timely responses to complex queries.
I monitor and manage the progress and handling of RTI requests to meet statutory deadlines and deliver high quality, legally compliant services to applicants.

proficiency_levels.label: Leads and strengthens RTI responsiveness in delivering legally sound, timely information to the citizens
proficiency_levels.description:
Evaluates and standardises RTI application screening by overseeing section-level checklists and protocols for consistent verification of fee payments, documentation, and formal compliance under Section 6 of the RTI Act, enabling quality control and timely processing. Designs information sharing procedures with other M/D/Os by developing clear agreements, ensuring comprehensive and consistent responses to RTI requests, and promoting accurate disclosures.
Establishes and enforces standards for consolidating records and inputs from diverse sections and external authorities to support consistent, legally defensible analysis of applicable exemptions (Sections 8, 9, and 24), managing third-party consultations and ensuring compliant partial disclosures.
Implements monitoring systems for RTI file tracking by designing digital registers, escalation protocols, and proactively addressing delays to maintain strict statutory timelines (30 days, 48 hours for life or liberty matters, 5 additional days for APIO-originated requests), preventing deemed refusals.
Anchors strategic prioritisation of RTI matters in section work planning by allocating resources, setting staff performance targets, scheduling workloads, etc to promote consistent, timely, and legally compliant service delivery in the M/D/O.
Designs and continuously improves department wide SOPs for transferring RTI applications to other public authorities within the statutory 5-day limit, specifying steps for preparing transfer letters, notifying applicants of the receiving authority's details, and documenting all transfer related actions.
Promotes continuous learning and capacity-building on RTI law and practice by leading internal training sessions, briefings, and mentoring on RTI legislation, Central Information Commission (CIC) interpretations, legal exemptions, departmental guidelines, and best practices, to improve team readiness towards RTI responsiveness.
Guide and mentors staff in drafting clear, well-reasoned, and legally defensible responses that appropriately cite RTI Act sections (e.g., Section 8 exemptions, Section 4(1)(b) proactive disclosures), ensuring transparency, safeguarding sensitive information, and strengthening citizen’s trust in government responsiveness.
Drives improvements in Section record management by leading digitisation initiatives, enhancing indexing and cataloguing practices, and enabling citizen centric dissemination of information to strengthen Section 4(1)(b) proactive disclosures to reduce RTI application volumes, and improve transparency in the M/D/O. Leads the preparation, quality assurance, and legal review of complex or sensitive RTI responses, especially those involving third-party consultations, national security exemptions, or high-profile applicants, ensuring all responses are legally sound, consistent with CIC expectations, and defensible during appeals or audits. I standardise and lead RTI screening and response processes to ensure consistent, legally sound, and timely service delivery across the M/D/O.
I coordinate M/D/O wide information sharing and synthesise records to support the PIO in delivering well reasoned and exemption-compliant responses.
I institutionalise monitoring, training, and record management improvements to strengthen transparency, accountability, and citizen trust in government RTI responsiveness.

theme_description: Demonstrates the ability to address grievances promptly and efficiently while prioritiSing transparency and citizen-centricity. Utilizes the Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) to manage grievance redressal, ensuring access of the digital systems to all citizens, tracking their status, and obtaining resolutions in accordance with established guidelines and procedures. Measures the effectiveness and efficiency of the Department/Ministry's administration by analysing data and providing feedback for enhancing processes and procedures.
sub_theme_description: Demonstrates the ability to monitor reports & dashboards of grievances received, pending for closure, and resolved cases as per the requirement of Ministries/Departments/Organizations for driving effective resolution for pending grievances.

proficiency_levels.label: Executes CPGRAMS grievance registration processes accurately to ensure compliant and traceable grievance handling
proficiency_levels.description:
Demonstrates working familiarity with the CPGRAMS portal interface (for e.g., grievance inbox, dashboard filters, appeal module, status history tab, report extraction features, etc) by navigating and performing routine actions without supervisory intervention.
Describes grievance categories and subcategories (for e.g., service delay, procedural grievance, staff behaviour, accessibility barrier, scheme eligibility issues, etc) from CPGRAMS semantic analysis dropdown and applies correct scheme tagging and deduplication validation to maintain data accuracy.
Registers and acknowledges grievances on CPGRAMS within 3 working days as per DARPG compliance, applying correct grievance category and sub-category from the CPGRAMS taxonomy dropdown.
Assigns grievances to the correct division/section using CPGRAMS workflow mapping and records file linkage number in e-Office to ensure traceability.
Generates daily pendency and aging reports from the CPGRAMS dashboard using date and registration ID filters and flags cases nearing the 21-day disposal norm to the Section Officer.
Performs basic reconciliation between CPGRAMS status updates and e-Office file movements and flags mismatches like missing ATRs to ensure file-portal alignment.
Maintains complete audit trails by recording every action in CPGRAMS status history notes (what/who/when) and links supporting documents using the attachment feature to ensure traceability.
Verifies that closure remarks clearly address each grievance point and reference applicable scheme guidelines, Citizen Charter timelines, or relevant Office Memoranda. Coordinates with subordinate offices/field units through CPGRAMS reminder feature and records follow-up dates in status notes to prevent pendency. I register and route grievances correctly within DARPG timelines.
I maintain complete digital audit trails aligned with e-Office records.
I ensure replies are evidence-based and clearly address citizen concerns.

proficiency_levels.label: Improves grievance performance through data-driven monitoring and timely disposal standards
proficiency_levels.description:
Analyses monthly CPGRAMS MIS data (for e.g., pendency, aging, appeal rate, feedback score, etc) and prepares consolidated variance dashboards for leadership review, highlighting section-wise deviations and corrective priorities.
Design and monitoring internal SLA trackers aligned with the 21-day DARPG norm and Citizen Charter timelines using CPGRAMS export data in Excel/MIS dashboards.
Identifies duplicate or misclassified grievances using CPGRAMS validation reports and issues corrective instructions to sections.
Conducts fortnightly grievance review meetings using CPGRAMS dashboard projections and records action points with responsible officers and disposal deadlines.
Uses the CPGRAMS Tree Dashboard AI to identify top recurring grievance themes and CAPA notes, referencing scheme guidelines or procedural gaps.
Standardises grievance reply templates and quality checklists, and conducts monthly sample audits to ensure first-time-right disposal.
Reviews appeal pendency and reversal rate from the CPGRAMS appellate module and directs sections to revise closure quality where required. Performs quarterly access audits of CPGRAMS user roles and disables inactive accounts in coordination with the Ministry’s CPGRAMS Nodal Admin to ensure data security compliance. I analyse CPGRAMS data to identify performance gaps and drive corrective action across sections.
I enforce SLA timelines and strengthen grievance disposal quality.
I reduce appeals, rework, and repeat grievances by strengthening disposal standards and monitoring compliance.

proficiency_levels.label: Leads grievance performance by setting clear targets, and driving systemic improvements using CPGRAMS data
proficiency_levels.description:
Reviews M/D/O-level CPGRAMS performance indicators (for e.g., overall pendency, average disposal time, appeal reversal percentage, citizen feedback score, etc) and issues written performance directions to divisions.
Reviews M/D/O performance against DARPG rankings and sets clear targets (for e.g., reduce long-pending cases by 30%, lower appeal rate by 10%, improve citizen feedback score, etc).
Oversees high-risk grievances (for e.g., legal matters, parliamentary references, media-sensitive cases, etc) flagged through CPGRAMS and activates escalation matrix within 48 hours.
Approves and operationalises M/D/O-wide Grievance Redressal SOP aligned with DARPG OM, linking disposal timelines with e-Office workflow controls.
Directs independent internal audit of CPGRAMS data integrity (for e.g., status mismatch, delayed uploads, incomplete ATRs, etc) and ensures rectification within defined timelines.
Uses grievance analytics (for e.g., repeat grievance rate, geographic clustering, scheme-wise trends, etc) to recommend policy clarifications, FAQ revisions, and track impact on grievance inflow.
Publishes quarterly grievance performance summaries (for e.g., pendency, disposal rate, systemic improvements, etc) on the Ministry website to strengthen transparency and public trust.
Champions CPGRAMS innovations (for e.g., bulk closure, horizontal transfers, AI theme classification, etc) and implements efficiency improvements to reduce disposal time. Leads capacity building through iGOT-aligned certifications, structured grievance clinics for GROs , and participation in DARPG benchmarking forums to sustain performance improvement. I set clear performance targets for grievance disposal.
I ensure sustained reduction in pendency and appeals across divisions.
I use grievance data to drive policy and process improvements.

theme_description: Demonstrates a thorough understanding and practical application of administrative vigilance and disciplinary procedures, which serve as safeguards to ensure the proper implementation of government processes, policies, and rules, while identifying instances of breach by government employees who may abuse their authority or power of approval for personal gain. Facilitates in building a positive perception and image of the government and its policies, both within the government ecosystem, among citizens, and globally. Adheres to guidelines on implementation of strict anti-corruption measures, vigilant oversight, and a commitment to integrity in public service.
sub_theme_description: Understands the extent, applicability, intent, and content of the Central Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1964 (updated) for Government servants with a view to maintain integrity in public services by taking required action to promote its adherence.

proficiency_levels.label: Follows prescribed conduct rules and compliance practices
proficiency_levels.description:
Identifies provisions of the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 (updated), such as Rule 13 (Gifts), Rule 15 (Private trade or employment), and Rule 22 (Consumption of intoxicating drinks and drugs), among others, to uphold integrity in public services. Recognises institutional structures (e.g. Central Vigilance Commission (CVC), Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT), disciplinary authorities, among others), including their roles and jurisdiction in enforcing CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 (updated).
Identifies standard procedures for disciplinary matters, such as receipt of complaint, preliminary inquiry, issue of charge sheet, submission of written statements, among others, in line with the guidelines for disciplinary procedure for CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 (updated) mentioned in the Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965.
Follows basic compliance practices such as disclosure of assets, handling of gifts, prevention of conflicts of interest, etc among others to uphold integrity in public services.
Follows prescribed steps for documenting breaches (e.g., gift violations, unexplained assets) using digital vigilance portals such as Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS), CVC Complaint Management System, among others.
Examines digital system records (e.g., e-office audit trails, electronic file movement systems, Government e-Marketplace [GeM] logs, time-stamped approval workflows, digital attendance and access logs, and CCTV surveillance records, among others) to trace accountability gaps. Maintains impartiality while reporting inconsistencies in basic administrative processes (e.g., approvals, file noting, procurement, among others) that may indicate compliance risks. I understand the intent, scope, and key provisions of the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 (updated)
I apply the rules and report basic compliance risks using prescribed digital and institutional channels
I follow standard procedures impartially when flagging breaches or irregularities.

proficiency_levels.label: Strengthens adherence to conduct rules by identifying gaps, mentoring peers, and documenting violations
proficiency_levels.description:
Evaluates administrative procedures (e.g., approvals, file noting, procurement, among others) to identify systemic gaps that could lead to misconduct or reputational risks. Analyses data from digital system records (e.g., e-office audit trails, electronic file movement systems, Government e-Marketplace [GeM] logs, time-stamped approval workflows, digital attendance and access logs, and CCTV surveillance records) to identify patterns of non-compliance and recommend corrective measures.
Analyses compliance exceptions (e.g., procurement lapses, service delays) and proposes targeted corrective measures.
Drafts departmental circulars, SOPs, and advisories to strengthen adherence to the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964, promote uniform compliance, and reinforce a culture of integrity and transparency in public service.
Leads internal reviews of select cases and prepares structured reports that support decision-making by disciplinary authorities. Mentors team members on vigilance procedures, CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 (updated), use of digital vigilance tools, and documentation protocols, to promote shared accountability and procedural consistency. I analyse procedures and workflows to identify risks and recommend transparent, tech-enabled alternatives.
I investigate rule breaches and document findings using evidence and conduct rule mapping.
I lead select compliance reviews and sensitise teams to ensure consistent vigilance practices.

proficiency_levels.label: Leads vigilance systems by embedding conduct rules into departmental workflows and driving transparency reforms
proficiency_levels.description:
Conducts risk assessment of departmental workflows to identify malpractice sources workflows to identify malpractice sources (e.g., multiple-window clearances, discretionary approvals, manual file processing, opaque procurement processes, among others) and proposes transparent alternatives (e.g., single-window clearances, e-tenders, automated workflow systems, e-office file tracking, online public dashboards, etc) to uphold integrity in public services. Promotes the use of technology-enabled corrective measures (e.g., blockchain records, AI-audit systems, public-facing vigilance dashboards, among others) to preempt breaches and enhance transparency in public service delivery.
Establishes department-wide compliance frameworks aligned with CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 (updated) and national priorities such as Zero Tolerance Against Corruption, Viksit Bharat, Aatmanirbhar Bharat, among others.
Oversees complex disciplinary matters, ensuring procedural fairness, documentation integrity, and accountability to law and citizens.
Conducts internal vigilance reviews in collaboration with designated authorities to evaluate the effectiveness of existing conduct enforcement mechanisms and identify areas for structural or procedural reform.
Leads collaboration with key stakeholders such as CVC, DOPT, etc. to refine vigilance protocols, while incorporating feedback from citizen grievance systems and institutional audits.
Approves departmental circulars, SOPs, and advisories to strengthen adherence to the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964, promote uniform compliance, and reinforce a culture of integrity and transparency in public service. Builds a culture of ethical leadership, reinforcing accountability across vertical and horizontal structures within the organisation. I promote technology-enabled systems to prevent misconduct and enhance transparency.
I collaborate with key institutions to strengthen vigilance frameworks through institutional audits and citizen feedback.
I build a culture of ethical leadership and systemic accountability across the organisation.

sub_theme_description: Displays understanding of extent, applicability and intent of the CCS (CCA)(Classification, control & Appeal) Rules, 1965- Central Civil Services, Group 'A', Group ‘B’, ‘C’, ’D’ (classification of service, posts), AIS (Discipline & Appeal) Rules, 1969 for officers from All India Services, Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal (CCA)) Rules, 1965 (rule 10); Fundamental Rules (FR) 53 & 54 (b), in relation to provisions and circumstances under which a Government servant may be placed under suspension in the Ministry/Department. Ensures timely payment of subsistence allowance in cases of suspension.

proficiency_levels.label: Understands key suspension rules and assists in suspension documentation and subsistence allowance processing
proficiency_levels.description:
Understands and identifies key provisions of Rule 10 of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965, AIS (D&A) Rules, 1969, and FR 53 & 54-B, and identifies what suspension means and the common grounds under which it may occur, ensuring correct understanding and preliminary assessment of suspension situations. Recognises the distinctions between suspension, deemed suspension, and revocation, including the roles of disciplinary and appointing authorities, to enable accurate categorisation and routing of cases in line with legal mandates.
Follows prescribed formats and instructions for maintaining suspension-related records, including use of DoPT templates and prescribed documentation formats, to ensure standardised, secure and audit-ready recordkeeping.
Assists in preparing simple draft notes/orders related to suspension with guidance and records grounds for suspension in file, to ensure timely and defensible documentation.
Processes routine steps for subsistence allowance (data entry, forwarding, and verification) and assists in initial preparation of claims to ensure accurate and timely administrative processing.
Maintains confidentiality and handles documents to protect sensitive information and uphold procedural integrity. Seeks clarification when the interpretation of rules or processes is unclear, to prevent procedural errors and ensure accurate application of suspension provisions. I understand the provisions, scope, and basic procedures under Rule 10, AIS (D&A) Rules, and FR 53/54-B.
I prepare basic suspension documentation and process subsistence allowance steps accurately.

proficiency_levels.label: Manages suspension cases ensuring statutory compliance and accurate allowance administration
proficiency_levels.description:
Applies CCS (CCA) Rule 10, FR 53, FR 54-B, and AIS (D&A) Rules accurately to cases to ensure suspension decisions and allowance processes comply with statutory provisions and M/D/O integrity standards.
Reviews suspension cases for the accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of periodic reviews and monitors statutory timelines (for e.g., 90-day review, extensions, etc), escalating delays where necessary, to ensure that continuation or revocation decisions follow due process and mandated review cycles.
Analyses disciplinary/vigilance data to identify trends in delays, non-compliance, or documentation gaps, and recommends corrective measures to enable process improvements and reduce repeat procedural lapses.
Drafts departmental advisories, SOPs, and structured reports on suspension cases in line with DoPT/CVC guidance and prepares materials for disciplinary authorities to support standardised practices and informed decision making.
Maintains complete and well-indexed suspension records, ensuring they are ready for audit to enable easy tracking and institutional transparency.
Calculates and processes subsistence allowance accurately, including DA and admissible compensatory allowances, while verifying required certifications (e.g., non-engagement in other employment) to ensure timely and compliant financial support during suspension.
Coordinates with vigilance units, disciplinary authorities, and investigative agencies (for e.g., police, CBI, etc) to obtain case updates and required records for reviews, to enable informed and timely decision making. Maintains compliance with procedural requirements and confidentiality norms and mentors team members on drafting, recordkeeping, and allowances processing to safeguard case integrity and build departmental capability. I administer subsistence allowance accurately and coordinate with relevant authorities to support timely decision making.

proficiency_levels.label: Provides guidance and oversight to ensure lawful, proportionate, and defensible suspension administration
proficiency_levels.description:

Mentors officers and review committees on rule-consistent interpretation, documentation quality, and principles of natural justice. sub_theme_description: Demonstrates prudence and clarity in comprehending and implementing The Public Servants Enquiries Act and action on complaints forwarded by the Administrative Ministry/Department. Disposal of complaints of non-vigilance nature, Action on anonymous/pseudonymous complaints, procedure for dealing with complaints and engagement of retired officials to conduct Investigation and perform other vigilance functions

proficiency_levels.label: Gathers and organises initial facts and evidence to support the commencement of disciplinary proceedings
proficiency_levels.description:
Demonstrates awareness of essential legal policies, rules, etc., e.g., the Public Servants Enquiries Act, CCS (Conduct, Discipline & Appeal) Rules (Chapter 18), Revised AIS Rule (Vol I, Rule 12) and guidelines from the Vigilance Manual (CVC 2021).
Applies basic principles of natural justice, maintains confidentiality in routine tasks, and adheres to prescribed procedural timelines with consistency (for e.g., uses standard confidentiality covers, vigilance file classification codes, etc).
Identifies complaint category (for e.g., vigilance, non-vigilance, or A/P) using the CVC admissibility grid or departmental categorisation matrix.
Comprehends administrative processes related to disposal of complaints, including non-vigilance cases, anonymous/pseudonymous complaints, and the role of retired officials in investigations.
Updates vigilance case progress using departmental MIS fields such as ‘Stage’, ‘Timeline’, ‘Action Taken’, and ‘Pending Inputs’.
Assists disciplinary authorities in the preparation of preliminary documentation, charge sheets, and related reports.

Observes ethical standards and confidentiality protocols during documentation and communication management. I identify relevant rules and route the case to the correct authority.

proficiency_levels.label: Drafts charge sheets and disciplinary proposals, ensuring admissibility and due process
proficiency_levels.description:

Ensures due process, adherence to fair inquiry principles, and compliance with timelines using statutory timeline charts, issuance logs, and vigilance MIS alert functions.
Maintains effective liaison with vigilance sections, legal departments, and administrative authorities for smooth procedural flow.
Tracks case status using vigilance digital dashboards, pendency trackers, and workflow audit logs for transparency.
Reviews regulatory updates using DoPT circulars and departmental regulatory trackers.
Prepares draft FRs and speaking notes using approved FR-drafting templates and rule-citation reference sheets. Documents mandatory consultations (for e.g., vigilance, legal, CVC, UPSC, etc) using consultation registers, advice-upload modules, and advice-reference coding formats. proficiency_levels.label: Oversees the disciplinary processes, evaluates inquiry reports, and ensures a fair, evidence-based, and legally defensible conclusion
proficiency_levels.description:
Leads process optimisation and reform initiatives to enhance the efficacy and compliance of disciplinary proceedings. Provides expert advice on legislative amendments, provisions and policy updates, including integration of amended CCS (Conduct, Discipline & Appeal)/AIS (All India Service) rules and the Vigilance Commission’s guidelines.
Champions capacity building interventions to build team competencies in disciplinary preparation and case management.

Maintains archive of posts, comments, and DMs as per Public Records Act, 1993 using a content inventory (for e.g., ID, date, platform, status).
Tracks basic KPIs (for e.g., reach, engagement rate, response time, etc) using platform insights or spreadsheet, flagging unusual spikes linked to campaigns or news cycles. Routes grievances to CPGRAMS/State grievance portals and replies with reference numbers within defined timelines. I publish verified and accessible updates that guide citizens to official services and helplines.
I respond to, and route citizen queries through CPGRAMS or approved systems within defined timelines.
I maintain secure, compliant, and auditable records of social media activity.

proficiency_levels.label: Manages multi-platform communication and moderation to improve citizen understanding and trust
proficiency_levels.description:
Plans and executes coordinated campaigns across social media platforms to explain schemes, highlight service benefits, and improve public understanding of the M/D/Os work, adapting content formats for different audiences (for e.g., reels, explainers, FAQs, etc).
Develops content calendars linked to programme milestones and Cabinet/Parliament sessions.
Designs and enforces moderation policy (for e.g., response scripts, tone guidelines, privacy norms, do-not-engage list) aligned with IT Rules, 2021 and DPDP Act, 2023.
Establishes and monitors Service Level Agreements for citizen responsiveness, ensuring timely and empathetic communication that builds trust.
Implements simple audience and content tagging to identify stakeholder groups that need additional clarification or awareness, and supports targeted communication when gaps are observed.
Produces monthly analytics reports, sentiment analysis and behavioural insights, to recommend content pivots that improve clarity, advocacy, and citizen comprehension.
Coordinates with programme divisions, NIC, PIB liaison, and legal cell before issuing sensitive updates (for e.g., disaster alerts, policy corrections, etc).
Monitors platform insights and public feedback monthly, identifying trending concerns and information gaps, to refine messaging and improve public understanding. Uses social listening and citizen feedback to identify misinformation themes, then publishes evidence-based clarifications (linked to official releases/notifications), to address misconceptions and reduce harm. I design and manage coordinated campaigns that improve citizen understanding of schemes and entitlements.
I moderate discussions and correct misinformation using verified sources.
I use analytics and citizen feedback to refine messaging and strengthen service delivery outcomes.

proficiency_levels.label: Leads M/D/O-wide social media strategy, governance, and crisis communication to strengthen public trust and service outcomes
proficiency_levels.description:
Defines M/D/O-wide social media strategy aligned with policy priorities, citizen needs, and annual communication plans.
Establishes governance structures (for e.g., role matrix, approval tiers, vendor controls, access lifecycle management, etc) in coordination with NIC and IT divisions to ensure high quality and consistent dissemination of information.
Develops crisis communication playbooks for high-risk scenarios (for e.g., disasters, public health alerts, data breaches, misinformation spikes, etc), including decision rights and escalation routes, to enable rapid, coordinated public guidance.
Integrates social listening with policy teams to provide structured insights on citizen sentiments, misconceptions, emerging grievances, and information gaps, enabling programme divisions to improve policy communication and messaging.
Conducts periodic compliance audits covering IT Rules 2021, DPDP Act 2023, Public Records Act 1993, State Emblem of India Act 2005, and GIGW 3.0 accessibility.
Defines measurable impact indicators (for e.g., portal traffic, verified grievance closure rate, scheme application spikes, citizen trust sentiment index, etc).
Champions inclusive and multilingual communication by setting targets for vernacular reach, accessibility compliance, representation, and clarity, ensuring that diverse citizens understand government initiatives.
Leads compliance reviews for social media operations (for e.g., IT Rules, data protection requirements, election-period restrictions, emblem/branding rules, etc), documenting findings and corrective actions, to reduce legal and reputational risk. Allocates budgets using cost-per-outcome metrics (e.g., verified query resolution, scheme uptake, traffic to gov portals, etc.), ensuring resources are spent on efforts that strengthen advocacy and improve public awareness. I set and govern the M/D/Os social media strategy to ensure consistent, compliant, and service-oriented communication.
I lead coordinated crisis and misinformation responses across departments to provide timely and verified public guidance.
I measure and report digital communication impact on awareness, service uptake, and citizen trust.

theme_description: Disseminates information through various media channels on behalf of the government to increase public awareness and advocacy of government policies and schemes, and addresses any misconceptions using a range of media vehicles such as government websites. Facilitates in generating positive media coverage, building relationships with key stakeholders, managing conflicts or criticisms, and improving public understanding of a Ministry/Department/Organisation and its objectives. Utilises social media to communicate official government policies and information to the public, with a focus on creating an informed citizenry through a people-centric communication approach.
sub_theme: Management of Information on Official Websites
sub_theme_description: Ensures compliance with the ‘Guidelines for Indian Government Websites’ (GIGW) in maintaining official websites of all Central Government Ministries, Departments, Offices, and CPSEs. This includes keeping data and information up to date and providing user-friendly interfaces and transactions that meet the high expectations of citizens and customers regarding security, the privacy of personal data, and the accuracy of information.

proficiency_levels.label: Maintains accurate, traceable, and GIGW-compliant content for website sections
proficiency_levels.description:
Identifies and categorises the required information elements for assigned government web pages (for e.g., statutory disclosures, scheme/service details, notices, forms, contacts, FAQs, privacy/accessibility statements, etc) using the GIGW checklist, ensuring published content remains complete, accurate, and compliant for citizens.
Maintains an inventory of assigned pages (for e.g., URL, content owner, last reviewed date, etc) and updates it weekly to ensure every page has a clear owner and review cycle.
Publishes approved updates in the CMS within defined timelines (for e.g., minor text updates within 3 working days) to keep citizen-facing information current.
Applies a pre-publication checklist (for e.g., bilingual parity in Hindi/English, “Last Updated” date, contact details, accessibility statement link, etc).
Verifies links, downloadable PDFs, forms, and embedded media before and after publishing, logging broken link fixes within defined SLAs.
Ensures accessibility basics (for e.g., proper heading structure, alt text, meaningful link text, etc) and runs automated checks using GIGW accessibility validators or similar tools.
Applies privacy safeguards in line with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (for e.g., purpose statement, consent text, minimal data collection in forms, etc).
Uses safe content-handling practices (for e.g., approved file formats, NIC-hosted links, malware scanning where available, etc) and escalates suspected issues to NIC/IT. Archives superseded documents with version labels (for e.g., date, owner, file reference, etc) as per record retention schedules to support RTI responses and audit verification. I ensure multiple website sections remain compliant and updated.
I use dashboards, grievance trends, and search analytics to prioritise improvements and simplify citizen journeys.
I coordinate accessibility, privacy and security across divisions to maintain consistent standards.

proficiency_levels.label: Coordinates multi-section website governance, compliance, and quality assurance
proficiency_levels.description:
Establishes a periodic content review calendar with focal points across divisions and tracks completion to ensure all sections are reviewed and updated on time.
Maintains GIGW 3.0 and STQC readiness documentation (for e.g., evidence folders, screenshots, approval trails, etc) and tracks remediation through defined closure timelines.
Reviews CPGRAMS grievance trends and RTI queries linked to website information gaps and initiates corrective content updates.
Runs a monthly quality dashboard (for e.g., content freshness, broken links, top searched terms, form drop-offs, etc) and logs improvement actions with owners to improve findability and completion of citizen tasks.
Operates an accessibility process (for e.g., published accessibility statement, issue-reporting channel, periodic keyboard/screen-reader spot checks, etc) and tracks fixes to reduce barriers for persons with disabilities.
Implements structured publishing standards (for e.g., HTML and accessible PDF for key documents, metadata tagging for search optimisation, etc).
Implements data protection and records practices for web content (for e.g., privacy notice updates, consent wording control, upload retention/expiration checks, takedown workflow, etc) to reduce privacy risk and prevent the exposure of stale personal data.
Coordinates with NIC /IT teams to ensure timely patch updates, secure CMS configurations, and proper hosting settings, and maintains documented proof of closure to prevent security risks. Conducts periodic content clinics for section owners (for e.g., GIGW do’s/don’ts, bilingual consistency, proactive RTI disclosures, etc) to improve first-time-right publishing. I ensure multiple website sections remain compliant, updated, and audit-ready through structured review cycles.
I use dashboards, grievance trends, and search analytics to prioritise improvements and simplify citizen journeys.
I coordinate accessibility, privacy, security, and STQC readiness across divisions to maintain consistent standards.

proficiency_levels.label: Institutionalises M/D/O-web governance, risk management, and citizen-centric digital standards
proficiency_levels.description:
Issues and enforces a M/D/O-wide Web Governance Policy (for e.g., roles, RACI, approval workflows, retention, takedown, escalation) aligned with GIGW, MeitY advisories, and NIC hosting norms.
Establishes a GIGW-aligned design system (for e.g., templates, components, pattern library, etc) and rollout plan so that all departmental sites share consistent branding, navigation, and semantic HTML structures.
Institutionalises sustained STQC Website Quality Certification readiness through structured internal audits and corrective action governance.
Establishes a M/D/O-wide web risk register (for e.g., content accuracy risk, privacy exposure risk, uptime risk, reputational risk, accessibility risk, etc).
Embeds privacy-by-design and security-by-design principles in web transactions, including periodic privacy impact assessments for new forms.
Defines service quality and performance standards (for e.g., content freshness thresholds, availability targets, response time expectations, user satisfaction measures, etc) and reviews them to drive measurable improvements in public service delivery.
Aligns website disclosures and datasets with Open Government Data (data.gov.in) standards to improve transparency and public trust. Establishes a structured user research and feedback governance framework (for e.g., usability testing for high-impact services, feedback loops, transaction success monitoring, etc) and translates findings into roadmap decisions. I institutionalise privacy, accessibility, security, and risk controls to protect citizen data and ensure reliable digital services.
I drive measurable improvements in transparency, usability, and trust across official government websites.

theme_description: Adopts a structured approach for the effective initiation and implementation of multi-level, multi-faceted changes in the government ecosystem, with the aim of achieving a prescribed mandate as part of a Govt. program, scheme, project, or government initiative. Drives preparedness to unlearn and relearn, communicates the need for change to gain stakeholder acceptance and shared commitment, and drives change from the current state to the desired future state.
sub_theme_description: Communicates effectively, enabling to comprehend the cause and purpose of proposed change, the vision of the change, and the anticipated impact (such as increased efficiency in processes, transparency, speed, accuracy, etc.) for the beneficiaries (including government employees, staff, citizens, etc.), in order to foster willingness and preparedness to adopt the change.

proficiency_levels.label: Understands and identifies the stated purpose and rationale of proposed changes
proficiency_levels.description:
Understands and identifies the stated purpose and rationale of proposed changes (for e.g., introduction of a new SOP , portal, reporting format, etc) by reviewing official communications, circulars, or guidelines. Describes the key features and intended outcomes of the change initiative such as anticipated impact, increased efficiency in processes, transparency, speed, accuracy, etc. to peers or supervisors, ensuring its correct interpretation.
Explains how the proposed change affects one’s own tasks and responsibilities by comparing current practices with revised procedures or systems.
Articulates beneficiary-facing benefits and acknowledges initial concerns or adjustments required during the transition.
Uses newly introduced tools, formats, or digital systems (for e.g., updated e-Office modules, revised MIS formats, etc) as instructed, demonstrating willingness to move away from legacy practices.
Raises clarification requests or flags basic challenges through appropriate channels and incorporates corrective feedback within defined timelines. Recognises potential disruptions or challenges during early adoption and seeks guidance to minimise impact on routine work or service delivery. I understand why a change has been introduced and how it affects my work within the team.
I adopt new systems, processes, or tools as instructed to support their effective implementation.
I contribute to an effective transition by seeking clarifications and following revised procedures.

proficiency_levels.label: Facilitates team readiness and adoption of change by aligning processes and supporting transition to new ways of working
proficiency_levels.description:
Interprets change objectives and implementation plans by assessing differences between current processes and the desired future state for team deliverables.
Communicates the purpose, vision, and expected benefits of the change to team members and stakeholders using clear, context-specific messaging to build their shared understanding.
Aligns team processes, roles, and timelines with revised guidelines by planning structured transition steps and clarifying interim responsibilities to ensure consistent and timely adoption of the change.
Identifies resistance or concerns related to change by systematically reviewing staff feedback, implementation queries, and early adoption patterns to understand operational and behavioral apprehensions that may hinder acceptance of the change.
Builds team capacity by mentoring and guiding team members considering change readiness variance across staff to unlearn outdated practices and adopt new methods through hands-on support, demonstrations, and peer learning.
Monitors early adoption of change initiatives by reviewing KPIs, compliance levels, and feedback from staff or beneficiaries, and refines communication and implementation approaches by analysing gaps and adjusting messages, channels, or rollout methods to improve acceptance and effectiveness. Anticipates operational risks or service disruptions during transition and introduces corrective measures to maintain continuity. I help my team understand and adopt changes by clearly communicating their purpose and benefits.
I address concerns and support others in transitioning to new ways of working.
I align team processes and timelines with change objectives and implementation plans.

proficiency_levels.label: Institutionalises change by building M/D/O-wide readiness, commitment, and sustained adoption
proficiency_levels.description:
Owns and leads M/D/O readiness assessment for proposed changes by analysing field feedback, pilot outcomes, compliance data, grievance trends, and organisational capacity indicators, and formally determining whether critical prerequisites (capacity, systems, approvals, staffing readiness) are in place before authorising scale-up within the M/D/O. Assesses organisational absorption capacity before scaling or launching parallel change initiatives, considering workload, dependencies, and service delivery risks.
Translates policy or programme-level change mandates into clear implementation expectations by issuing M/D/O-level directions, timelines, and responsibility matrices through official orders, review notes, or meeting minutes.
Reviews and validates change communication material (for e.g., presentations, circulars, FAQs, training notes, etc) to ensure that the rationale, benefits, and implications of the change are clearly articulated for staff and implementing agencies.
Builds institutional trust in reform efforts by leading structured review meetings (for e.g., monthly progress reviews, video conferences with field offices) to track change adoption, resolve inter-departmental issues, ensure alignment between timelines and actions, and model commitment during uncertainty or resistance.
Analyses and addresses recurring bottlenecks during change initiatives by reviewing programme reports, grievance trends, and field feedback, and issues targeted corrective directions (such as clarifying the purpose of change) to improve acceptance and consistent adoption of the change.
Approves and embeds revised processes by incorporating change requirements into SOPs, system configurations, or official guidelines, thereby enabling officials to transition away from legacy practices and consistently adopt the new way of working.
Guides teams in sequencing and pacing multiple change initiatives by clarifying priorities, dependencies, and expected impact, so that teams are adequately prepared to adopt changes without disrupting service delivery or missing mandated timelines. Enforces the sustainability of change by incorporating adherence to new processes into review agendas, monitoring formats, or performance discussions, thereby normalising the change in the routine administrative functioning of the M/D/O. I convert reform or programme mandates into clear, adoptable actions across the organisation.
I address systemic adoption barriers through structured reviews, corrective directions, and system-level adjustments.
I ensure changes are sustained by embedding them into official processes, reviews, and administrative routines.

theme_description: Adopts a structured approach for the effective initiation and implementation of multi-level, multi-faceted changes in the government ecosystem, with the aim of achieving a prescribed mandate as part of a Govt. program, scheme, project, or government initiative. Drives preparedness to unlearn and relearn, communicates the need for change to gain stakeholder acceptance and shared commitment, and drives change from the current state to the desired future state.
sub_theme_description: Demonstrates the ability to plan, execute, monitor, and institutionalise approved changes by translating policy, programme, or organisational decisions into sustained operational practices that achieve intended outcomes.

proficiency_levels.label: Follows approved plans and guidance for change implementation in the M/D/O
proficiency_levels.description:
Understands the purpose, scope, and intended outcomes of the approved change by reviewing official instructions and briefings, so that assigned tasks are carried out correctly and in alignment with the change objective.
Identifies the specific change-related tasks required within their role or unit by referring to the implementation plan and role guidance (for e.g., Responsibility Matrix, Section-wise Task Allocation Sheet, e-Office note assigning duties, etc) ensuring clarity on responsibilities and reducing execution errors.
Assesses whether basic requirements for implementation, including staff availability and clarity of instructions, are in place to avoid delays or incomplete implementation.
Executes assigned change activities in the prescribed sequence and within agreed timelines to ensure consistency and compliance with the implementation plan.
Communicates approved implementation instructions using prescribed circulars, meeting notes, or digital channels, so that affected stakeholders receive clear and reliable information.
Maintains basic records of actions taken, instructions received, and immediate outcomes in the prescribed format, and systems such as e-Office, file notes, MIS Updates, etc, supporting traceability and accountability during implementation. I understand the purpose of approved changes and what is expected during implementation.
I carry out assigned change activities as per approved instructions, timelines, and methods.
I track progress and flag issues early to support effective implementation.

proficiency_levels.label: Translates approved decisions into coordinated execution and adoption across teams
proficiency_levels.description:
Assesses team readiness by examining capacity, coordination, and operational constraints to support effective adoption of the approved change (for e.g, checking staff deployment review, workload sheet analysis, fund availability check through PFMS, system readiness checklist, etc).
Aligns available human and financial resources with implementation processes and timelines (for e.g., revising expenditure plan in PFMS, reallocating staff through office order, updating Gantt chart, etc) to ensure priorities are realistically resourced and executable.
Implements approved changes to procedures, systems, and role responsibilities to embed the change into routine operations.
Coordinates approved communication interventions for affected stakeholders to ensure an accurate understanding of the change.
Coordinates approved capacity building interventions to enable stakeholders to implement the change in their routine functions.
Uses defined indicators to track adoption, performance, and early outcomes, and reviews them regularly to assess whether the change is being implemented as intended.
Reviews implementation data and feedback to identify delays, uneven adoption, or emerging risks, enabling timely corrective action.
Initiates or suggests corrective actions such as adjusting timelines, clarifying roles, or strengthening support to address gaps in execution or adoption. Documents and consolidates implementation learnings to inform subsequent phases or future initiatives, strengthening M/D/O learning. I implement approved changes to procedures, systems, or role responsibilities to support routine operational use.
I use defined implementation indicators to monitor adoption and take corrective action where required.
I document implementation learnings to support subsequent phases of rollout.

proficiency_levels.label: Builds change implementation as a repeatable, governed organisational capability
proficiency_levels.description:
Establishes M/D/O-wide standards, roles, and governance mechanisms for change implementation by defining clear accountabilities and decision rights, ensuring consistency and reliability across initiatives.
Ensures implementation readiness inputs inform policy approval and rollout decisions, improving feasibility and delivery outcomes.
Ensures readiness and implementation risk assessments are reviewed prior to scale-up or phased rollout, preventing overextension and implementation failure.
Embeds adoption and outcome indicators into M/D/O performance and review systems (for e.g., monthly dashboard review, inclusion in Departmental Performance Review, PRAGATI-style monitoring format, etc) enabling leadership oversight of implementation quality and results.
Establishes structured internal or independent review mechanisms to assess implementation quality and outcomes, strengthening accountability and learning.
Reviews the cumulative impact of multiple concurrent change initiatives on organisational capacity and performance, enabling prioritisation and sequencing decisions.
Codifies effective change implementation practices into institutional guidance, toolkits, and reference materials, enabling repeatability and scale. Ensures new processes and practices are embedded into routine organisational systems and reviews, sustaining change outcomes beyond initial implementation. I establish M/D/O-wide standards and ownership for implementing approved changes.
I use routine M/D/O performance and review systems to assure implementation quality and adoption.
I ensure that implemented changes are embedded into standard administrative processes and reviews.

theme_description: Adopts a structured approach for the effective initiation and implementation of multi-level, multi-faceted changes in the government ecosystem, with the aim of achieving a prescribed mandate as part of a Govt. program, scheme, project, or government initiative. Drives preparedness to unlearn and relearn, communicates the need for change to gain stakeholder acceptance and shared commitment, and drives change from the current state to the desired future state.
sub_theme_description: Drives willingness and acceptance to change and manages resistance to change at the Ministerial, Departmental, or Organizational level. Identifies practical challenges associated with the said change, stays open to new opportunities, and maintains a proactive and positive mindset toward achieving goals.

proficiency_levels.label: Understands the immediate impact of the change within their own role or unit
proficiency_levels.description:
Understands the rationale for specific changes in daily tasks by comparing current or established processes with revised structures such as transition from physical files to e-Office modules.
Identifies and documents potential practical and functional challenges faced during personal adoption of the change and shares them with supervisors/team for resolution.
Follows prescribed transition instructions and checklists to implement the changes in day-to-day work while complying with departmental guidelines to ensure effective integration into daily systems.
Documents practical issues faced during adoption (for e.g., system access, workflow delays, skill gaps, etc) and reports them to supervisors.
Participates in training or orientation activities to build readiness for change and applies new learning to adjust work practices accordingly.
Communicates accurate and consistent information and feedback about expected impacts of the change using approved messages, helping reduce misinformation and uncertainty. Identifies personal skill or access gaps that may affect smooth adoption of new systems and seeks support proactively. I understand how changes affect my work and adjust accordingly.
I follow revised SOPs and transition guidelines to ensure continuity.
I report practical implementation challenges in a timely manner.

proficiency_levels.label: Assesses team-level impact of change and recommends mitigation measures to ensure smooth transition
proficiency_levels.description:
Communicates the expected impact of change differently to staff, supervisors, and stakeholders (for e.g., explaining new timelines to field units, compliance implications to finance, and performance impact to leadership, etc).
Consolidates structured feedback from team members and stakeholders to identify systemic change implementation gaps.
Assesses operational risks to change such as workload imbalance, skill gaps, dependency bottlenecks, or resistance within the team.
Analyses how new policies, systems, or reforms affect team roles, workflows, and skill requirements (for e.g., automation replacing manual registers, DBT replacing cheque-based payments, centralised procurement through GeM, etc).
Uses MIS dashboards, performance trackers, or compliance reports to monitor adoption progress.
Guides the team in correctly identifying and resolving gaps in understanding of process changes by facilitating discussions and setting up feedback mechanisms. Prepares analytical notes summarising change impact, risks, and mitigation recommendations for supervisory review. I assess how changes affect team operations and identify transition risks.
I recommend practical measures to mitigate disruption and maintain performance.
I ensure revised processes are implemented consistently and in line with approved timelines and guidelines.

proficiency_levels.label: Leads structured change impact assessment to sustain major reforms
proficiency_levels.description:
Designs structured impact matrices and transition risk registers to assess how reforms affect processes, roles, systems, and service delivery.
Evaluates the absorption capacity of the M/D/O by analysing data on current workloads, technical dependencies, and existing skill gaps to determine the feasibility of proposed implementation timelines.
Identifies critical failure points in transition (for e.g., legal approvals, financial clearances, IT integration, etc) and establishes mitigation protocols.
Advises senior leadership on implementation sequencing, phased rollouts, or resource reallocation to reduce transition risk.
Embeds monitoring mechanisms to track adoption metrics such as digital file movement rates, PFMS usage, compliance timelines, training completion, and grievance patterns during transition.
Integrates revised SOPs, workflows, and digital configurations into official rulebooks to replace obsolete processes.
Identifies sources of resistance (for e.g., skill insecurity, workload concerns, loss of role clarity, etc) and designs targeted engagement, training, or phased adoption strategies to build acceptance and ownership.
Reviews post-implementation outcomes and institutionalises lessons learned into future reform planning. Encourages pilot testing and adaptive refinement of reforms to leverage emerging opportunities and improve outcomes. I design and lead structured change impact assessments to anticipate systemic risks before implementation.
I develop mitigation strategies to ensure service continuity and M/D/O stability during reform.
I institutionalise monitoring and governance mechanisms that sustain reform adoption and reduce resistance over time.

theme_description: Demonstrates the ability to handle various administrative processes and procedures relating to Allowances & Reimbursement, Leave and Travel related matters. miscellaneous matters (Car, Residence, Personal Staff etc.), Official Language duty and ensures implementation across the Department / Ministry.
sub_theme_description: Demonstrates understanding and ability to apply the relevant rules, regulations and guidelines for processing of Allowances and Reimbursements related matters in the Ministry, Department or Organisation.

proficiency_levels.label: Processes routine allowance and reimbursement claims correctly by applying rules
proficiency_levels.description:
Identifies types of allowances and reimbursements under 7th Central Pay Commission (CPC) and their ceilings, slabs, and conditions from Department of Expenditure (DoE) Office Memorandums (OMs) and M/D/O specific instructions. Understands tax exemption rules under Income Tax Act/CBDT circulars (for e.g., Children Education Allowance (CEA) exemption limits, newspaper/briefcase treatment, transport allowance rules, etc) and applies them while marking claims.
Explains eligibility conditions such as dependent criteria, school recognition, CGHS vs CS(MA) applicability, and documentation validity before processing claims on e-Office.
Checks each claim against eligibility, ceilings, and required documents using a standard checklist and returns incomplete cases with a feedback note to improve first-time-right submissions.
Verifies rate applicability from the relevant OM/rate list and documents the recalculated amount to demonstrate due diligence.
Processes sanctions with the correct head of account, attaches sanction‑bill‑receipt trails, and posts payments through PFMS/e‑Bill, to maintain traceability.
Uses authorised channels where prescribed (for e.g., empanelled providers/CGHS rates, approved telephone plans, etc) and secures prior sanction where required, to prevent inadmissible payments.
Maintains a monthly exception list (for e.g., over ceiling claims, repeated deficiencies, late submissions, etc) and escalates to supervisors to trigger corrective action. Stores personal data (for e.g., medical records, dependency proofs) with need‑to‑know access and removal of sensitive data for RTI responses to protect privacy. I understand key allowance rules and verify eligibility, ceilings, and rates before processing claims.
I complete the sanction and payment trails accurately ensuring claims are compliant, documented, and traceable.
I maintain compliant, well documented files that support transparent claim processing.

proficiency_levels.label: Coordinates and audits allowances and reimbursements processes to improve accuracy, turnaround time, and budget discipline
proficiency_levels.description:
Conducts monthly claims governance reviews and pre-audit reviews, using dashboards (for e.g., claims received and settled, rejection rates, cycle time, etc) and systematic pre-verification against entitlements and sanctions to ensure timely settlement and minimise recoveries.
Standardises SOPs and maker–checker controls in e‑Office/HRMS (for e.g., mandatory fields, document proofs, auto‑calculation sheets, etc) to improve consistency and reduce manual errors.
Coordinates with CGHS/empanelled providers for medical claims to ensure use of approved packages, rates, and receipt formats, to prevent overpayment.
Tracks budget utilisation and prepares quarterly forecasts, highlighting risks of excesses or shortfalls to keep expenditure within approved grants.
Coordinates with DDO /payroll to align tax flags and exemptions (for e.g., CEA, uniform, newspaper where applicable, etc) and validates reflection in payslips or Form 16, to ensure correct taxation.
Handles edge cases (for e.g., time‑barred claims, relaxation/condonation proposals, partial admissibility, etc) with rule citations and speaking orders, to make decisions defensible.
Conducts quarterly training sessions for staff on allowance rules and documentation standards, and evaluates improvements in claim quality and turnaround time to build capacity. Responds to internal audit and RTI with document trails and rule references within timely, to uphold transparency. I improve the accuracy and efficiency of claims through data-driven reviews, audits, and standardised processes.
I ensure financial discipline by keeping claims and budgets rule-compliant.
I strengthen organisational capability by resolving complex cases with clear rule interpretation and by training staff to reduce errors.

proficiency_levels.label: Leads M/D/O wide policy and assurance systems to deliver transparent and compliant, allowances and reimbursements administration
proficiency_levels.description:
Issues an annual Allowances and Reimbursement Administration Plan with SLAs (for e.g., scrutiny, settlement, and audit targets, savings goals, etc) and reviews with leadership to align performance of processing teams against defined SLAs.
Embeds digital workflows in HRMS, e‑Office, or PFMS (for e.g., validation rules, entitlement masters, exception reports, digital signatures, etc), and publishes an exceptions dashboard, to prevent errors and misuse.
Establishes risk‑based internal audit and commissions third‑party reviews tracking findings to closure with owners and due dates, strengthening assurance.
Establishes data protection controls (for e.g., retention schedules, masking/redaction for RTI, access logs, etc) for medical/identity data, conducting annual privacy briefings, to reduce data risk.
Aligns policies with GFR, DoE, OMs, etc instructions, and CBDT guidance, issuing consolidated standing orders and model templates, to harmonise practice across units.
Publishes quarterly analytics on spend by category, savings from process changes, and SLA adherence, using insights to refine targets and resource allocation, driving evidence‑based improvements. Builds section capability by mentoring processors and reviewers and evaluating improvements through SLA and audit metrics. I establish policies, SLAs, and digital workflows that make allowance administration predictable, compliant, and audit ready.
I manage system risks through targeted audits and exception monitoring that prevent errors and misuse.
I build organisational capability by mentoring staff and harmonising practices across units.

theme_description: Demonstrates the ability to handle various administrative processes and procedures relating to Allowances & Reimbursement, Leave and Travel related matters. miscellaneous matters (Car, Residence, Personal Staff etc.), Official Language duty and ensures implementation across the Department / Ministry.
sub_theme_description: Demonstrates understanding and ability to apply the relevant rules, regulations and guidelines for processing of Leave and Travel related matters in the Ministry, Department or Organization.

proficiency_levels.label: Processes basic leave and travel requests by understanding and applying rules and procedures
proficiency_levels.description:
Applies basic provisions of the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972, such as types of leave, eligibility, leave balances, and required certificates, while processing routine leave applications in a rule based manner.
Checks LTC2 cases as per the CCS (LTC) Rules, 1988, including Home Town and anywhere in India LTC, by verifying eligibility, block periods, and mandatory declarations.
Verifies travel claims using basic Travelling Allowance Rules (FRSR Part II), including admissible fares, class of travel, and use of authorised travel agents.
Prepares clear and complete note sheets, attaches required supporting documents, and follows prescribed M/D/O procedures to ensure transparency and accountability.
Records leave, uploads documents, and supports financial processing through digital systems such as e-Office, HRMS,3 and PFMS, ensuring accuracy and audit readiness. Identifies missing information or inconsistencies in leave or travel cases and seeks timely guidance from supervising officers to correct errors and ensure fair and timely processing. I process basic leave and travel requests by applying the relevant CCS Leave, LTC and Travelling Allowance Rules and ensuring that all documentation is complete.
I use digital systems such as eOffice, HRMS and PFMS to route files, update records and maintain accuracy in line with Ministry procedures.
I seek clarification when needed to ensure that leave and travel cases are compliant, correctly documented and error-free.

proficiency_levels.label: Reviews leave and travel requests while coordinating with sections for timely processing
proficiency_levels.description:
Reviews leave and LTC cases by interpreting relevant provisions of the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972 and CCS (LTC) Rules, 1988 - such as eligibility limits, block-year rules, journey admissibility, and documentation norms - to ensure accurate and fair processing before approval. Verifies the completeness and correctness of supporting documents, including medical certificates, service records, authorised travel agent tickets, boarding passes, and fare details, in line with the Travelling Allowance Rules (FRSR Part II), ensuring records are audit-ready.
Identifies recurring documentation gaps or procedural errors in leave and travel submissions and provides clear guidance to colleagues to reduce rework, avoid delays, and improve transparency in processing.
Consolidates information across HRMS, eOffice, and PFMS to ensure leave records, file movement, and financial data are consistent, traceable, and aligned with GFR 2017 and departmental procedures
Coordinates with administrative sections, DDO /Accounts units, and controlling officers to resolve discrepancies related to leave balances, LTC eligibility, claim admissibility, or prior approvals, supporting timely and accountable decision making. Prepares structured note sheets with relevant rule references, admissibility checks, and clear recommendations, and escalates cases requiring interpretation such as overlapping leave, LTC carry forward, advances, or delayed claims with a reasoned summary of options for decision-making authorities. I review leave and travel requests by verifying eligibility, documentation and compliance with the relevant rules.
I update and reconcile information across HRMS, eOffice and PFMS to keep leave and travel records accurate.
I coordinate with colleagues to clarify issues in submissions and resolve them to support timely approvals.

proficiency_levels.label: Oversees leave and travel cases and applies the rules to guide teams in making correct and timely decisions
proficiency_levels.description:
Examines complex and exceptional leave and travel cases - such as special leave categories, foreign travel, relaxations, or deviations from standard norms - and applies relevant rules with reasoned justification to ensure compliant, fair, and defensible outcomes.
Interprets and operationalises updated Government instructions, policy clarifications, and circulars (for example, revised LTC entitlements or travel restrictions), ensuring consistent application across the M/D/O.
Reviews high-risk and sensitive cases, including high-value travel claims, repeated LTC usage, or disputed leave balances, and strengthens internal checks to prevent misuse and reinforce accountability.
Analyses patterns in pendency, audit objections, and recurring errors in leave and travel cases, and initiates process improvements - such as workflow rationalisation, system-based validations, or partial automation, etc to improve turnaround time and reliability.
Embeds standard operating procedures by developing and updating these SOPs, templates, checklists, and rule summaries for leave and travel processing, ensuring uniform practices and audit-ready documentation. Builds the capacity of dealing staff and supervisory officers by contributing to guidance notes, internal training material, or knowledge sessions, and by providing structured feedback to improve overall quality and consistency of leaves and travels processes. I evaluate complex leave and travel cases and apply the rules to support accurate and consistent decisions.
I use digital tools and apply these insights to keep processing timely and efficient.
I provide clear guidance and apply these to help colleagues improve their work.

theme_description: Demonstrates the ability to handle various administrative processes and procedures relating to Allowances & Reimbursement, Leave and Travel related matters. miscellaneous matters (Car, Residence, Personal Staff etc.), Official Language duty and ensures implementation across the Department / Ministry.
sub_theme: Handling Miscellaneous Matters (Car, Residence, Personal Staff etc.)
sub_theme_description: Demonstrates understanding and ability to apply diverse provisions, methodologies, and protocols for overseeing miscellaneous affairs including Telephone, Car, Residence, Personal Staff etc in the Ministry, Department or Organization.
